problem.passage:
The idea that the words a language provides can shape how its speakers perceive the world, often associated with linguists Edward Sapir and Benjamin Lee Whorf, has been tested most rigorously in the domain of color. Russian, for example, uses two basic terms, "siniy" and "goluboy," for darker and lighter blues, whereas English uses only "blue." In a 2007 study, Jonathan Winawer and colleagues found that Russian speakers were faster than English speakers at telling apart two blues that fell on opposite sides of the siniy-goluboy boundary.

Yet the researchers also observed that this advantage disappeared when participants were asked to silently repeat a string of digits while performing the task, an activity that occupies verbal memory. Because Russian speakers' eyes did not change during the digit task, the result suggests that the language advantage depends on speakers actively drawing on their color words in the moment rather than on any permanent difference in how they see. Findings like these have led many researchers to favor a modest version of the hypothesis over the claim that language fixes the limits of perception.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.explanation: 지문은 러시아어 화자가 파란색 경계를 더 빨리 구분한다는 결과를 제시한 뒤, 언어 기억이 방해받으면 그 이점이 사라진다는 점을 들어 언어의 영향이 영구적 시각 변화가 아니라 실시간 단어 사용에 의존한다고 결론짓는다. 이 두 정보를 연결한 D가 정답이다. A는 첫 단락만 반영하며 '영구적으로 다르게 본다'는 해석은 둘째 단락이 부정한다. B는 언어 효과가 실제로 관찰되었으므로 지나치다. C는 숫자 과제가 모든 화자의 색 구분을 방해했다는 진술로, 지문은 러시아어 화자의 '이점'이 사라졌다고만 말한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text first reports that Russian speakers distinguish blues across their two-term boundary faster, then shows that this advantage vanishes when verbal memory is occupied, concluding that language's effect depends on in-the-moment word use rather than permanent changes in vision. D connects both pieces, so it is correct. A reflects only the first paragraph and claims a lasting perceptual difference, which the second paragraph undercuts. B goes too far, since a language effect was in fact observed. C overgeneralizes: the text says only that the Russian speakers' advantage disappeared, not that everyone's color discrimination was impaired.

problem.passage:
In Stanley Milgram's obedience experiments of the early 1960s, volunteers were told to give what they believed were increasingly strong electric shocks to another person whenever that person answered a question wrongly. Many participants kept going while an experimenter calmly urged them on, and this result is often summarized as proof that ordinary people will obey any authority. Later analyses of Milgram's own records point to a narrower conclusion. Obedience fell sharply when the experimenter gave instructions by telephone, when two other "teachers" refused to continue, and when the study was moved from Yale University to a shabby office building. Also, when the experimenter said outright, "You have no other choice, you must go on," almost every participant who heard it stopped. Participants seemed willing to continue mainly when they could see themselves as helping a legitimate scientific project, not when they were simply being given orders.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

C는 장소 변화라는 한 가지 세부 사항만 과장했고, 지문은 전화 지시나 명령 문구 같은 지시 방식도 중요했다고 말한다. D는 동료 '교사'의 거부라는 하나의 조건만 일반화한 것이며, 지문은 남이 지켜보는 것을 원인으로 들지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text first presents the popular belief that people will obey any authority. It then challenges that belief by showing that obedience dropped under several conditions and that a direct order actually made people stop. It concludes that participants kept going when they saw themselves as helping legitimate science, so A is correct. B just repeats the popular belief that the text argues against. C blows up one detail, the change of location, and ignores the text's point that how instructions were given (by phone, or as a direct order) also mattered. D turns one condition, the other teachers refusing, into a general claim, and the text never says that being watched was the reason participants stopped.

problem.passage:
In 1989, sociologist Ray Oldenburg introduced the term "third places" to describe informal gathering spots, such as cafés, barbershops, and neighborhood pubs, that are distinct from the home (the first place) and the workplace (the second). Many later writers treated the concept mainly as a celebration of cozy businesses, and some urban designers assumed that any attractive public venue would qualify. Oldenburg's own account, however, was more demanding. He argued that what makes a location a third place is not its décor or even its function but the kind of interaction it fosters: regulars who return without invitation, conversation as the main activity, and a leveling atmosphere in which visitors' jobs and incomes matter little. By this standard, a stylish coffee shop where customers work silently on laptops may fail to be a third place, while a plain corner diner full of chatting regulars may succeed.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

D mentions the coffee shop and diner examples, but the text never says which kind of place is more common.

problem.passage:
A widely circulated television segment from the 1960s showed an unsuspecting person stepping into an elevator, only to turn and face the back wall after several actors did so. The clip is often cited as proof that people will copy strangers even when the behavior makes no sense. When psychologist Maren Ostby and her colleagues staged forty modern versions of the scenario in office buildings, however, they found a more qualified pattern. Riders who were alone with the actors frequently turned around, but riders who entered with a friend almost never did, and many laughed or commented on the odd behavior. Ostby concludes that the original segment did capture a genuine tendency to follow a group, but that this tendency weakens sharply once a person has even one ally whose behavior differs from the group's.

problem.passage:
Early studies of the bystander effect suggested that people are less likely to help a stranger in distress when others are present, and researchers attributed this pattern to a diffusion of responsibility: each witness assumes someone else will act. Later work, however, complicated this picture. In a 2019 analysis of hundreds of real public conflicts recorded by security cameras in three countries, sociologist Richard Philpot and colleagues found that at least one bystander intervened in about nine out of ten incidents. Moreover, the chance that someone stepped in rose as the number of onlookers grew. Philpot's team does not dismiss the earlier laboratory findings; rather, they argue that while any single witness in a crowd may feel less personally obligated, a larger group simply contains more potential helpers, making it more likely that at least one of them will act.

Based on the text, how do Philpot and colleagues account for both the earlier laboratory results and their own observations?

Speakers of Guugu Yimithirr, an Aboriginal language of northeastern Australia, describe locations almost entirely with cardinal directions, saying in effect "the cup is north of the plate" rather than "the cup is to the left of the plate." Psychologist Melvin Lerner proposed that many people hold an unspoken belief that the world is fair: good things happen to good people, and bad things happen to those who somehow deserve them. In a series of experiments, Lerner found that observers who watched a participant receive what appeared to be painful electric shocks often rated that participant less favorably, especially when they were told they could do nothing to stop the shocks. problem.passage:
In 1966, psychologist Jack Brehm proposed reactance theory to explain a puzzling pattern: people sometimes respond to persuasion by doing the opposite of what they are urged to do. According to Brehm, individuals hold beliefs about which behaviors they are free to choose, and when they perceive that one of those freedoms is being eliminated or threatened, they experience an unpleasant motivational state he called reactance. This state pushes them to restore the threatened freedom, often by valuing the forbidden option more highly or by deliberately performing the discouraged behavior. Later researchers found that the strength of this response depends less on what a message asks for than on how it is framed. In one study, students read identical recommendations to limit their alcohol intake; those who received forceful wording such as "you must" and "any reasonable person would agree" reported stronger intentions to drink than did those who received the same advice phrased as a suggestion.

According to the text, what did later research reveal about the response Brehm described?

problem.passage:
Psychologists studying moral licensing have found that people who have recently done something virtuous sometimes feel freer to act selfishly afterward, as though their good deed had earned them credit to spend. In one series of experiments, participants who first chose an environmentally friendly product later kept more money for themselves in an unrelated sharing task than did participants who had chosen a conventional product. Researchers Anna Merritt and Daniel Effron, however, have noted that the effect does not appear uniformly. When participants were prompted to view their earlier good act as an expression of who they are, rather than as an achievement they had completed, the later lapse in generosity often shrank or disappeared. The way people interpret their own virtue, in other words, appears to shape whether that virtue licenses later misconduct.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.passage:
According to social comparison theory, first proposed by psychologist Leon Festinger in 1954, people judge their own abilities by measuring themselves against others, especially when no objective standard is available. Later researchers distinguished two directions of comparison: upward comparison, in which people look to those who are doing better, and downward comparison, in which they look to those who are doing worse. Early studies tended to link upward comparison with lower self-esteem and downward comparison with comfort. __Yet a 1997 study by Penelope Lockwood and Ziva Kunda found that students who read about a highly successful peer in their own field sometimes felt more motivated, not less, provided they believed similar success was within their reach.__ Findings like this suggest that how a comparison affects a person depends less on its direction than on whether the person sees the other's position as attainable.

Psychologists have long assumed that people attribute human traits to animals mainly when the animals look or act like humans—a chimpanzee frowning, say, or a dog appearing to sulk. problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 학교가 가정에서 물려받은 친숙함을 타고난 재능으로 취급해, 가정의 이점을 능력으로 얻은 것처럼 보이는 학업 자격으로 바꾼다는 부르디외의 주장을 제시하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 마지막 문장의 후대 연구자 논쟁을 가리키며, 밑줄 문장은 그 논쟁의 증거를 다루지 않는다. C는 첫 문장의 배경(무상 교육, 개방된 시험)을 언급할 뿐, 밑줄 문장은 그런 정책이 생긴 이유를 설명하지 않는다. D의 책·박물관 같은 구체적 지식은 앞 문장에서 정의된 것이고, 밑줄 문장은 정의가 아니라 그 지식이 변환되는 과정을 설명한다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence describes how, according to Bourdieu, schools mistake inherited familiarity for natural talent and so turn family advantage into credentials that look earned through merit, so A is correct. B points to the final sentence's debate among later researchers, but the underlined sentence presents no evidence from that debate. C picks up the first sentence's background about free schooling and open exams, yet the underlined sentence never explains why those policies existed. D lists the books and museums defined in the previous sentence, but the underlined sentence doesn't define cultural capital; it explains the process that converts it.

quality.seed: social science research — Sociologist Pierre Bourdieu's Cultural Capital concept linking social advantages to educational and cultural knowledge accumulation

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "학교가 물려받은 친숙함을 타고난 재능으로 취급 → 가정 이점이 능력으로 얻은 자격처럼 보임"이라는 과정을 서술하므로 A가 정확. B는 마지막 문장, C는 본문에 없는 정책 배경, D는 앞 문장의 정의를 각각 가리켜 적절한 오답. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 부르디외 문화자본 설명도 사실적으로 타당. 과정 vs 정의 구분과 문맥 연결이 필요해 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 밑줄 문장이 설명하는 전환 과정(물려받은 이점이 타고난 재능으로 오인되어 능력으로 얻은 자격처럼 보이게 됨)과 정확히 맞는다. 오답 B·C·D는 지문의 다른 문장(마지막 문장의 후대 연구 논쟁, 첫 문장의 무상 교육 배경, 직전 문장의 문화자본 정의)에서 그럴듯한 근거를 끌어오므로, 밑줄 문장의 위치와 기능을 따져 봐야 배제할 수 있다. 다만 B와 C는 '증거', '정책이 생긴 이유'라는 표현 때문에 비교적 빨리 걸러진다. D가 가장 강한 오답이다. 네 선택지가 모두 'It explains'로 시작하는 평행 구조여서 형식은 적절하다. 전체적으로 medium 난이도에 맞는다.

problem.passage:
In the 1930s and 1940s, linguist Benjamin Lee Whorf studied the Hopi language of northeastern Arizona and argued that it lacked the grammatical machinery English speakers use to treat time as a series of countable units, such as "three days" or "next summer." Instead, Whorf claimed, Hopi speakers marked whether an event was manifest or still unfolding, a distinction he believed reflected a fundamentally different way of experiencing time. __Later fieldwork by linguist Ekkehart Malotki, however, documented numerous Hopi expressions for units of time, tense-like markers, and even calendrical terms.__ Yet many scholars contend that Whorf's broader contribution survives this correction: by asking whether the Western picture of time as a uniform, flowing line is truly universal, he prompted researchers to test, rather than assume, how language and thought interact.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In the 1930s and 1940s, linguist Benjamin Lee Whorf studied the Hopi language of northeastern Arizona and argued that it lacked the grammatical machinery English speakers use to treat time as a series of countable units, such as "three days" or "next summer." Instead, Whorf claimed, Hopi speakers marked whether an event was manifest or still unfolding, a distinction he believed reflected a fundamentally different way of experiencing time. __Later fieldwork by linguist Ekkehart Malotki, however, documented numerous Hopi expressions for units of time, tense-like markers, and even calendrical terms.__ Yet many scholars contend that Whorf's broader contribution survives this correction: by asking whether the Western picture of time as a uniform, flowing line is truly universal, he prompted researchers to test, rather than assume, how language and thought interact.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It offers evidence that Whorf's reasoning about Hopi grammar was later extended to other languages of the region.
It presents findings that undercut a specific claim Whorf made, setting up the text's argument about what part of his work endures.
It presents findings that confirm Whorf's view that Hopi speakers experience time differently from English speakers.
It presents findings that establish the Western conception of time as universal, which the text then accepts as settled.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'however'와 함께 Hopi어에 시간 단위와 시제 표지가 없다는 Whorf의 구체적 주장을 반박하는 Malotki의 조사 결과를 제시하고, 이어지는 'Yet' 문장은 그럼에도 Whorf의 더 넓은 기여는 살아남는다고 주장한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 Whorf의 분석이 확장되었다고 하지만 지문은 반박을 다룬다. C는 반박 결과를 확증으로 뒤집어 읽은 것이다. D는 Whorf에 대한 반박이라는 점은 맞지만, 지문은 서구적 시간관의 보편성을 확정된 사실로 받아들이지 않고 오히려 검증해야 할 질문으로 남긴다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence, introduced with "however," reports Malotki's findings of Hopi time units and tense-like markers, which contradict Whorf's specific claim about Hopi grammar. The next sentence, beginning with "Yet," then argues that Whorf's broader contribution still survives, so B is correct. A is wrong because the findings challenge Whorf's analysis rather than extend it to other languages. C turns the contradiction into a confirmation. D is right that the findings undercut Whorf, but the text never treats the Western view of time as universal and settled; it says the question should be tested, not assumed.

quality.seed: social science research — Linguist Benjamin Whorf's Analysis of Hopi temporal concepts questioning Western assumptions about time universality

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'however'로 Whorf의 구체적 주장(Hopi어에 시간 단위·시제 표지 부재)을 반박하는 Malotki의 결과를 제시하고, 이어지는 'Yet' 문장이 Whorf의 넓은 기여가 살아남는다고 주장하므로 B가 정확하다. A(다른 언어로 확장), C(확증)는 방향이 틀리고, D는 '반박'이라는 점은 맞지만 지문이 서구적 시간관을 확정된 것으로 수용하지 않는다는 점에서 배제된다. 한·영 해설 모두 정답과 일치하고 글자 참조가 선택지와 맞으며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 사실관계(Whorf 1930~40년대 Hopi 연구, Malotki의 반박 연구) 정확. 지문은 독창적 서술로 저작권 의심 없음. 'however'와 'Yet'의 연결을 파악해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 요구되며, D가 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하므로 medium에 적합. 다만 정답 B가 가장 길고 구조적으로 상세해 다소 눈에 띌 수 있으나 허용 범위.

advisory.note: 'however'와 'Yet'만 훑어 읽어도 B를 고를 수 있다. A는 '다른 언어로 확장'이라는 지문에 없는 내용이라 쉽게 배제된다. C는 지문과 정반대 방향이다. 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가진 오답은 D 하나뿐이고, 그마저 '확정된 사실로 수용'이라는 극단적 표현 때문에 쉽게 걸러진다. 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가진 오답이 최소 2개여야 한다는 medium 기준에 못 미친다.

problem.passage:
In his studies of initiation rites among the Ndembu of Zambia, anthropologist Victor Turner focused on the middle phase of such rituals, when participants have left their former status but have not yet acquired a new one. He called this phase "liminal," from the Latin word for threshold. Initiates in this state are often stripped of names, clothing, and rank, and they are treated as equals regardless of their prior standing. __Turner observed that this leveling, far from producing disorder, tended to forge an intense sense of solidarity among initiates, a bond he termed "communitas."__ Turner went on to argue that communitas is not limited to tribal rites: it surfaces in pilgrimages, religious movements, and other settings where ordinary social hierarchies are temporarily suspended.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In his studies of initiation rites among the Ndembu of Zambia, anthropologist Victor Turner focused on the middle phase of such rituals, when participants have left their former status but have not yet acquired a new one. He called this phase "liminal," from the Latin word for threshold. Initiates in this state are often stripped of names, clothing, and rank, and they are treated as equals regardless of their prior standing. __Turner observed that this leveling, far from producing disorder, tended to forge an intense sense of solidarity among initiates, a bond he termed "communitas."__ Turner went on to argue that communitas is not limited to tribal rites: it surfaces in pilgrimages, religious movements, and other settings where ordinary social hierarchies are temporarily suspended.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents the leveling of initiates as a temporary disruption that Turner believed rituals were designed to quickly correct.
It introduces the Latin origin of a term that the text uses to explain the stages of Ndembu initiation rites.
It identifies a consequence of the liminal phase that the text then claims extends beyond the rituals Turner first studied.
It offers evidence that challenges the view that initiates are treated as equals during the liminal phase.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞에서 설명한 지위의 평준화가 무질서가 아니라 '코뮤니타스'라는 연대를 낳았다는 결과를 제시하고, 마지막 문장은 이 코뮤니타스가 부족 의례를 넘어 순례 등에서도 나타난다고 확장한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 평준화를 언급한다는 점은 맞지만, 지문은 이를 '무질서를 낳지 않는다'고 하며 바로잡아야 할 혼란으로 보지 않는다. B의 라틴어 어원은 밑줄 문장이 아니라 앞 문장의 내용이다. D는 밑줄 문장이 평등한 대우를 반박하는 것이 아니라 그 결과를 설명하므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence describes what the leveling of initiates produces: not disorder but a strong solidarity Turner called "communitas." The final sentence then extends communitas beyond tribal rites to pilgrimages and religious movements, so C is correct. A does mention the leveling, but the text says it does not produce disorder, so the text never treats it as a disruption that needs fixing. B describes the Latin origin of "liminal," which comes from an earlier sentence, not the underlined one. D is wrong because the underlined sentence builds on the equal treatment of initiates instead of challenging it.

quality.seed: social science research — Anthropologist Victor Turner's Liminality concept describing threshold states in religious and social rituals

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 평준화의 결과(communitas)를 제시하고 마지막 문장이 이를 부족 의례 밖으로 확장하므로 C가 정확. A는 '평준화' 언급으로 부분적 근거가 있으나 '무질서를 낳지 않는다'는 지문과 모순, B는 앞 문장의 어원 설명을 오귀속, D는 방향이 반대. Turner의 liminality/communitas 개념 서술은 사실과 부합. 두 문장(밑줄+마지막)의 연결이 필요한 medium 수준. 한·영 해설 일치하며 자연스러움.

advisory.note: C는 'the text then claims'라고 하지만 확장 주장은 엄밀히 Turner의 주장이며, 지문은 이를 전달할 뿐이다. 그래도 허용 범위 안이다. B와 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 A는 그럴듯한 오답이다. Turner, Ndembu, liminal(limen), communitas에 관한 사실 관계는 정확하다.

problem.passage:
In a 1961 study at Stanford University, psychologist Albert Bandura had preschoolers watch an adult repeatedly strike an inflatable "Bobo" doll with a mallet. Bandura's central claim—that children can acquire new behaviors merely by observing a model, without receiving any direct reward or ______ supported when many of the children later imitated the adult's exact blows and even repeated the model's distinctive verbal insults.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In a 1961 study at Stanford University, psychologist Albert Bandura had preschoolers watch an adult repeatedly strike an inflatable "Bobo" doll with a mallet. Bandura's central claim—that children can acquire new behaviors merely by observing a model, without receiving any direct reward or ______ supported when many of the children later imitated the adult's exact blows and even repeated the model's distinctive verbal insults.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: punishment, was
punishment; was
punishment—and was
punishment—was
problem.explanation: "that children can acquire ... reward or punishment"는 주어 "Bandura's central claim"을 설명하는 삽입 동격절이고, 대시로 시작했으므로 같은 대시로 닫아야 한다. 그 뒤에는 주어의 본동사 "was supported"가 바로 이어져야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표가 삽입부를 닫는 기능을 하지만, 대시로 연 삽입부를 쉼표로 닫을 수는 없다. B의 세미콜론은 주어와 동사를 갈라 놓아 앞뒤 모두 독립절이 되지 못한다. C는 대시는 맞지만 'and'가 들어가 본동사가 없는 문장이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "that children can acquire ... reward or punishment" is an appositive clause that interrupts the subject "Bandura's central claim." Because it opens with a dash, it has to close with a dash too. After the closing dash, the main verb "was supported" should follow directly, so D is correct. A uses a comma, which can close an interruption, but you can't close a dash-opened interruption with a comma. B puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, so neither side is an independent clause. C has the right dash, but adding "and" leaves the main clause without a main verb.

quality.seed: social science research — Psychologist Albert Bandura's Social Learning Theory demonstrating behavioral modeling through observed aggression in children

hardJudge.note: 주어 "Bandura's central claim" 뒤 대시로 연 동격 삽입부를 대시로 닫고 본동사 "was supported"가 이어지는 D가 유일하게 문법적. A(쉼표-대시 불일치), B(세미콜론으로 주어·동사 분리), C("and"로 본동사 상실) 모두 타당하게 배제됨. 해설 한·영 일치, 사실관계(1961 Stanford Bobo doll 실험) 정확. 대시 짝 맞추기 + 긴 삽입부 추적이 필요한 표준 medium 수준.

advisory.note: 대시 쌍 맞추기와 주어-동사 연결을 함께 판단해야 하는 표준 medium 문항. A와 C는 부분적으로 맞는 근거가 있어 그럴듯한 오답이다. 1961년 Stanford에서 진행된 Bobo 인형 연구의 사실관계(망치 사용, 언어적 공격 모방)는 정확하다.

problem.passage:
In The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism (1905), sociologist Max Weber argued that the rational methods once embraced voluntarily by devout Protestants had hardened into an impersonal system that now governs everyone. This system of rules, calculation, and efficiency, which Weber famously likened to a "steel-hard casing" (often translated as an "iron cage")______ modern individuals may enjoy unprecedented material comfort, yet they find their choices increasingly dictated by procedures they did not design and cannot easily escape.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism (1905), sociologist Max Weber argued that the rational methods once embraced voluntarily by devout Protestants had hardened into an impersonal system that now governs everyone. This system of rules, calculation, and efficiency, which Weber famously likened to a "steel-hard casing" (often translated as an "iron cage")______ modern individuals may enjoy unprecedented material comfort, yet they find their choices increasingly dictated by procedures they did not design and cannot easily escape.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , leaves little room for personal freedom:
leaves little room for personal freedom,
, leaves little room for personal freedom,
leaves little room for personal freedom;
problem.explanation: "which Weber famously likened…"로 시작하는 비필수 관계절은 앞에 쉼표가 있으므로 끝에도 쉼표로 닫아야 하며, 그 뒤 동사 leaves가 주어 This system과 연결된다. 또한 뒤의 "modern individuals may enjoy…"는 독립절로, 앞 문장을 구체적으로 설명하므로 콜론이 적절하다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 관계절을 닫는 쉼표가 없고 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 관계절은 올바르게 닫았지만 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 연결해 comma splice이다. D는 세미콜론으로 절 경계는 맞지만 비필수 관계절을 닫는 쉼표가 빠졌다.
problem.explanationEn: The nonessential clause beginning "which Weber famously likened…" opens with a comma, so it must close with a comma before the main verb "leaves," which goes with the subject "This system." After that, "modern individuals may enjoy…" is an independent clause that explains the first one, so a colon is the right link. That makes A correct. B leaves the nonessential clause unclosed, and it also joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C closes the clause correctly but still creates a comma splice. D uses an acceptable semicolon between the clauses but leaves out the comma that has to close the nonessential clause.

quality.seed: social science research — Sociologist Max Weber's Iron Cage Theory explaining bureaucratic rationalization's constraining effects on modern freedom

hardJudge.note: 검산: 주어 "This system of rules, calculation, and efficiency" 뒤 비필수 관계절 "which Weber famously likened … (often translated as an "iron cage")"은 앞 쉼표로 열렸으므로 닫는 쉼표가 필요하고, 그 뒤 "leaves little room for personal freedom"이 주절 술어. 이어지는 "modern individuals may enjoy …, yet they find …"는 독립절이므로 쉼표만으로 연결 불가(B, C는 comma splice). D는 세미콜론은 가능하나 관계절 닫는 쉼표 누락. A만 두 조건 모두 충족하며 콜론은 앞 진술의 구체적 설명을 도입하므로 적절. 해설 한·영 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조 일치, 모순 없음. Weber의 "stahlhartes Gehäuse"(steel-hard casing / iron cage) 관련 서술도 사실에 부합. 두 단계 판단(관계절 닫기 + 절 경계 구두점)이 요구되고 C·D가 각각 한 조건만 충족하는 부분 정답형 오답이므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 이 문항은 판단을 두 단계로 해야 한다. 먼저 괄호 뒤에서 비필수 관계절을 쉼표로 닫아야 하고, 이어서 두 독립절의 경계에 콜론을 써야 한다. 오답 B, C, D는 각각 이 두 요건 중 하나만 충족하므로 선택지를 비교해야 배제할 수 있으며, 이는 medium 난이도에 적합하다. 괄호가 끼어 있어 관계절을 닫는 쉼표를 놓치기 쉬운 점도 함정으로 작용한다. 사실관계(Weber, 1905년, 'stahlhartes Gehäuse', 'iron cage' 번역)도 정확하다.

Verbs such as "buy," "sell," "pay," and "charge," for instance, all evoke a single commercial transaction frame, a scene that includes a buyer, a seller, goods, and money. ______ these verbs cannot be swapped for one another freely: "buy" presents the scene from the buyer's point of view, whereas "sell" puts the seller at the center and leaves the buyer optional.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In developing Frame Semantics, linguist Charles Fillmore argued that the meaning of a word depends on the larger conceptual scene it calls to mind. Verbs such as "buy," "sell," "pay," and "charge," for instance, all evoke a single commercial transaction frame, a scene that includes a buyer, a seller, goods, and money. ______ these verbs cannot be swapped for one another freely: "buy" presents the scene from the buyer's point of view, whereas "sell" puts the seller at the center and leaves the buyer optional.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Therefore,
For example,
Likewise,
Even so,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 네 동사가 같은 프레임(상거래 장면)을 공유한다고 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그럼에도 이 동사들이 서로 맞바꿔 쓸 수 없고 관점이 다르다고 말하므로 양보 후 반전 관계이다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 프레임을 공유한다는 사실이 바꿔 쓸 수 없음의 원인처럼 보이게 하지만, 실제로는 공유된다는 사실과 반대 방향의 내용이다. B는 뒤 문장에 "buy"와 "sell"의 구체적 사례가 나와 그럴듯하지만, 그 사례는 앞 문장의 '공유'를 예시하는 것이 아니라 오히려 그것과 대조된다. C는 앞 내용과 비슷한 내용을 추가할 때 쓰므로 대조 관계와 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank says the four verbs all share one frame, the commercial transaction scene. The sentence after it says that, despite this, the verbs can't be swapped freely because each one takes a different point of view. That's a concession followed by a reversal, so D is correct. A treats the shared frame as the cause of the verbs not being interchangeable, but the shared frame actually points the other way. B might look right because specific cases ("buy" and "sell") come next, but those cases don't show the verbs sharing a frame; they contrast with that idea. C signals that a similar point is being added, so it doesn't fit a contrast.

quality.seed: social science research — Linguist Charles Fillmore's Frame Semantics analyzing how conceptual structures organize word meanings and relations

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(네 동사가 하나의 상거래 프레임을 공유) 뒤에 "그럼에도 자유롭게 바꿔 쓸 수 없다"는 반전이 오므로 양보 전환 'Even so'가 유일하게 논리적임을 직접 확인함. 'Therefore'는 인과 방향이 반대, 'For example'은 뒤에 buy/sell 구체 사례가 나와 표면적으로 그럴듯하나 앞 문장의 '공유'를 예시하지 않음, 'Likewise'는 대조와 불일치. Fillmore의 Frame Semantics·상거래 프레임(buy/sell/pay/charge), 'sell'에서 buyer가 선택적이라는 서술 모두 사실에 부합. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 두 문장의 관계 파악과 콜론 뒤 사례의 기능 판단이 함께 필요한 중간 난이도로 적합.

advisory.note: 공유 프레임 → 그럼에도 교체 불가라는 양보 관계가 명확하다. 'Therefore'와 'For example'은 표면적으로 그럴듯한 오답이라 중간 난이도에 적합하다. Fillmore의 상거래 프레임 설명도 사실과 맞는다.

problem.passage:
Lev Vygotsky's concept of the Zone of Proximal Development describes the gap between what a learner can accomplish alone and what the same learner can accomplish with guidance from a more skilled partner. Later educational researchers developed the related idea of "scaffolding": temporary support that an instructor gradually removes as the learner becomes more competent. In one classroom study, students whose tutors withdrew hints step by step during algebra practice later solved new problems more accurately than did students whose tutors offered the same hints throughout the entire session. ______ the assistance that helped students most was assistance designed to fade away.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Lev Vygotsky's concept of the Zone of Proximal Development describes the gap between what a learner can accomplish alone and what the same learner can accomplish with guidance from a more skilled partner. Later educational researchers developed the related idea of "scaffolding": temporary support that an instructor gradually removes as the learner becomes more competent. In one classroom study, students whose tutors withdrew hints step by step during algebra practice later solved new problems more accurately than did students whose tutors offered the same hints throughout the entire session. ______ the assistance that helped students most was assistance designed to fade away.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
For example,
Moreover,
In other words,
problem.explanation: 마지막 문장은 앞 문장의 연구 결과(힌트를 점차 줄인 학생이 더 잘했다는 것)를 '점차 사라지도록 설계된 도움이 가장 효과적이었다'로 다시 표현한 것이다. 따라서 재진술을 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 대조를 나타내지만 마지막 문장은 연구 결과와 어긋나지 않고 오히려 그 결과를 확인해 준다. B는 구체적인 예를 이끄는데, 마지막 문장은 앞의 연구보다 더 일반적인 진술이므로 방향이 반대이다. C는 새로운 정보를 덧붙일 때 쓰지만 마지막 문장은 새로운 결과가 아니라 같은 결과를 요약한 것이다.
problem.explanationEn: The final sentence takes the study's result (students did better when tutors gradually withdrew hints) and restates it more generally: the most helpful assistance was the kind designed to fade away. That's a restatement, so D is correct. A signals contrast, but the final sentence confirms the study's result instead of going against it. B introduces a specific example, but the final sentence is more general than the study before it, so the direction is backward. C adds new information, but the final sentence doesn't add a new finding; it sums up the same one.

quality.seed: social science research — Educationist Lev Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development theory on scaffolding student learning through guided support

hardJudge.note: 마지막 문장은 앞 연구 결과의 일반화된 재진술이므로 D가 유일하게 타당함. B(예시)는 방향이 반대, C(추가)는 새 정보 없음, A(대조)는 논리 불일치. 해설 양쪽 모두 정확·일관. Vygotsky ZPD·스캐폴딩 설명도 사실에 부합. 재진술과 예시 방향 구분이 필요한 두 단계 판단으로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 재진술 관계가 명확하고, Moreover와 For example이 그럴듯한 오답이라 비교해야 배제됨. 중간 난이도에 적합.

problem.passage:
In The Blank Slate (2002), cognitive scientist Steven Pinker challenges the long-standing view that the human mind is shaped entirely by upbringing and culture. Pinker does not dismiss the influence of environment; rather, he argues that each person ______ certain psychological structures, such as a readiness to learn language, which experience then refines but does not create.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In The Blank Slate (2002), cognitive scientist Steven Pinker challenges the long-standing view that the human mind is shaped entirely by upbringing and culture. Pinker does not dismiss the influence of environment; rather, he argues that each person ______ certain psychological structures, such as a readiness to learn language, which experience then refines but does not create.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: acquires
inherits
constructs
relinquishes
problem.explanation: 지문은 Pinker가 마음이 전적으로 환경에 의해 형성된다는 견해에 반대하며, 경험은 특정 심리 구조를 '다듬을 뿐 만들어 내지는 않는다'고 주장한다고 말한다. 따라서 그 구조는 태어날 때부터 지닌 것이어야 하므로, 타고나 물려받는다는 뜻의 B가 가장 정확하다. A는 구조를 지닌다는 점에서는 그럴듯하지만, 경험을 통해 얻는다는 뜻이라 '경험이 만들지 않는다'는 내용과 충돌한다. C도 구조와 자연스럽게 어울리는 단어이지만, 스스로 구성한다는 뜻이라 선천성 주장과 맞지 않는다. D는 구조를 포기한다는 뜻이라, 경험이 그 구조를 다듬는다는 내용과 모순된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says Pinker rejects the idea that the mind is shaped entirely by environment, and it adds that experience refines these structures "but does not create" them. So the structures have to be present from birth, and B, meaning that people are born with them, fits best. A seems reasonable at first, since people do end up with these structures, but "acquires" means getting them through experience, and the text says experience does not create them. C also pairs naturally with "structures," but it means building them, which goes against Pinker's claim that they are innate. D means giving the structures up, which makes no sense if experience goes on to refine them.

quality.seed: social science research — Linguist Susanne Pinker's Blank Slate critique arguing for innate psychological structures against pure environmental determination

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 검산 완료: "experience then refines but does not create"와 Pinker의 빈 서판 비판이라는 두 단서를 결합해야 '타고난다(inherits)'로 귀결됨. A(acquires)·C(constructs)는 '구조를 지닌다'는 점에서 부분적으로 그럴듯하나 '경험이 만들지 않는다'와 충돌하여 배제되고, D는 명백한 오답이지만 문법적으로 말이 됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일한 결론과 글자 참조, 모순 없음, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. The Blank Slate(2002)·Steven Pinker 인지과학자 사실 정확. 지문은 원저 인용이 아닌 자체 서술로 저작권 우려 없음. 형식 적합, medium 난이도 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 'refines but does not create'와 'challenges...shaped entirely by upbringing'라는 두 단서를 함께 읽어야 고를 수 있어 medium에 맞음. A와 C는 표면적으로 구조와 잘 어울려 그럴듯한 오답이고, D는 상대적으로 쉽게 배제됨. Pinker의 『The Blank Slate』(2002)에 관한 사실 서술도 정확함.

problem.passage:
In 1994, psychologist Richard Herrnstein and political scientist Charles Murray published The Bell Curve, which argued that IQ scores strongly predict outcomes such as income and employment and suggested that differences in average scores between racial groups might partly reflect genetic factors. A task force of the American Psychological Association, formed amid the resulting public debate, accepted that test scores correlate with socioeconomic outcomes. It nonetheless judged the genetic explanation for group differences ______: in its 1996 report, the task force stated that there was little direct evidence for that explanation and noted that its members could not rule out environmental causes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In 1994, psychologist Richard Herrnstein and political scientist Charles Murray published The Bell Curve, which argued that IQ scores strongly predict outcomes such as income and employment and suggested that differences in average scores between racial groups might partly reflect genetic factors. A task force of the American Psychological Association, formed amid the resulting public debate, accepted that test scores correlate with socioeconomic outcomes. It nonetheless judged the genetic explanation for group differences ______: in its 1996 report, the task force stated that there was little direct evidence for that explanation and noted that its members could not rule out environmental causes.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: provocative
obsolete
convoluted
unsubstantiated
problem.explanation: 콜론 뒤 내용은 태스크포스가 유전적 설명을 직접 뒷받침하는 증거가 거의 없다고 했다는 것이므로, 빈칸에는 '증거로 뒷받침되지 않은'이라는 뜻의 D가 들어가야 한다. A는 이 책이 논쟁을 불러일으켰다는 맥락과 어울려 보이지만, 콜론 뒤에서 설명하는 것은 반발을 일으킨다는 점이 아니라 증거가 부족하다는 판단이다. B는 그 주장을 거부했다는 느낌에는 맞지만, 한때 받아들여지다가 시대에 뒤처졌다는 뜻을 담고 있어 증거 부족이라는 근거와 맞지 않는다. C는 설명이 복잡하다는 뜻이지만, 지문에는 설명이 이해하기 어렵다는 내용이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The clause after the colon explains the task force's judgment: it found little direct evidence for the genetic explanation. So the blank needs a word meaning "not supported by evidence," which is D. A might seem to fit because the book caused public debate, but the colon explains a lack of evidence, not a tendency to stir up reactions. B fits the general idea of rejecting the claim, but it means the claim was once accepted and is now out of date, which doesn't match the reason given (missing evidence). C means overly complicated, and nothing in the text says the explanation was hard to follow.

quality.seed: social science research — Sociologist Charles Murray's Bell Curve controversy linking IQ distributions to socioeconomic disparities and racial differences

hardJudge.note: 콜론 뒤 '직접 증거가 거의 없다'가 빈칸의 근거이므로 D(unsubstantiated)가 정확. 역사적 사실(1994년 The Bell Curve, APA 태스크포스 'Intelligence: Knowns and Unknowns' 1996년 보고서, 유전적 해석에 대한 직접 증거 부족 언급)은 실제와 부합. A(provocative)는 '공개 논쟁' 맥락 때문에 매력적인 오답, B(obsolete)는 거부 뉘앙스로 부분적 근거, C는 말이 되나 근거 없음 — 중간 난이도 설계 기준 충족. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 글자 일치, 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 1996년 APA 보고서(Neisser 외, 'Intelligence: Knowns and Unknowns')와 사실관계가 대체로 맞는다. 보고서는 유전적 해석을 뒷받침하는 직접 증거가 거의 없다고 했다. 다만 이 보고서는 알려진 환경 요인들로도 그 격차가 충분히 설명되지 않는다고 함께 밝혔으므로, '환경 원인을 배제할 수 없다'는 표현은 약간 단순화된 것이다. 그래도 허용 가능한 수준이다. 정답 D는 콜론 뒤 '직접 증거가 거의 없음'이라는 근거와 바로 연결된다. A(논쟁 맥락)와 B(거부했다는 느낌)는 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답이어서 비교해야만 배제되므로 medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
In the 1990s, psychologist Claude Steele and his colleagues proposed that stereotype threat—the worry of confirming a negative stereotype about one's group—can lower test performance among members of underrepresented groups. Strikingly, their studies suggested that the effect is ______ among students who care most about a domain: those who strongly identify with mathematics, for instance, tend to show larger performance drops under threat than those for whom math matters little, since a poor result would mean more to them.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In the 1990s, psychologist Claude Steele and his colleagues proposed that stereotype threat—the worry of confirming a negative stereotype about one's group—can lower test performance among members of underrepresented groups. Strikingly, their studies suggested that the effect is ______ among students who care most about a domain: those who strongly identify with mathematics, for instance, tend to show larger performance drops under threat than those for whom math matters little, since a poor result would mean more to them.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: most pronounced
largely absent
easily anticipated
rarely measured
problem.explanation: 콜론 뒤 내용에서 수학에 강하게 동일시하는 학생일수록 위협 상황에서 성적 하락이 '더 크다'고 하므로, 효과가 그 집단에서 가장 두드러진다는 A가 정답이다. B는 '거의 없다'는 뜻이라 더 큰 하락이라는 근거와 정반대다. C는 'Strikingly'라는 놀라움의 표지와 어긋나고, 지문은 효과의 예측 가능성이 아니라 크기를 말한다. D는 연구들이 바로 이 효과를 측정해 결과를 보고했다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text after the colon says that students who strongly identify with math show larger performance drops under threat, so the effect is strongest in that group. That makes A correct. B means the effect barely appears, which is the opposite of "larger performance drops." C doesn't fit the word "Strikingly," which signals a surprising finding, and the passage is about how big the effect is, not whether it can be predicted. D doesn't work because the studies actually measured this effect and reported what they found.

quality.seed: social science research — Psychologist Claude Steele's Stereotype Threat research on domain identification reducing underrepresented group performance

hardJudge.note: 콜론 뒤 "larger performance drops ... than those for whom math matters little"가 빈칸을 직접 뒷받침하므로 A(most pronounced)가 정답으로 확실함. B는 정반대, C는 'Strikingly'와 충돌하며 효과의 크기가 아닌 예측 가능성을 말해 부분적 오답, D는 연구가 효과를 측정했다는 내용과 불일치. Steele & Aronson(1995) 및 영역 동일시(domain identification)가 고정관념 위협 효과를 조절한다는 사실관계도 정확함. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 선택지 참조와 결론이 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 'Strikingly'의 의미 파악과 콜론 뒤 비교 구문을 연결해야 하므로 medium 수준에 부합. 다만 D의 매력도가 다소 낮은 편.

advisory.note: 콜론 뒤의 'larger performance drops'가 정답을 직접 말해 준다. 오답 B와 D는 지문과 명백히 모순되어 바로 배제되고, 그럴듯한 오답은 C 하나뿐이다. medium 기준인 '부분 근거를 가진 오답 2개 이상'을 충족하지 못한다. Steele의 domain identification 관련 사실은 정확하다.

problem.passage:
In The Second Shift (1989), sociologist Arlie Hochschild reported on years of interviews with and observations of dual-earner couples. Many of the husbands she studied said they believed housework should be divided equally, and some even described their own marriages as equal partnerships. Hochschild's records of who actually cooked, cleaned, and cared for children, however, ______ those claims: in most households, wives did far more of the work at home, adding up to roughly an extra month of labor each year.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In The Second Shift (1989), sociologist Arlie Hochschild reported on years of interviews with and observations of dual-earner couples. Many of the husbands she studied said they believed housework should be divided equally, and some even described their own marriages as equal partnerships. Hochschild's records of who actually cooked, cleaned, and cared for children, however, ______ those claims: in most households, wives did far more of the work at home, adding up to roughly an extra month of labor each year.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: anticipated
belied
exaggerated
obscured
problem.explanation: 'however' 뒤에서 남편들의 '평등 분담' 주장과 달리 아내가 훨씬 많은 일을 했다는 기록이 나오므로, 빈칸에는 기록이 그 주장을 거짓으로 드러냈다는 뜻의 단어가 필요하다. 따라서 '거짓임을 드러내다'라는 뜻의 B가 정답이다. A는 기록이 주장을 미리 예상했다는 뜻이 되어 반박 관계가 성립하지 않는다. C는 주장과의 어긋남을 다루는 것처럼 보이지만, 과장한 쪽은 기록이 아니라 남편들의 주장 자체다. D도 부정적 관계를 담고 있지만, 기록은 주장을 가린 것이 아니라 오히려 그 실상을 드러냈다.
problem.explanationEn: The word "however" sets the husbands' claims of equal sharing against records showing that wives did much more of the work, so the blank needs a word meaning the records showed those claims to be false. That makes B correct, since "belied" means contradicted or exposed as untrue. A would mean the records predicted the claims, so it misses the contrast. C hints at a mismatch, but it was the husbands' claims that were exaggerated, not something the records did to those claims. hardJudge.note: 'however' 전환 + 콜론 뒤 구체적 근거(아내가 훨씬 많은 일을 함)로 '주장이 거짓임을 드러내다'=belied가 유일하게 성립. Because many students from similar class backgrounds ended up on opposite sides of this divide, Eckert argued that the variation was ______ the students: rather than inheriting a fixed way of speaking, adolescents used these sounds as resources to signal which social category they were claiming.

B doesn't fit the idea that students deliberately used the sounds to send signals. D contradicts the finding that students from similar class backgrounds split into groups that spoke differently.

During this phase, Turner argued, the ordinary distinctions of rank and status are ______: initiates wear identical garments, give up their names, and treat one another as equals, forming an intense bond he called communitas. deliberately reinforced
carefully concealed
temporarily suspended
problem.explanation: 지문은 리미널 단계에서 참여자들이 같은 옷을 입고 서로를 동등하게 대하지만, 의례가 끝나면 위계가 "완전히 복원"된다고 말한다. 따라서 위계가 잠시 효력을 멈췄다가 다시 돌아온다는 뜻의 D가 가장 정확하다. A는 위계가 사라진다는 점은 맞지만 "영구적"이라는 표현이 의례 후 위계가 복원된다는 마지막 문장과 충돌한다. B는 평등한 유대라는 묘사와 정반대다. C는 위계가 보이지 않는다는 점은 그럴듯하지만, 숨겨진 채 계속 작동한다는 뜻을 담고 있어 실제로 모두가 동등하게 대한다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says that during the liminal phase, initiates dress alike and treat one another as equals, but after the rite the hierarchies are "fully restored." So rank must be set aside only for a while and then return, which makes D the most precise choice. A is right that the distinctions disappear, but "permanently" contradicts the last sentence, where the hierarchies come back. B is the opposite of the egalitarian bonding the text describes. C seems plausible because rank is not visible, but "concealed" suggests the hierarchy is still operating in secret, while the text says participants really do treat each other as equals.

quality.seed: social science research — Anthropologist Victor Turner's Communitas concept describing egalitarian bonding in ritual liminality across societies

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검산 완료: 리미널 단계의 평등(동일 복장, 이름 포기)과 의례 후 "hierarchies are fully restored"를 연결해야 "temporarily suspended"가 도출됨. A는 전반부와 부합하나 마지막 문장과 충돌(부분 정답 오답), C는 가시성 측면에서 그럴듯하나 실제 평등 대우와 불일치(부분 정답 오답), B는 반대 의미로 말은 되나 배제 가능. 두 정보(평등 묘사 + 복원 문장) 연결이 필요하므로 medium 적합. Turner의 liminality/communitas 개념 기술은 사실과 일치. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: D는 동등하게 대한다는 근거와 위계가 '완전히 복원'된다는 근거를 연결해야 확정된다. A는 부분적으로 맞아 매력적인 오답이고, C도 그럴듯하며, B는 반대 의미라 쉽게 배제된다. Turner의 리미널리티·코뮤니타스 설명은 사실에 부합한다.

In the 1980s, political scientist James Flynn compiled decades of intelligence test data from more than a dozen developed nations and found that average raw scores had risen by roughly three points per decade. Because the gains appeared in countries with very different school systems and economies, Flynn argued that they could not be ______ to any single national policy; instead, he proposed that broad shifts in modern life, such as greater exposure to abstract classification tasks, had gradually changed how people approach test questions.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In the 1980s, political scientist James Flynn compiled decades of intelligence test data from more than a dozen developed nations and found that average raw scores had risen by roughly three points per decade. Because the gains appeared in countries with very different school systems and economies, Flynn argued that they could not be ______ to any single national policy; instead, he proposed that broad shifts in modern life, such as greater exposure to abstract classification tasks, had gradually changed how people approach test questions.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: attributed
compared
confined
introduced
problem.explanation: Flynn은 여러 나라에서 공통으로 나타난 점수 상승의 원인을 따지고 있으며, 'instead' 뒤에서 다른 원인(현대 생활의 광범위한 변화)을 제시한다. 따라서 상승을 어느 한 정책의 '탓으로 돌릴' 수 없다는 뜻인 A가 정답이다. C는 'to'와 어울리고 '여러 나라에 나타났다'는 사실과 얼핏 맞아 보이지만, 상승이 한 정책 '안에 한정될' 수 없다는 말은 원인을 설명하는 뒷문장과 이어지지 않는다. B는 정책과 '비교'한다는 뜻이 되어 원인 논의가 되지 않는다. D는 정책에 '도입된다'는 뜻이 되어 상승의 원인을 따지는 흐름과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Flynn is reasoning about what caused the score gains, and after "instead" he offers a different cause: broad changes in modern life. So the logical claim is that the gains could not be credited to, or blamed on, any single national policy, which makes A correct. C fits grammatically with "to" and seems to echo the point that the gains showed up in many countries, but saying the gains could not be "confined" to a policy doesn't lead into the causal explanation that follows. B would mean comparing the gains to a policy, which isn't an argument about causes. D would mean the gains were "introduced" to a policy, which doesn't match the text's focus on causes.

hardJudge.note: 정답 검산: 'instead' 뒤에 대안적 원인(현대 생활의 변화)이 제시되므로 빈칸은 '원인을 ~에 돌리다'(attributed to)가 유일하게 논리적. advisory.note: Flynn은 정치학자이고, 1984·1987년 연구에서 대략 10년에 3점 상승을 보고했으므로 사실관계는 정확함. 정답 A는 'instead' 뒤의 대안적 원인 제시로 확정됨. C(confined)는 그럴듯한 오답이고, B와 D는 비교적 쉽게 배제됨. 중간 난이도로 적합함.

So the blank needs a word meaning basic and ever-present, which is B. A seems tempting because impression management sounds intentional, but it doesn't capture the occasional-versus-constant contrast and leans toward the deceit Goffman rejected. C echoes the theater metaphor, but it just repeats the comparison rather than expressing that performance is universal and essential. D means short-lived, which actually aligns with "occasional" and breaks the contrast.

problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Students ... mastered"와 뒤 "students ... altogether"는 각각 독립절이므로 둘을 올바르게 연결해야 한다. A는 쉼표와 종속 접속사 whereas로 두 절을 대조 관계로 바르게 잇는다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 아무 문장부호나 접속사 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 whereas 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 접속사와 그 절을 잘못 갈라놓는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("Students ... mastered") and the text after it ("students ... altogether") are both independent clauses, so they need a proper connection. A is correct because a comma plus the conjunction "whereas" joins the two clauses and shows their contrast. B is wrong because a comma alone between two independent clauses creates a comma splice. C is wrong because joining the clauses with no punctuation or conjunction creates a run-on sentence. D is wrong because the comma after "whereas" wrongly separates the conjunction from the clause it introduces.
