In the 1980s, anthropologist Richard Shweder and his colleagues interviewed children and adults in Chicago and in Bhubaneswar, India, about which actions they considered morally wrong. Many Western philosophers had assumed that people everywhere judge right and wrong mainly by asking whether an action harms someone or treats them unfairly. ______ Shweder found that participants in Bhubaneswar often described actions such as breaking food or family customs as serious moral wrongs, even when no one appeared to be harmed.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In the 1980s, anthropologist Richard Shweder and his colleagues interviewed children and adults in Chicago and in Bhubaneswar, India, about which actions they considered morally wrong. Many Western philosophers had assumed that people everywhere judge right and wrong mainly by asking whether an action harms someone or treats them unfairly. ______ Shweder found that participants in Bhubaneswar often described actions such as breaking food or family customs as serious moral wrongs, even when no one appeared to be harmed.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: For example,
Similarly,
As a result,
However,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 사람들이 어디서나 해악·불공정 여부로 도덕을 판단한다는 가정을 제시하고, 뒷문장은 해악이 없어도 관습 위반을 도덕적 잘못으로 본 결과를 보여 준다. 따라서 두 문장은 대조 관계이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 뒷문장이 가정을 뒷받침하는 예시인 것처럼 만들지만, 실제로 뒷문장은 가정과 어긋난다. B는 두 내용이 비슷하다고 표시하고, C는 가정이 발견의 원인인 것처럼 만들기 때문에 둘 다 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence states an assumption: people everywhere judge morality mainly by harm and fairness. The next sentence reports that people in Bhubaneswar called customs violations serious wrongs even when no one was harmed. That finding contradicts the assumption, so the two sentences contrast, and D is correct. A would make the finding an example that supports the assumption, but it actually goes against it. B says the two ideas are alike, and C says the assumption caused the finding, so neither one works.

quality.seed: social science research — Anthropologist Richard Shweder's Moral Relativism study challenging universality of Western ethical principles across cultures

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(해악·공정성 가정)과 뒷문장(해악 없는 관습 위반도 도덕적 잘못으로 판단)의 대조가 명확하여 "However"가 유일한 정답. 오답 A·B·C는 각각 예시·유사·인과라는 전형적 오개념 선택지로 적절. Shweder의 1980년대 시카고·부바네스와르 연구 내용과 일치하며 사실 오류 없음. 한·영 해설이 동일한 결론과 선택지 참조를 가지며 영어 자연스러움. 단서가 지문에 직접 드러나고 한 단계 추론으로 풀리므로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 'had assumed' 다음에 반대 증거가 오는 대조 구조가 분명하고 추론은 한 단계뿐이다. 오답은 예시·유사·인과를 나타내는 전형적인 연결어여서 easy 난이도에 맞다. Shweder의 Chicago·Bhubaneswar 연구도 사실과 맞다.

problem.passage:
In the 1950s, psychologist Leon Festinger studied a small group whose members believed the world would end on a specific date. He reasoned that people who had given up jobs and possessions for a belief would feel intense discomfort if that belief were proven false. ______ he predicted that, after the date passed uneventfully, many members would hold their belief even more strongly and begin seeking new followers to ease that discomfort.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In the 1950s, psychologist Leon Festinger studied a small group whose members believed the world would end on a specific date. He reasoned that people who had given up jobs and possessions for a belief would feel intense discomfort if that belief were proven false. ______ he predicted that, after the date passed uneventfully, many members would hold their belief even more strongly and begin seeking new followers to ease that discomfort.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Therefore,
However,
For example,
Similarly,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 믿음이 틀린 것으로 드러나면 구성원들이 강한 불편함을 느낄 것이라는 Festinger의 추론이고, 뒤 문장은 그 추론에서 나온 예측(믿음 강화와 신도 모집)이다. 따라서 결과·결론을 나타내는 A가 정답이다. B는 대조를 나타내지만 뒤 문장은 앞 문장과 반대되는 내용이 아니다. C는 예시를 나타내지만 예측은 불편함의 구체적 사례가 아니다. D는 유사한 내용을 추가할 때 쓰는데, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장과 비슷한 별개의 내용이 아니라 앞 문장에서 이어지는 결론이다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentence gives Festinger's reasoning: members would feel intense discomfort if their belief were proven false. The next sentence gives the prediction he drew from that reasoning, which is that they would strengthen the belief and recruit followers. Because the second idea follows from the first, choice A, which signals a result or conclusion, is correct. Choice B signals contrast, but the prediction does not oppose the reasoning. Choice C introduces an example, but the prediction is not a specific case of discomfort. Choice D adds a similar point, but the second sentence is a conclusion drawn from the first, not a parallel idea.

quality.seed: social science research — Psychologist Leon Festinger's Cognitive Dissonance prediction confirming belief intensification after failed prophecy dates

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(추론: 믿음이 틀리면 강한 불편함) → 뒤 문장(그로부터 도출된 예측)이므로 결과·결론 전환어 'Therefore'가 유일하게 논리적임. 직접 검산 결과 정답 A 타당. 역사적 사실(Festinger, When Prophecy Fails, 1956, 인지부조화·개종 활동 예측)과 부합. 오답 B(대조)·C(예시)·D(유사 추가)는 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제되지만 전형적 오개념으로 그럴듯함. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. 지문은 원 출처 그대로의 인용이 아닌 자체 서술로 판단되어 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: Festinger의 When Prophecy Fails(1956) 사례가 사실에 맞게 서술됨. 추론→예측의 인과 관계가 명시적이어서 Therefore가 정답이며, 나머지 세 선택지는 전형적인 오개념 선택지임. 다만 예측 내용이 직관에 반해 보여 However를 고르는 학생이 있을 수 있으나, 앞 문장의 '불편함'이 근거로 제시되므로 easy 수준에 적합함.

problem.passage:
In his 1983 book Frames of Mind, psychologist Howard Gardner argued that a single IQ score captures only a narrow slice of human ability. Rejecting the idea of one general intelligence, ______ eventually eight in all, including musical, spatial, and interpersonal intelligence, each of which he claimed could develop largely independently of the others.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In his 1983 book Frames of Mind, psychologist Howard Gardner argued that a single IQ score captures only a narrow slice of human ability. Rejecting the idea of one general intelligence, ______ eventually eight in all, including musical, spatial, and interpersonal intelligence, each of which he claimed could develop largely independently of the others.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the book proposed several distinct cognitive domains,
Gardner proposed several distinct cognitive domains,
IQ tests were challenged by several distinct cognitive domains,
several distinct cognitive domains were proposed by Gardner,
problem.explanation:
정답 B. 분사구 'Rejecting the idea of one general intelligence'의 의미상 주어는 어떤 생각을 거부하는 행위자, 즉 Gardner이므로 주절 주어도 Gardner여야 한다.
A: 'the book'은 Gardner의 저작물이다. 수식 대상과 관련은 있지만 범주가 다르다(사람이 아니라 책). 책이 생각을 '거부한다'고 하면 수식어가 사람 대신 책에 걸리게 된다.
C: 'IQ tests'는 거부하는 주체가 아니라 오히려 비판받는 대상이라 수식어와 연결되지 않는 엉뚱한 주어다.
D: 수동태로 바꾸면서 'several distinct cognitive domains'가 주어가 되었다. 복수 주어와 동사 were의 수일치는 맞지만, 인지 영역들이 하나의 일반 지능이라는 생각을 거부할 수는 없으므로 현수 수식어가 된다.
problem.explanationEn:
B is correct. The opening phrase "Rejecting the idea of one general intelligence" needs a subject that can actually reject an idea. That person is Gardner, so he must be the subject of the main clause.
A is wrong because "the book" is Gardner's work, not Gardner himself. It's a related noun from a different category, so the phrase would describe the book instead of the person who did the rejecting.
C is wrong because "IQ tests" are what Gardner was arguing against. They aren't the ones doing the rejecting, so the phrase would attach to an unrelated subject.
D is wrong because the passive version makes "several distinct cognitive domains" the subject. The subject and verb agree ("domains were"), but domains can't reject an idea, so the opening phrase is left dangling.

hardJudge.note: 문두 분사구 'Rejecting the idea of one general intelligence'의 행위자는 Gardner이며 B만 주어가 일치. A(the book)는 저작물로 범주 차이 오답, C(IQ tests)는 비판 대상, D는 수동태로 인지 영역이 주어가 되어 현수 수식. 네 선택지 모두 문법적으로 완전하고 수일치로는 구분 불가. 사실관계(1983년 Frames of Mind, 최종 8개 지능, musical/spatial/interpersonal 포함) 정확. 단, 이 문항은 College Board 분류상 'Boundaries'보다 'Form, Structure, and Sense'(modifier placement)에 가까움을 참고로 기록.

advisory.note: B가 정답인 것은 맞다. 앞 문장의 주체가 Gardner이고 뒤의 'he claimed'도 Gardner를 가리킨다. 다만 A('the book proposed')는 환유로 볼 여지가 있어 복수정답 시비가 생길 위험이 있다. 그래도 'each of which he claimed'와 이어지는 흐름, 그리고 거부하는 행위자가 사람이라는 점에서 B가 가장 낫다. 네 선택지 모두 수일치가 맞아 수일치만으로는 정답을 가려낼 수 없다. C와 D는 명백한 현수 수식어다.

problem.passage:
In her study of airline flight attendants, sociologist Arlie Hochschild observed that moods moved readily between workers and passengers. An attendant's practiced warmth, she found, could noticeably calm anxious passengers______ that same warmth, sustained hour after hour across long shifts, often left the attendants themselves feeling emotionally depleted.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In her study of airline flight attendants, sociologist Arlie Hochschild observed that moods moved readily between workers and passengers. An attendant's practiced warmth, she found, could noticeably calm anxious passengers______ that same warmth, sustained hour after hour across long shifts, often left the attendants themselves feeling emotionally depleted.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , for
, but
but;
problem.explanation:
정답 C: 빈칸 앞(승무원의 따뜻함이 승객을 진정시킴)과 뒤(그 따뜻함이 승무원 자신을 지치게 함)는 모두 독립절이며, 승객에게는 이롭지만 승무원에게는 해롭다는 대조 관계이다. 따라서 쉼표+대조 등위접속사 ', but'이 알맞다.
A: 쉼표+등위접속사 형식은 맞지만 'for'는 '왜냐하면'이라는 이유를 나타낸다. 승무원이 지친 것이 승객이 진정된 이유는 아니므로 논리 관계가 맞지 않는다.
B: 쉼표 하나만으로 두 독립절을 이었으므로 콤마 스플라이스이다.
D: 세미콜론이 접속사 'but' 뒤에 와서 'but'이 앞 절에 붙어 버린다. 그러면 앞 절이 'but'으로 어색하게 끝나므로 절 경계를 잘못 나눈 것이다.
problem.explanationEn:
C is correct. The text before the blank ("An attendant's practiced warmth... could noticeably calm anxious passengers") is an independent clause, and so is the text after it ("that same warmth... often left the attendants themselves feeling emotionally depleted"). The two ideas contrast: the warmth helps passengers but drains the attendants. A comma plus the contrasting coordinating conjunction "but" joins the clauses correctly and signals that relationship.
A is wrong because a comma plus a coordinating conjunction is the right structure, but "for" means "because." The attendants' exhaustion doesn't explain why the passengers calmed down, so the logic doesn't work.
B is wrong because it joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice.
D is wrong because putting the semicolon after "but" attaches the conjunction to the first clause, which then ends awkwardly on "but." The semicolon doesn't fall at the real boundary between the clauses.

hardJudge.note: 앞 절("An attendant's practiced warmth, she found, could noticeably calm anxious passengers")과 뒤 절("that same warmth, sustained ..., often left the attendants themselves feeling emotionally depleted")은 각각 삽입구('she found', 'sustained hour after hour across long shifts')를 품은 완전한 독립절이며, 승객에게 이롭지만 승무원에게 해롭다는 대조가 문맥상 명확하다. 정답 C ', but'은 쉼표+등위접속사로 대조를 정확히 표현한다. A ', for'는 형식은 적법하나 인과 관계가 성립하지 않아 논리 오류(A·C 모두 문법적으로 가능하므로 논리 관계 판단이 필수), B는 콤마 스플라이스, D는 세미콜론이 접속사 뒤에 놓여 절 경계가 아닌 곳에 위치한다. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 정확히 설명하며 모순 없음. Hochschild의 감정노동 연구 서술은 사실에 부합하고 원문 인용 흔적 없음. 선택지 D의 이중 공백은 경미한 표기 문제로 판정에는 영향 없음.

advisory.note: 삽입어 'she found'와 분사구 'sustained hour after hour...' 때문에 절 경계를 판별하기가 까다롭다. ', for'는 문법적으로 맞고 논리 관계로만 걸러지는 오답이어서 대조 관계를 판단해야 한다. 다만 접속사 의미를 고르는 판단은 transitions 유형과 일부 겹친다. D는 세미콜론이 절 경계가 아닌 'but' 뒤에 붙어 있어 체크리스트 5번을 충족한다.

problem.passage:
In a well-known study by psychologist Elizabeth Loftus, participants read short accounts of childhood events supplied by their relatives. One account, describing being lost in a shopping mall as a child, was entirely made up. After repeated interviews, a substantial minority of participants not only accepted the invented episode but also added vivid details of their own. Most participants, however, consistently said they had no memory of the event, even when told that a family member remembered it clearly. ______ false childhood memories seem to be possible to create but far from inevitable, with susceptibility varying considerably from person to person.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In a well-known study by psychologist Elizabeth Loftus, participants read short accounts of childhood events supplied by their relatives. One account, describing being lost in a shopping mall as a child, was entirely made up. After repeated interviews, a substantial minority of participants not only accepted the invented episode but also added vivid details of their own. Most participants, however, consistently said they had no memory of the event, even when told that a family member remembered it clearly. ______ false childhood memories seem to be possible to create but far from inevitable, with susceptibility varying considerably from person to person.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
Taken together,
By contrast,
Meanwhile,
problem.explanation:
정답 B: 지문에는 상반되어 보이는 관찰 두 가지가 나온다. (1) 상당수의 소수 참가자가 지어낸 기억을 받아들였고, (2) 대다수는 끝까지 거부했다. 마지막 문장의 '가능하지만 필연적이지는 않다'는 이 두 관찰을 함께 고려해야만 나오는 결론이므로, 종합을 나타내는 'Taken together,'가 알맞다.
A(Nevertheless,): 바로 앞 문장(대다수가 거부함)과 반대되는 내용이 이어질 때 쓰는 말이다. 따라서 첫 번째 관찰(기억 이식 가능)만 반영하는 셈이다. 그런데 마지막 문장은 앞 문장의 '거부'도 포함하므로 맞지 않는다.
C(By contrast,): 두 관찰이 서로 어긋난다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 것이다. 마지막 문장은 앞 내용과 대비되는 새 사실이 아니라 두 관찰을 아우르는 결론이다.
D(Meanwhile,): 동시에 일어나는 별개의 사건이나 화제 전환을 나타내므로, 결론 도출과 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, B: The passage gives two observations that seem to conflict. First, a substantial minority of participants accepted and added details to an invented memory. Second, most participants consistently rejected it. The last sentence says false memories are "possible to create but far from inevitable." You can only reach that conclusion by considering both observations at once, so "Taken together," is the right transition.
A ("Nevertheless,") would mean the last sentence goes against the sentence right before it, the one about most people resisting. That reflects only the first observation, but the conclusion actually builds on the resistance too.
C ("By contrast,") treats the two findings as a simple contrast. The last sentence doesn't set up a new opposing fact; it combines both findings into one conclusion.
D ("Meanwhile,") signals something happening at the same time or a change of topic, so it doesn't introduce a conclusion.

hardJudge.note: 두 관찰(소수 수용 vs 다수 거부)을 종합해 '가능하지만 필연적이지 않음'이라는 결론으로 잇는 구조가 명확하며 B가 유일한 정답. A는 직전 문장과의 역접만, C는 단순 대조만, D는 화제 전환으로 각각 배제 가능. 사실관계(Loftus & Pickrell 'lost in the mall', 친척 제공 사건, 반복 면담, 약 1/4 수용)도 문제 없음. 다만 'Taken together, false childhood memories seem...'은 분사구문이 '연구 결과'가 아닌 'false childhood memories'를 수식하는 형태라 엄밀히는 현수분사(dangling modifier)에 가깝고 'seem to be possible to create'도 다소 어색함—논리 판정에는 영향 없으나 실제 SAT 문체 기준으로는 정답 문장의 표현을 다듬을 여지가 있음.

advisory.note: Loftus의 lost-in-the-mall 연구 내용은 사실에 부합한다(약 25% 수용). 마지막 문장은 두 관찰을 종합한 결론이므로 정답은 B 하나로 정해진다. Nevertheless는 앞 문장만 거슬러 첫 번째 관찰만 반영하는 오답, By contrast는 단순 대조 오답이다.

problem.passage:
In her research on online communities, Sherry Turkle described multiuser games as possible "identity workshops," spaces where people try out versions of themselves that differ from who they are offline. A research team building on her work surveyed players who keep more than one character, or persona, in online role-playing games. For each player, the team recorded two things: how many personas the player kept and how much those personas differed from the player's offline personality. The team proposes that playing many personas does not by itself lead to self-insight. Instead, the team argues, players gain self-insight when they keep several personas that each differ sharply from their offline selves.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the research team's proposal?
problem.stimulus: In her research on online communities, Sherry Turkle described multiuser games as possible "identity workshops," spaces where people try out versions of themselves that differ from who they are offline. A research team building on her work surveyed players who keep more than one character, or persona, in online role-playing games. For each player, the team recorded two things: how many personas the player kept and how much those personas differed from the player's offline personality. The team proposes that playing many personas does not by itself lead to self-insight. Instead, the team argues, players gain self-insight when they keep several personas that each differ sharply from their offline selves.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the research team's proposal?
options: Players who kept five or more personas reported much more self-insight than players who kept only two personas, whether or not their personas resembled their offline personalities.
Players whose personas differed sharply from their offline personalities reported more self-insight than other players, and these players also tended to keep more personas than other players did.
Players who spent more than twenty hours a week in the games reported more self-insight than players who spent less time playing, regardless of how many personas they kept.

Among players who kept the same number of personas, those whose personas differed sharply from their offline selves reported the most self-insight, while players who kept many personas resembling their offline selves reported no more insight than players who kept few.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: 연구팀의 주장에는 두 부분이 있다. (1) 페르소나의 개수만으로는 자기 통찰이 생기지 않는다. (2) 통찰을 낳는 것은 오프라인 성격과 크게 다른 페르소나를 여러 개 갖는 것이다. D는 페르소나 개수를 같게 맞춘 상태에서 차이 정도가 클수록 통찰이 크다는 것을 보여 주고, 오프라인 자아와 비슷한 페르소나는 개수가 많아도 효과가 없다는 것도 보여 준다. 두 변수를 함께 다루므로 주장의 두 부분을 모두 뒷받침한다.
A(한쪽 변수만 봄: 개수): 차이 정도와 상관없이 개수만으로 통찰이 늘어났다는 결과다. '개수만으로는 부족하다'는 주장과 정면으로 어긋난다.
B(다른 쪽 변수만 봄: 차이 정도): 차이가 큰 플레이어의 통찰이 컸다는 점은 주장과 맞아 보인다. 하지만 이 플레이어들은 페르소나 개수도 더 많았다. 그래서 통찰의 원인이 차이 정도인지 개수인지 가려낼 수 없다.
C(자료에 없는 제3의 변수): 연구팀이 기록하지 않은 플레이 시간으로 통찰을 설명한다. 연구팀의 주장과는 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, D: The team's proposal has two parts. (1) The number of personas alone does not lead to self-insight. (2) Self-insight comes from keeping several personas that each differ sharply from the offline self. D compares players who kept the same number of personas and shows that the ones with more divergent personas reported more insight. It also shows that keeping many personas that resemble the offline self brings no extra insight. Because D looks at both variables together, it supports both parts of the proposal.
A looks only at the number of personas. It says insight rose with the number of personas whether or not they differed from the offline self. That contradicts the team's claim that numbers alone aren't enough.
B looks only at how much the personas differed. It seems to fit the proposal, but the players with divergent personas also kept more personas. So you can't tell whether their insight came from the divergence or from the number.
C uses a third variable, playing time, which the team never recorded. It tells you nothing about the team's proposal.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검산: 개수를 통제한 상태에서 차이 정도가 통찰을 좌우하고, 비슷한 페르소나는 개수가 많아도 효과가 없음을 보여 주어 주장의 두 부분(개수만으로는 불충분 + 크게 다른 페르소나 여러 개가 핵심)을 모두 뒷받침한다. A는 주장 (1)과 정면 충돌, B는 차이 정도와 개수가 함께 움직여 교란되어 원인 분리 불가(단일 변수만 보면 정답처럼 보이는 함정), C는 자료에 없는 플레이 시간 변수 사용. 해설은 각 오답의 결함을 정확히 기술. 사소한 참고: 'identity workshop'이라는 표현은 원래 Amy Bruckman의 용어이며 Turkle이 이를 인용해 사용했으므로 "Turkle described ... as 'identity workshops'"는 틀린 서술은 아니나 귀속이 다소 느슨함(정답 판단에는 무관). 문항은 원작이며 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: D는 페르소나 개수를 통제하고 차이 정도의 효과를 보이며, 차이가 작으면 개수가 많아도 효과가 없음을 보인다. 따라서 주장의 두 부분을 모두 뒷받침한다. B는 교란 변수 함정으로서 hard 수준에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
In the late 1970s, anthropologist Catherine Lutz lived on Ifaluk, a small atoll in Micronesia. She found that its residents sorted feelings into categories that do not line up neatly with the English words often treated as universal. For example, Ifaluk speakers use the word song for a kind of justified, morally charged anger. It is directed at someone who has broken a community rule, especially a rule about sharing food and labor. Lutz noticed that this emotion word is used most often in the same settings where duties to share are strongest. From this, she argued that a community's social arrangements actively shape which emotion categories its members recognize and use, rather than people everywhere starting from a fixed set of basic emotions.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Lutz's argument?
problem.stimulus: In the late 1970s, anthropologist Catherine Lutz lived on Ifaluk, a small atoll in Micronesia. She found that its residents sorted feelings into categories that do not line up neatly with the English words often treated as universal. For example, Ifaluk speakers use the word song for a kind of justified, morally charged anger. It is directed at someone who has broken a community rule, especially a rule about sharing food and labor. Lutz noticed that this emotion word is used most often in the same settings where duties to share are strongest. From this, she argued that a community's social arrangements actively shape which emotion categories its members recognize and use, rather than people everywhere starting from a fixed set of basic emotions.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Lutz's argument?
options: After a wage-labor program released some Ifaluk families, but not their neighbors on the same atoll, from traditional food-sharing duties, those families gradually used song less often than their neighbors did.
Several other Pacific atolls where duties to share food are strong also have a word for a justified, rule-enforcing anger similar to song.
Ifaluk children who learned to use song at an unusually early age grew up to be especially strict about following food-sharing rules as adults.
On Pacific islands where frequent typhoons make food scarce, both strict sharing duties and words like song are common, while both are rare on islands with plentiful food.
problem.explanation: Lutz는 사회 구조(나눔 의무)가 원인이 되어 감정 범주(song)를 만든다고 주장한다. A는 같은 섬, 같은 환경에 사는 이웃 가구 중 일부에게서만 나눔 의무가 사라진 뒤에 song 사용이 줄었다는 발견이다. 원인이 결과보다 먼저 변했으므로 인과 방향이 맞고, 환경이 같으므로 제3의 요인도 통제된다. 따라서 주장을 가장 직접적으로 지지한다. B는 다른 섬에서도 같은 동시 발생이 나타난다는 것일 뿐이라 상관을 인과로 받아들이는 오류다. C는 감정어 학습이 나눔 행동을 낳는다는 뜻이어서 인과 방향이 거꾸로다. D는 식량 부족이라는 제3의 원인이 나눔 의무와 song을 함께 만들어 낸다는 설명이므로, 사회 구조가 감정 범주를 형성한다는 주장을 지지하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: Lutz claims that social arrangements (sharing duties) cause emotion categories like song. Choice A describes a change that happened only to some families, while their neighbors on the same atoll kept the old duties. Song use dropped afterward, and only in the families whose duties changed. Because the cause comes before the effect, the direction is right. Because the environment is the same for both groups, a third factor is ruled out. That makes A the most direct support. Choice B just repeats the same co-occurrence on other islands, so it treats correlation as causation. Choice C runs the causation backward: learning the emotion word leads to stricter sharing. Choice D points to a third cause, food scarcity, that could produce both strict sharing and words like song. That offers an alternative explanation instead of supporting Lutz's claim.

hardJudge.note: 지문의 관찰 자료(song 사용이 나눔 의무가 강한 상황과 동시 발생)는 상관에 그치고, Lutz의 주장만이 인과를 담고 있어 구조가 적절함. A는 원인(나눔 의무) 변화가 선행하고 같은 환경의 이웃이 대조군 역할을 해 제3요인을 통제하는 자연실험 형태로 정답 타당. B는 상관 반복(상관→인과 치환), C는 인과 방향 역전, D는 식량 부족이라는 제3 원인으로 각각 레시피 오답 유형에 정확히 대응. Lutz의 Ifaluk 연구·song 개념은 실제 인류학 문헌과 일치하며 지문 자체는 원창작으로 저작권 우려 없음. 해설도 각 선지 판단 근거를 정확히 기술함.

advisory.note: A는 사례 내 자연 실험 구조로, 원인이 먼저 바뀌고 같은 환경이라는 대조군이 있어 정답으로 타당하다. B는 상관을 반복한 것, C는 인과 방향이 뒤바뀐 것, D는 교란 변수(식량 부족)다. D는 '무관한 원인'이라기보다 제3의 공통 원인에 가깝지만 5번 항목의 취지에는 맞는다. 자료가 하나뿐이라 multi_source 특성은 해당하지 않는다. 임금노동 프로그램 자체가 교란 요인이 될 여지는 약간 있지만, 다른 선지와 비교하면 A가 확실히 우위다.

problem.passage:
Psychologist Barry Schwartz has argued that an abundance of options can leave people less satisfied with the choices they make. According to Schwartz, the problem is not simply that more options take longer to sort through. Rather, when many alternatives are available, people more easily imagine that one of the options they passed over would have been better, and this sense of forgone possibilities lowers how much they enjoy whatever they end up choosing. Schwartz notes that, in surveys, shoppers often say they prefer stores with wide selections.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Schwartz's explanation of why abundant options reduce decision satisfaction?
problem.stimulus: Psychologist Barry Schwartz has argued that an abundance of options can leave people less satisfied with the choices they make. According to Schwartz, the problem is not simply that more options take longer to sort through. Rather, when many alternatives are available, people more easily imagine that one of the options they passed over would have been better, and this sense of forgone possibilities lowers how much they enjoy whatever they end up choosing. Schwartz notes that, in surveys, shoppers often say they prefer stores with wide selections.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Schwartz's explanation of why abundant options reduce decision satisfaction?
options: Participants who chose a chocolate from a display of 30 varieties took longer to decide than participants who chose from a display of 6 varieties, and both groups rated their chocolate as equally enjoyable.

Participants who chose a chocolate from 30 varieties rated it less enjoyable than those who chose from 6, but this difference disappeared when the unchosen varieties were removed from view before tasting, so that participants could no longer compare their pick with the alternatives.
Participants who chose a chocolate from 30 varieties reported spending more total money on chocolate in the following month than participants who chose from 6 varieties.
When asked before choosing, most participants said they would rather pick a chocolate from a display of 30 varieties than from a display of 6 varieties.
problem.explanation:
정답 B: Schwartz의 주장은 선택지가 많으면 만족도가 떨어지고, 그 원인이 선택 시간이 아니라 '포기한 대안과의 비교(놓친 가능성에 대한 생각)'라는 것이다. B는 만족도 저하를 보여 줄 뿐 아니라, 대안을 눈앞에서 치워 비교를 막으면 그 저하가 사라진다는 결과를 제시한다. 따라서 가설이 말하는 원인 메커니즘을 직접 확인해 준다.
A(가설을 반박하는 결과): 결정 시간은 더 길었지만 만족도에는 차이가 없었다. 이는 선택지가 많으면 만족도가 낮아진다는 핵심 주장과 정면으로 어긋난다.
C(가설과 무관한 사실): 이후 지출액은 결정 만족도나 포기한 대안과의 비교와 아무 관련이 없다.
D(지문 재진술): 사람들이 다양한 선택지를 선호한다는 내용은 지문의 설문 결과를 다시 말한 것일 뿐이다. 만족도가 어떻게 되는지나 그 원인에 대해서는 아무것도 보여 주지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, B: Schwartz claims that having many options lowers satisfaction. He also says the cause is not the extra time spent deciding but people comparing their choice with the alternatives they gave up. B shows lower enjoyment with 30 varieties. It also shows that this drop disappears when the unchosen options are taken out of view, so participants can't compare. That result directly supports the cause Schwartz proposes.
A (contradicts the hypothesis): Choosing took longer, but enjoyment was the same in both groups. This goes against the central claim that more options reduce satisfaction.
C (irrelevant): How much people spent later has nothing to do with how satisfied they were with their choice or with comparing it to forgone options.
D (restates the passage): Saying people prefer large selections just repeats the survey finding already in the passage. It tells us nothing about satisfaction or what causes it.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 Schwartz의 가설(선택지 과다→만족도 저하, 원인은 시간이 아니라 포기한 대안과의 비교)만 제시하고 증거는 없으며, 설문 언급은 오히려 대조적 사실이다. B는 만족도 저하 + 대안 제거 시 효과 소멸이라는 가상 결과로 원인 메커니즘(비교)을 직접 지지하며 '시간' 대안 설명을 배제한다. A는 만족도 차이 없음으로 가설 반박(시간 요소 포함해 매력적), C는 무관, D는 지문 설문 재진술. 해설은 각 선택지 판정과 정확히 일치하고 모순 없음. 단순 '만족도 저하' 확인이 아니라 메커니즘 수준에서 증거를 선별해야 하므로 medium 이상의 인과 추론을 요구한다.

advisory.note: B는 만족도 저하가 있다는 점과 함께 비교를 차단했을 때 그 차이가 사라진다는 개입 결과까지 보여 준다. 그래서 단순한 연관성을 넘어 가설이 말하는 메커니즘을 검증한다. A는 시간 설명을 배제하는 오답이자 반박 사례, D는 지문 설문의 재진술이다. 다만 B만 유독 길고 상세해서 길이가 정답 단서가 될 수 있다는 점은 경미한 우려다. 지문의 설문 언급은 가설을 뒷받침하는 증거가 아니므로 1번 항목은 충족된다.

problem.passage:
Sociologist Erving Goffman used the term "footing" to describe the stance a speaker takes toward their own words, noting that a person may present a statement as their own view or as someone else's. In one meeting that researchers recorded, a department manager announced a new scheduling policy that many employees disliked. When a staff member objected, the manager said, "Look, I'm just passing along what headquarters decided," even though the meeting notes later showed that the manager had drafted the policy and pushed for it at headquarters. A few minutes later, after an employee praised the policy's flexible break times, the manager answered, "Yes, I worked hard to get that part included."

Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about the manager's comments during the meeting?
problem.stimulus: Sociologist Erving Goffman used the term "footing" to describe the stance a speaker takes toward their own words, noting that a person may present a statement as their own view or as someone else's. In one meeting that researchers recorded, a department manager announced a new scheduling policy that many employees disliked. When a staff member objected, the manager said, "Look, I'm just passing along what headquarters decided," even though the meeting notes later showed that the manager had drafted the policy and pushed for it at headquarters. A few minutes later, after an employee praised the policy's flexible break times, the manager answered, "Yes, I worked hard to get that part included."
problem.question: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about the manager's comments during the meeting?
options: The manager was only passing along a decision made at headquarters, so the manager could not answer employees' objections.
The manager changed how the comments were presented because the manager came to doubt the policy after hearing the staff member's objection.
The manager's comments show that people in leadership roles usually avoid explaining unpopular decisions to the employees they affect.
The manager presented the same policy either as someone else's choice or as personal work, depending on whether the part being discussed was criticized or praised.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: 매니저는 비판을 받을 때는 "본사 결정을 전할 뿐"이라며 정책을 남의 것처럼 말했지만, 실제로는 자신이 직접 정책 초안을 쓰고 밀어붙였다. 반면 칭찬을 받자 "내가 애써 넣었다"며 자기 공으로 돌렸다. 말한 것과 실제 사이의 이런 차이로 보아, 매니저는 반응에 따라 자기 말에 대한 입장(footing)을 전략적으로 바꿨다고 추론할 수 있다.
A: 지문에 나온 매니저의 말을 그대로 사실로 받아들인 오답이다. 회의록을 보면 그 말은 사실이 아니다.
B: 어긋남을 반대로 해석한 오답이다. 매니저는 정책을 의심한 것이 아니다. 오히려 칭찬받은 부분은 자기 공으로 내세웠다.
C: 지문과 상관없는 일반론이다. 지문은 리더 전반의 경향을 다루지 않고 한 사람의 입장 전환을 다룬다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, D: When the manager was criticized, they said they were "just passing along" headquarters' decision. But the meeting notes show the manager actually drafted the policy and pushed for it. Later, when someone praised part of the policy, the manager took credit for it. This gap between what the manager said and what really happened suggests the manager changed their footing on purpose: they avoided responsibility when the policy was criticized and claimed ownership when it was praised.
A: This choice treats the manager's own words as true. The meeting notes show they weren't.
B: This choice reads the mismatch backward. Nothing in the text shows the manager came to doubt the policy. In fact, the manager proudly claimed part of it afterward.
C: This is a general claim about leaders that the text doesn't support. The text describes one manager's shifts, not a common pattern among leaders.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 매니저의 표면 발언("본사 결정 전달")과 회의록이 드러내는 실제(본인이 초안·추진), 그리고 칭찬 시 자기 공으로 돌리는 두 번째 장면을 함께 제시한다. 정답 D는 두 장면과 회의록을 통합해야만 도출되며 어느 한 문장의 인용이 아니다. A는 매니저 발언을 그대로 옮긴 오답, B는 전략적 전환을 '진심 어린 의심'으로 뒤집은 오답, C는 과잉일반화 오답으로 역할이 분명하다. Goffman의 footing 개념 서술도 정확. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 모순 없이 뒷받침한다. hard 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 맞다. 다만 D는 두 발언을 거의 그대로 다시 말한 것이어서 회의록 정보(표면 진술과 실제의 모순)를 보지 않아도 고를 수 있다. 숨은 함의를 추론하는 단계(예: 칭찬받을 공은 챙기고 비판받을 책임은 피하려는 전략)를 정답이 요구하지 않는다. 오답 C는 과잉일반화라서 쉽게 지워지고, B는 동기를 잘못 읽은 것이어서 쉽게 배제된다. 그래서 medium 수준으로 판단한다. B가 '방향을 뒤집은 오답'인지는 다소 느슨하지만 충족으로 본다.

problem.passage:
When a professor's recommendation letter for a student applying to graduate school in philosophy says only that the student "has excellent handwriting and always attended class," readers rarely conclude that the professor admires the student. Philosopher of language Paul Grice argued that such inferences are not accidents of interpretation but follow from a general expectation that conversation is cooperative: listeners assume that speakers are trying to say as much as is needed, no more, and to be truthful, relevant, and clear. Because the letter conspicuously omits any comment on the student's philosophical ability—the very thing a reader would need to know—the reader infers that the writer has nothing favorable to say about it.

Grice called meanings of this kind "implicatures," and he stressed that they differ from what words literally encode. An implicature can be canceled without contradiction: the professor could add, "and, incidentally, she is the most gifted philosopher I have taught," and the earlier inference would simply dissolve. Literal content cannot be withdrawn this way, which, for Grice, showed that much of what speakers communicate arises from shared assumptions about how conversation works rather than from the words themselves.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Grice held that listeners derive much unstated meaning by assuming speakers are cooperating, and that such meaning, unlike literal content, can be retracted.
Grice held that a recommendation letter silent about a student's ability signals the writer's low opinion of that student.
Grice held that nearly all human communication, spoken or not, depends on cooperative assumptions rather than on the meanings of words.
Grice held that implicatures can be canceled because recommendation letters are expected to say no more than is needed.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 지문의 넓은 주장(협력 가정에 따른 함축 추론)과 이를 문자적 의미와 구분하는 핵심 특징(취소 가능성)을 정확한 범위로 함께 담는다.
B(과잉축소): 추천서 사례는 이론을 보여 주는 세부사실 하나일 뿐 전체 요지가 아니다.
C(과잉확장): 지문은 화자가 전달하는 것 중 '상당 부분(much)'을 말할 뿐, 말 이외의 소통까지 포함한 '거의 모든' 소통이 단어 의미와 무관하다고 하지 않는다.
D(범위 혼합): 취소 가능성이라는 일반 원리와 추천서 사례를 잘못된 인과관계로 엮었다. 지문에서 취소 가능성은 함축이 문자적 내용과 다르기 때문이지, 추천서 관행 때문이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn:
A is correct. It captures the passage's broad claim (listeners infer unstated meaning by assuming speakers are cooperating) along with the key feature that sets such meaning apart from literal content: it can be canceled. The scope is just right.
B is too narrow. The recommendation letter is only the example the passage uses to illustrate the theory, not the overall point.
C goes too far. The passage says "much" of what speakers communicate comes from shared assumptions. It never says nearly all communication, including nonspoken communication, works this way rather than through word meaning.
D blends the general principle and the example in the wrong way, creating a false cause. In the passage, implicatures can be canceled because they aren't part of literal content, not because of how recommendation letters are expected to be written.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 1문단(협력 가정→함축 추론)과 2문단(함축의 취소 가능성→문자적 의미와 구분)의 두 단계 논지를 갖고, A가 둘을 정확한 범위로 통합한다. B는 사례 축소, C는 'much'→'nearly all', 'spoken or not'으로 과잉확장, D는 일반 원리와 사례를 거짓 인과로 엮은 함정으로 설계가 명확하다. Grice의 협력 원리·격률·취소 가능성 서술은 사실에 부합하며, 추천서 사례는 Grice 원저의 유명 예시를 재구성한 것으로 저작권 문제는 없다. 두 문단 구조 통합과 'much' vs 'nearly all'의 범위 구분이 전형적 medium보다 추가 사고를 요구한다.

advisory.note: Grice 함축 이론은 사실에 부합한다(대화 격률, 취소 가능성). B는 과잉축소, C는 'nearly all'·'spoken or not'으로 과잉확장, D는 잘못된 인과로 묶은 오답이다. 'much'와 'nearly all'의 범위를 구별해야 하므로 범위 판단이 필요하다. 다만 A의 진술이 길고 지문의 두 문단을 그대로 반영해 비교적 식별하기 쉽다.

problem.passage:
For decades, many anthropologists treated social structures—kinship rules, gender hierarchies, systems of rank—as forces operating largely above individuals, who were seen as simply carrying out roles assigned to them. In her work on practice theory, however, Sherry Ortner argued that everyday actions do more than passively mirror these systems: by repeating, bending, or resisting customs, people continually remake them. On her account, ordinary individuals are ______ both sustaining and altering the structures that shape their lives.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: For decades, many anthropologists treated social structures—kinship rules, gender hierarchies, systems of rank—as forces operating largely above individuals, who were seen as simply carrying out roles assigned to them. In her work on practice theory, however, Sherry Ortner argued that everyday actions do more than passively mirror these systems: by repeating, bending, or resisting customs, people continually remake them. On her account, ordinary individuals are ______ both sustaining and altering the structures that shape their lives.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: incidental to
instrumental in
somewhat peripheral to
indifferent to
problem.explanation:
정답 B. 'however' 앞 문장은 개인이 주어진 역할만 수행한다는 통념이고, 뒤 문장은 사람들이 관습을 반복·변형·저항하며 구조를 계속 '다시 만든다'고 반박한다. 따라서 Ortner의 견해에서 개인은 구조를 유지하고 바꾸는 데 핵심적 역할을 하는 존재, 즉 'instrumental in'이다.
A 'incidental to'(부수적인)는 반박된 통념을 그대로 반영한다.
C 'somewhat peripheral to'(다소 주변적인)는 전환어를 놓쳐 통념과 같은 방향에서 강도만 약하게 만든 것이다.
D 'indifferent to'(무관심한)는 역할의 크기가 아니라 개인의 태도에 관한 말이라 지문의 논점과 무관하다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is B. The sentence before "however" gives the old view: individuals simply carry out roles assigned to them. The sentence after it rejects that view. People repeat, bend, or resist customs, and in doing so they "continually remake" social structures. So in Ortner's account, individuals play a central role in keeping structures going and in changing them. That makes them "instrumental in" doing so.
A ("incidental to") repeats the old view that the passage rejects.
C ("somewhat peripheral to") misses the turn at "however." It points the same way as the old view and just makes it a little weaker.
D ("indifferent to") describes how people feel, not how big a role they play, so it doesn't fit the passage's point.

hardJudge.note: 통념(개인은 수동적 역할 수행자) → however → Ortner 반박(관습을 반복·변형·저항하며 구조를 '다시 만든다')의 역전 구조가 명확하고, 'do more than passively mirror'라는 부정 층위를 재구성해야 B 'instrumental in'에 도달한다. A는 통념 방향, C는 통념 방향의 약화형, D는 태도 어휘로 논점 이탈이라 정답 유일성 확보. 다만 C가 정답 방향의 강도 변형(예: indispensable to)이 아니라 통념 방향의 약화형이어서 confidence_calibration 부담은 낮고, 오답 셋 중 둘이 같은 쪽을 향해 소거가 비교적 쉬운 편(hard 중 하위 수준). Sherry Ortner 실천이론 서술은 사실에 부합하며 원문 인용 흔적 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 맞고 해설도 일관된다. 다만 'however' 뒤의 'continually remake them'이 정답을 거의 그대로 알려 준다. 오답 A·C·D는 모두 '중요하지 않다/관여하지 않는다'는 같은 극성이어서 극성만 판단해도 바로 소거된다. 이중부정, 확신도 조정, 여러 단서 통합 같은 추가 사고가 필요 없어 전형적인 medium 수준의 통념 반전 문항이다. 4번 항목은 C를 A와 같은 방향의 약화형으로 보면 충족된다.

problem.passage:
Graphene, a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice, conducts electricity remarkably well in laboratory samples, but the methods used to make it in large quantities tend to undermine that property. The cheapest approach, chemically peeling apart graphite and then removing the oxygen added during the process, yields large amounts of material, yet the resulting flakes are riddled with holes and leftover oxygen groups that scatter electrons. Materials scientist Priya Raman and her colleagues reasoned that the defects themselves might be repaired after production rather than avoided beforehand. They exposed chemically produced graphene to a brief pulse of intense microwave radiation, which heated the flakes to over 2,000°C in about two seconds. The treatment drove off most of the remaining oxygen and allowed carbon atoms to resettle into an orderly lattice, raising the material's conductivity nearly to that of graphene grown by slower, far more expensive vapor-deposition methods.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

They exposed chemically produced graphene to a brief pulse of intense microwave radiation, which heated the flakes to over 2,000°C in about two seconds. The treatment drove off most of the remaining oxygen and allowed carbon atoms to resettle into an orderly lattice, raising the material's conductivity nearly to that of graphene grown by slower, far more expensive vapor-deposition methods.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Researchers found that flaws introduced by an inexpensive way of making graphene could be largely corrected afterward, bringing its electrical performance close to that of costlier graphene.
Researchers found that an inexpensive way of making graphene could be modified to prevent flaws from forming, making costlier production methods unnecessary for most uses.
Researchers found that heating graphene to extreme temperatures removes oxygen groups, although the process leaves its carbon lattice too disordered to conduct electricity well.
Researchers found that graphene made by vapor deposition conducts electricity better than any other form of carbon, which explains why it remains the most widely used type.
problem.explanation: 지문은 값싼 화학적 그래핀 생산법이 결함을 남기지만, Raman 연구팀이 마이크로파 처리로 생산 후 결함을 복구해 고가 방식에 가까운 전도도를 얻었다고 설명하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 결함을 '사전에 막는다'고 하지만 지문은 미리 피하는 대신 나중에 고친다고 명시하며, 고가 방식이 불필요하다는 주장도 없다. C는 산소 제거는 맞지만 탄소 원자가 질서 있는 격자로 재배열되어 전도도가 올랐다는 내용과 반대된다. D는 기상 증착 그래핀을 비교 기준으로만 언급한 점을 과장했고, 가장 널리 쓰인다는 정보도 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text explains that cheap chemical production leaves graphene full of defects, and that Raman's team used a microwave pulse to repair those defects after production, bringing conductivity close to that of expensive vapor-grown graphene, so A is correct. B says the flaws are prevented from forming, but the text specifically says the defects were repaired afterward instead of avoided, and it never claims that costlier methods become unnecessary. C is right that oxygen is removed, but it contradicts the text, which says the carbon atoms resettled into an orderly lattice and conductivity increased. D takes vapor-deposited graphene, which the text mentions only as a point of comparison, and makes it the focus; the text also never says it is the most widely used type.

hardJudge.note: A correctly synthesizes the passage (cheap method's defects repaired post-production, conductivity approaching costly vapor-deposition graphene). B contradicts 'repaired after production rather than avoided beforehand'; C contradicts the orderly lattice/increased conductivity; D inflates a comparison reference and adds unsupported 'most widely used' claim. Korean and English explanations align with the key and each other. Fictional researcher, original passage; no copyright concern. Two strong partial-truth distractors (B, C) plus plausible D meet medium criteria.

advisory.note: B는 '나중에 고친다'와 '미리 막는다'를 구분해야 배제되는 그럴듯한 오답이고, C는 산소 제거 부분이 맞아 부분 근거를 가진다. D는 비교적 쉽게 배제되지만 말은 된다. 난이도는 medium에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Perovskite solar cells have attracted attention because they can be made cheaply from solutions rather than from the ultrapure silicon wafers that conventional panels require. That low-temperature processing, however, leaves the crystals riddled with defects, such as missing ions and misaligned grain boundaries. Researchers long assumed these flaws would trap electrons and sharply reduce efficiency, as similar defects do in silicon. Yet perovskite cells routinely convert more than 25 percent of sunlight into electricity. Studies by materials physicists suggest an explanation: most of the common defects in perovskites create energy states that lie very close to the edges of the material's energy bands rather than deep within the gap between them. Electrons that fall into such shallow states can easily escape again, so the defects do little to hinder the flow of current. The material, in other words, appears to be unusually tolerant of its own imperfections.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Yet perovskite cells routinely convert more than 25 percent of sunlight into electricity. Electrons that fall into such shallow states can easily escape again, so the defects do little to hinder the flow of current. problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Perovskite solar cells reach high efficiency because researchers have learned to remove nearly all the defects that solution processing creates.
Perovskite solar cells perform well despite their many crystal defects because those defects mostly produce energy states that barely impede electrons.
Perovskite solar cells are more efficient than silicon panels because perovskite defects free trapped electrons that silicon would hold.
Perovskite solar cells are cheaper to make than silicon panels because they can be processed at low temperatures from solutions.
problem.explanation: 지문은 페로브스카이트 결정에 결함이 많은데도 효율이 높은 이유가 결함이 얕은 에너지 준위를 만들어 전자 흐름을 거의 방해하지 않기 때문이라고 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 결함이 제거되었다고 하지만, 지문에서는 결함이 그대로 남아 있어도 영향이 적다고 한다. C는 실리콘과 비교해 더 효율적이라고 주장하고 결함이 전자를 풀어 준다고 하는데, 둘 다 지문에 없는 내용이다. D는 지문 앞부분의 세부 내용일 뿐이고 글의 핵심인 결함 허용성을 담지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: B is correct because the text explains that perovskite cells stay efficient despite having many defects. Most of those defects create shallow energy states that electrons can easily escape. A is wrong because the text says the defects remain, not that they are removed. C makes two claims the text doesn't support: that perovskites are more efficient than silicon, and that the defects actively release electrons. D repeats a detail from the opening but misses the text's central point, which is that the material tolerates its defects.

quality.seed: physical science — Perovskite crystal lattice defects affecting solar cell efficiency

hardJudge.note: 지문 내용(저온 용액 공정, 결함, 25% 이상 효율, 얕은 결함 준위에 의한 결함 허용성)은 실제 페로브스카이트 연구와 부합하며 독창적 서술로 보임. B가 '결함에도 불구하고 + 얕은 준위 메커니즘'을 정확히 요약. A는 지문과 모순, C는 지문에 없는 실리콘 대비 효율 비교와 메커니즘 왜곡, D는 도입부 세부 사항으로 주제가 아님. D와 A가 부분적 근거를 가져 비교 필요, C도 그럴듯함. 해설 한·영 모두 정답과 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움, 한글 혼입 없음. medium 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 지문의 결함 허용성 논지와 일치한다. A·C는 일부 맞는 근거(높은 효율, 전자 탈출)를 왜곡한 매력적 오답이고, D는 실제 세부 사항이지만 핵심 논지가 아니다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
When a liquid is blasted with intense sound waves, tiny gas bubbles can form, swell, and then collapse violently, a process called acoustic cavitation. In 1990, physicist Felipe Gaitan showed that a single bubble trapped in a flask of water by a standing sound wave could be made to collapse over and over, giving off a faint flash of blue-white light with each cycle. This effect, called sonoluminescence, had first been noticed decades earlier in clouds of bubbles, but isolating one bubble let researchers time the flashes precisely. They found that each flash lasts less than a billionth of a second, far shorter than many had expected. Yet even with this precision, researchers still disagree about what produces the light. Some argue that the collapsing bubble heats its gas enough to form a glowing plasma, while others propose that the light comes from chemical reactions or from electric charges separating at the bubble wall, and no single model yet accounts for all the measurements.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

This effect, called sonoluminescence, had first been noticed decades earlier in clouds of bubbles, but isolating one bubble let researchers time the flashes precisely. They found that each flash lasts less than a billionth of a second, far shorter than many had expected. Yet even with this precision, researchers still disagree about what produces the light. Some argue that the collapsing bubble heats its gas enough to form a glowing plasma, while others propose that the light comes from chemical reactions or from electric charges separating at the bubble wall, and no single model yet accounts for all the measurements.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Trapping a single bubble showed that sonoluminescence flashes last far longer than earlier studies of bubble clouds had suggested.
Gaitan's single-bubble experiment confirmed that sonoluminescence results from gas heated into a glowing plasma during collapse.
Researchers abandoned the study of bubble clouds after Gaitan found that a single bubble produces brighter and more regular flashes.
Although isolating one bubble let researchers measure sonoluminescence precisely, the cause of its light remains unsettled.
problem.explanation: 지문은 단일 기포 실험으로 섬광을 정밀하게 측정할 수 있게 되었지만, 빛의 원인에 대해서는 여전히 합의가 없다는 점을 중심으로 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 섬광 시간을 언급하지만, 섬광은 예상보다 '짧았다'고 했으므로 방향이 반대다. B는 플라스마 가설을 언급하지만, 그것은 여러 가설 중 하나일 뿐 실험으로 확인된 것이 아니다. C는 기포 구름 연구를 포기했다거나 더 밝았다는 내용을 담고 있는데, 이는 지문에 나오지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text's focus is that a single-bubble setup made precise measurement of the flashes possible, but scientists still disagree about what causes the light, so D is correct. A mentions flash duration, but the text says the flashes were shorter than expected, not longer. B names the plasma idea, but the text presents it as only one of several competing explanations, not a confirmed one. C claims that researchers abandoned bubble-cloud studies and that the flashes were brighter, and the text says neither.

quality.seed: physical science — Sonoluminescence bubble collapse creating light from acoustic cavitation

hardJudge.note: D는 지문 전체 구조(정밀 측정 가능 → 그러나 원인 미합의)를 정확히 요약. A는 '짧다'를 '길다'로 뒤집은 세부 왜곡, B는 여러 가설 중 하나를 확정된 결론으로 과장, C는 지문에 없는 내용(기포 구름 연구 포기, 더 밝은 섬광). 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 서술 정확. Gaitan 1990 단일 기포 소노루미네선스, 1ns 미만 섬광, 플라스마/화학반응/전하분리 가설 등 사실 관계 무리 없음. 오답 A·B가 부분적 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하므로 medium 적합.

problem.passage:
Catalytic converters reduce harmful car exhaust by passing it over thin coatings of metals such as palladium. Molecules of carbon monoxide and unburned hydrocarbons stick briefly to the palladium surface, where they react with oxygen to form less harmful carbon dioxide and water. For decades, engineers assumed that the more palladium a converter contained, the cleaner its output would be. However, chemist Lena Ortiz and her colleagues found that this assumption breaks down when the engine is cold. In their tests, converters with heavy palladium loading performed no better during the first minutes after startup than converters with far less metal, because at low temperatures carbon monoxide molecules crowd the surface so densely that oxygen cannot reach the reactive sites. Ortiz's team concluded that how the palladium is arranged, such as spreading it into tiny, well-separated clusters, matters more for cold-start emissions than how much of it is used.

According to the text, what did Ortiz's team identify as the reason that extra palladium fails to lower emissions right after an engine is started?

problem.question: According to the text, what did Ortiz's team identify as the reason that extra palladium fails to lower emissions right after an engine is started?
options: Palladium does not react with oxygen until the converter has reached the temperature of a fully warmed engine.
One exhaust gas covers the metal so completely that a needed reactant is kept from the sites where reactions take place.
Heavy loading makes the palladium clump into large clusters that trap unburned hydrocarbons inside the converter.
Carbon dioxide and water produced in the first minutes build up on the metal and block further reactions.
problem.explanation: 지문은 낮은 온도에서 일산화탄소 분자가 표면을 빽빽하게 덮어 산소가 반응 자리에 닿지 못한다고 설명하므로, 이를 바꿔 말한 B가 정답이다. A는 온도가 중요하다는 점은 맞지만, 원인을 일산화탄소의 표면 점유가 아니라 팔라듐 자체가 반응하지 않는 것으로 잘못 설명한다. C는 팔라듐 배열(클러스터)이라는 지문 요소를 쓰지만, 클러스터가 탄화수소를 가둔다는 내용은 지문에 없다. D는 표면이 막힌다는 생각은 맞지만, 막는 물질을 생성물(이산화탄소와 물)로 바꿔 놓았다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says that at low temperatures, carbon monoxide molecules crowd the palladium surface so densely that oxygen can't reach the reactive sites, so B, which restates this, is correct. A is right that temperature matters, but it blames the palladium itself for not reacting instead of carbon monoxide covering the surface. C uses the text's idea of clusters, but the text never says clusters trap hydrocarbons. D gets the idea of a blocked surface right but swaps in the wrong blocker: the products, carbon dioxide and water, rather than carbon monoxide.

problem.passage:
Liquid crystals occupy an unusual middle ground between ordinary liquids and solids: their rod-shaped molecules flow freely, yet they tend to point in roughly the same direction. Display engineers exploit this partial order, because an electric field can rotate the aligned molecules and thereby change how much light passes through each pixel. That usefulness, however, depends on the material staying in its ordered "nematic" phase. If a screen warms past a threshold known as the clearing point, the molecules abruptly lose their shared orientation and the material becomes an ordinary, disordered liquid that no longer responds to the field in a controllable way. For this reason, chemists designing display materials rarely rely on a single compound. Instead, they blend several liquid crystals whose individual phase ranges are narrow, producing mixtures that remain nematic from well below freezing to temperatures far above those found in a parked car on a summer day.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

That usefulness, however, depends on the material staying in its ordered "nematic" phase. problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Because an electric field can rotate liquid crystal molecules, display engineers can control how much light passes through each pixel regardless of temperature.
Because individual liquid crystal compounds lose their order at the clearing point, chemists have largely abandoned them in favor of ordinary liquids for display screens.
Because liquid crystals flow like liquids but align like solids, they are more difficult to manufacture than other materials used in electronics.
Because liquid crystals are useful in displays only while they keep their ordered phase, chemists combine several compounds to keep that phase stable across a wide temperature range.
problem.explanation: 지문은 액정이 정렬된 네마틱 상태일 때만 디스플레이에 유용하고, 투명점을 넘으면 그 질서를 잃는다고 설명한 뒤, 그래서 화학자들이 여러 화합물을 섞어 넓은 온도 범위에서 그 상태를 유지한다고 결론짓는다. 이 두 부분을 연결한 D가 정답이다. A는 전기장 제어라는 세부는 맞지만 '온도와 무관하게'라는 표현이 지문의 핵심인 온도 한계와 정면으로 모순된다. B는 투명점은 언급하지만 화학자들은 액정을 버린 것이 아니라 혼합해 사용하므로 틀리다. C는 제조의 어려움을 말하지만 지문에는 그런 비교가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text explains that liquid crystals are useful in displays only while they stay in the ordered nematic phase, which they lose above the clearing point. It then concludes that chemists blend several compounds so the mixture stays nematic over a wide temperature range. D connects these two ideas, so it is the correct answer. A uses the accurate detail about electric fields, but "regardless of temperature" contradicts the text's central point about temperature limits. B mentions the clearing point, but chemists don't abandon liquid crystals; they blend them. C claims liquid crystals are harder to manufacture, and the text never makes that comparison.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 지문 전체를 정확히 요약함. A·B는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야 배제되고, C는 그럴듯하지만 근거가 없음. 다만 정답만 유일하게 두 부분을 모두 담은 긴 선택지라 길이로 추측할 위험이 약간 있음. 중간 난이도로 무난함.

problem.passage:
When titanium dioxide absorbs ultraviolet light, electrons in the material are boosted to a higher energy level, leaving behind positively charged "holes." At the surface, these holes and electrons react with water and oxygen to form highly reactive molecules that break down grime, which is why TiO2 coatings have been marketed as "self-cleaning" for windows and building facades. __Yet most excited electrons recombine with their holes within billionths of a second, releasing their energy as heat before they ever reach the surface.__ For this reason, chemists studying the material have focused less on increasing how much light TiO2 absorbs and more on keeping charges separated, for instance by adding trace amounts of metals such as platinum that pull electrons away from holes.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: When titanium dioxide absorbs ultraviolet light, electrons in the material are boosted to a higher energy level, leaving behind positively charged "holes." At the surface, these holes and electrons react with water and oxygen to form highly reactive molecules that break down grime, which is why TiO2 coatings have been marketed as "self-cleaning" for windows and building facades. __Yet most excited electrons recombine with their holes within billionths of a second, releasing their energy as heat before they ever reach the surface.__ For this reason, chemists studying the material have focused less on increasing how much light TiO2 absorbs and more on keeping charges separated, for instance by adding trace amounts of metals such as platinum that pull electrons away from holes.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why titanium dioxide must absorb ultraviolet rather than visible light in order to break down grime.
It presents evidence that the self-cleaning claims made for titanium dioxide coatings have been greatly exaggerated.
It describes a laboratory result that led chemists to replace titanium dioxide with platinum in surface coatings.
It identifies a limitation of the process described earlier that accounts for the research direction mentioned afterward.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞서 설명한 광촉매 과정에서 들뜬 전자 대부분이 표면에 닿기 전에 재결합한다는 한계를 제시하고, 마지막 문장은 "For this reason"으로 이 한계 때문에 연구가 전하 분리 유지에 집중한다고 이어 간다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 자외선과 가시광선을 비교하지만 지문에는 그런 비교가 없다. B는 한계를 언급한다는 점은 맞지만, 지문은 자가 세정 주장이 과장되었다고 판단하지 않는다. C는 백금을 언급하지만, 백금은 TiO2를 대체하는 것이 아니라 소량 첨가될 뿐이다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence points out a limitation of the photocatalytic process described earlier: most excited electrons recombine before they reach the surface. The final sentence begins with "For this reason," showing that this limitation explains why research has shifted toward keeping charges separated, so D is correct. A brings in a comparison between ultraviolet and visible light, but the text never makes that comparison. B is right that the sentence notes a drawback, but the text never says the self-cleaning claims are exaggerated. C mentions platinum, but platinum is added in trace amounts to TiO2; it doesn't replace it.

problem.passage:
Crystalline silicon dominates the solar-panel market, yet its physics imposes a firm ceiling on performance. Silicon's band gap—the minimum energy an electron must absorb to break free and carry current—is about 1.1 electron volts. Photons carrying less energy than this pass through the material without freeing electrons at all. __Photons carrying more energy, such as those in blue light, do free electrons, but any energy beyond the band gap is quickly shed as heat rather than converted to electricity.__ Because sunlight contains a broad mix of photon energies, these two losses together mean that even a flawless single-junction silicon cell cannot convert much more than about 30 percent of incoming sunlight into electrical power.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Crystalline silicon dominates the solar-panel market, yet its physics imposes a firm ceiling on performance. Silicon's band gap—the minimum energy an electron must absorb to break free and carry current—is about 1.1 electron volts. Photons carrying less energy than this pass through the material without freeing electrons at all. __Photons carrying more energy, such as those in blue light, do free electrons, but any energy beyond the band gap is quickly shed as heat rather than converted to electricity.__ Because sunlight contains a broad mix of photon energies, these two losses together mean that even a flawless single-junction silicon cell cannot convert much more than about 30 percent of incoming sunlight into electrical power.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why high-energy photons are more useful to silicon cells than low-energy photons, supporting the claim that blue light drives most electricity production.
It identifies a second way that energy goes unused in a silicon cell, which combines with the previously described loss to account for the efficiency limit stated afterward.
It describes a manufacturing flaw that causes silicon cells to overheat, which the text then argues could be corrected to exceed the efficiency limit.
It defines the band gap of silicon in terms of photon energy, providing the measurement that the text uses to compare silicon with other materials.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 저에너지 광자가 그냥 통과하는 손실에 이어, 고에너지 광자의 초과 에너지가 열로 사라지는 두 번째 손실을 제시하고, 마지막 문장은 '이 두 손실'이 약 30% 한계를 만든다고 말하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 고에너지 광자가 전자를 방출한다는 점은 맞지만, 초과 에너지가 낭비된다는 핵심을 놓쳤고 청색광이 대부분의 전력을 생산한다는 주장도 지문에 없다. C는 열 발생을 언급한 점은 맞지만, 이는 제조 결함이 아니라 '결함 없는' 전지에도 적용되는 물리적 한계이다. D의 밴드갭 정의는 밑줄 문장이 아니라 앞 문장에 나오며, 다른 소재와의 비교도 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence follows the loss from low-energy photons passing straight through and adds a second loss: the extra energy of high-energy photons is lost as heat. The final sentence then says "these two losses together" create the roughly 30 percent limit, so B is correct. A is right that high-energy photons free electrons, but it misses the main point that their extra energy is wasted, and the text never says blue light produces most of the electricity. C is right to mention heat, but the heat loss is not a manufacturing flaw; it applies even to a "flawless" cell. D is wrong because the band gap is defined in the earlier sentence, not the underlined one, and the text never compares silicon with other materials.

problem.passage:
Chemiluminescence occurs when a chemical reaction releases energy as visible light rather than mainly as heat. In the familiar glow stick, for example, hydrogen peroxide oxidizes a compound called an oxalate ester, producing a high-energy intermediate that passes its energy to a dye molecule; the dye then emits light as it returns to a lower energy state. Many people assume that the glow simply fades because the chemicals inside are used up. __Yet a glow stick placed in a freezer will dim noticeably within minutes and then brighten again once it is warmed, even though no fresh reactants have been added.__ This behavior indicates that temperature controls how quickly the oxidation proceeds, and thus how much light is emitted per second, independent of how much fuel remains.

problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and describes an observation (a cooled glow stick dims, then brightens when warmed) that conflicts with the common belief that the glow fades only because reactants run out; the next sentence draws the conclusion that temperature controls the reaction rate. So A is correct. B is wrong because the observation contradicts, not confirms, that belief. C is wrong because the energy transfer to the dye is explained in an earlier sentence, not by the underlined one. D is wrong because the text's first sentence says chemiluminescence releases energy as light rather than mainly as heat.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 타당: 'Yet'으로 통념(반응물 소진)에 반하는 관찰을 제시하고 다음 문장의 결론(온도가 반응 속도 제어)으로 연결됨. B는 방향 반대, C는 앞 문장의 내용, D는 첫 문장과 모순. 과학적 사실(글로우스틱 냉각 시 어두워지고 데우면 다시 밝아짐, 과산화수소–옥살레이트 에스터 반응)도 정확. 한·영 해설 일치, 선택지 참조 정확. 오답 B·C가 지문의 실제 내용을 담고 있어 비교가 필요하므로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 맞다. 다만 오답이 약하다. B는 'Yet'의 방향과 정반대이고, C는 앞 문장의 내용이며, D는 첫 문장과 바로 모순된다. 세 오답 모두 한 번만 대조해도 걸러지고, 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가진 오답이 없어 medium 기준(비교해야 배제되는 오답 2개 이상)에 못 미친다. 게다가 '통념에 도전하고 결론을 이끈다'는 표현을 가진 선택지가 A뿐이라 훑어 읽어도 맞힐 수 있다.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: When two optical fibers are spliced together, even a microscopic air gap between their polished ends can scatter or reflect part of the signal. To reduce this loss, technicians often fill the junction with an index-matching gel, a transparent compound whose refractive index nearly equals that of the fibers' glass core______ the light no longer meets an abrupt change in medium at the joint, very little of it is reflected backward.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , because
because
; because
because,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격어구(an index-matching gel, a transparent compound...)로 끝나는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤는 'because ~ at the joint'라는 종속절 뒤에 'very little of it is reflected backward'라는 주절이 오는 또 하나의 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 연결하려면 세미콜론이 필요하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 되고, because절이 앞 절을 수식하는 것처럼 보이지만 실제로는 뒤 주절에 속한다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 이어 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 because와 그 주어 사이에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣었고, 여전히 두 독립절 사이에 경계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank is an independent clause that ends with a long appositive (an index-matching gel, a transparent compound...). After the blank comes a second independent clause: the dependent clause "because ... at the joint" introduces the main clause "very little of it is reflected backward." Two independent clauses need a semicolon between them, so C is correct. A uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice, and it misleadingly attaches the because-clause to the first sentence when it actually belongs to the main clause after it. B uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D puts an unnecessary comma between "because" and its subject and still leaves no boundary between the two clauses.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 'technicians often fill ... glass core'는 독립절, 빈칸 뒤는 'because ... at the joint'(종속절) + 'very little of it is reflected backward'(주절)로 구성된 독립절. 세미콜론으로 경계를 만드는 C만 적법. A는 because절이 앞 절에 붙는 것처럼 보이며 결국 ', very little...'에서 comma splice 발생; B는 경계 없음; D는 because 뒤 불필요한 쉼표. 해설(한/영) 모두 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치. 광섬유 인덱스 매칭 젤 내용도 사실에 부합. 난이도: because절의 소속(앞 절 vs 뒤 주절)을 파악한 뒤 경계 규칙을 적용하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, A/B가 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯하여 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 세미콜론 뒤에 because로 시작하는 종속절이 오고, 그 뒤에 주절이 이어지는 구조라서 두 단계로 분석해야 합니다. 빈칸 앞 독립절 뒤에 because가 오면 이유를 덧붙이는 것처럼 읽히기 때문에, 훑어 읽으면 A나 B를 고르기 쉽습니다. 오답 선택지들은 모두 그럴듯해서 medium 난이도에 적합합니다. 사실 관계(굴절률 정합 겔이 반사를 줄인다는 내용)도 정확합니다.

problem.stimulus: Engineers who design vibration-resistant panels for aircraft cabins often turn to polymer composites, materials that behave partly like elastic solids and partly like viscous fluids. problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , the
the
, while, the
; meanwhile, the
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "the stiff carbon fibers ... springs back"은 주절이고, 빈칸 뒤의 "the long, tangled polymer chains ... slide past one another"도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 이으려면 세미콜론이 필요하며, 접속부사 "meanwhile" 뒤에 쉼표를 둔 D가 올바르다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이은 쉼표 이음 오류이다. B는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. C는 "while"로 두 절을 연결하려는 시도 자체는 타당하지만, 종속접속사 "while"과 그 절의 주어 사이에 쉼표를 넣으면 안 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank, "the stiff carbon fibers ... springs back," form a main clause, and the words after it, "the long, tangled polymer chains ... slide past one another," form another independent clause with its own subject and verb. To join two independent clauses, you need a semicolon, so D is correct: it uses a semicolon followed by the transition "meanwhile" and a comma. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence. C has the right idea in linking the clauses with "while," but a comma shouldn't separate the subordinating conjunction "while" from the subject of its clause.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞("the stiff carbon fibers ... store ... and release it as the panel springs back")과 뒤("the long, tangled polymer chains ... slide past one another")가 모두 독립절임을 직접 확인. D(세미콜론 + meanwhile + 쉼표)가 유일하게 올바름. A는 쉼표 이음, B는 무종지문, C는 "while" 뒤 불필요한 쉼표로 오류. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 오답 근거를 정확히 설명하고 선택지 글자 참조 일치. C가 접속사 자체는 타당해 비교 판단이 필요하고, A/B는 전형적 오답으로 기능하여 medium 난이도에 부합. 사소하게 선택지 B 앞 공백이 2칸이나 채점에 영향 없음. 내용(점탄성 복합재의 에너지 저장·열 변환)은 사실에 부합하며 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 두 독립절 사이의 경계를 묻는 문항이다. 빈칸 앞 절이 길고 'as the panel springs back'이라는 종속절로 끝나기 때문에 훑어 읽으면 절의 경계를 잘못 볼 수 있다. 오답 C는 'while'로 연결하는 방향 자체는 맞아 보여 그럴듯하므로 중간 난이도에 맞다. 다만 '세미콜론이 필요하다'는 표현은 일반 원칙으로 보면 다소 과장되어 있다(마침표나 '쉼표+등위접속사'도 가능). 그러나 주어진 선택지 안에서는 문제가 없다.

problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , yet
yet
, which
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 'Supercritical carbon dioxide ... can seep ... as a vapor'는 긴 동격구가 끼어 있지만 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤의 'it can dissolve caffeine ...'도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 쉼표와 등위접속사로 이어야 하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 알맞은 접속사가 있지만 그 앞에 쉼표가 없어 표준 규칙에 맞지 않는 run-on 문장이 된다. C는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. D의 'which'는 관계절을 만들지만, 뒤에 이미 주어 'it'과 완전한 절이 있어 문법적으로 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank, "Supercritical carbon dioxide ... can seep ... as a vapor," is a complete independent clause even though a long appositive interrupts it. The text after the blank, "it can dissolve caffeine ...," is also an independent clause. Two independent clauses can be joined with a comma plus a coordinating conjunction, so A is correct. B has a suitable conjunction but leaves out the comma before it, which doesn't follow standard conventions. C uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. D's "which" starts a relative clause, but the clause after it already has its own subject, "it," and is complete, so the sentence becomes ungrammatical.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격구가 삽입된 독립절, 뒤도 독립절(it can dissolve...)이므로 쉼표+등위접속사 ', yet'(A)가 정답임을 직접 확인. B(쉼표 누락), C(comma splice), D(', which' 뒤에 완전한 절)는 모두 배제 가능. 긴 삽입구로 절 경계를 파악한 뒤 규칙을 적용해야 하는 2단계 판단으로 medium에 적합. 초임계 CO2 조건(31°C, ~73 atm)과 디카페인 공정 사용은 사실에 부합. 독창적 지문으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 독립절 두 개를 ', yet'으로 잇는 구조이고 정답 A가 맞다. 긴 동격구가 끼어 있어 앞부분이 독립절인지 판단하기 어렵게 만들고, B(쉼표 누락)와 D(which)가 그럴듯한 오답이라 medium 난이도에 맞다. 사실관계: 임계점 31°C·약 73 atm은 정확하다. 다만 'it has largely replaced'(CO2가 유기용매를 대부분 대체했다)는 다소 과장일 수 있다. 메틸렌 클로라이드와 에틸 아세테이트 공정이 지금도 널리 쓰이기 때문이다. 다만 문항의 정답 판단에는 영향이 없다.

; in other words,

problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("As the ions depart, cobalt atoms in the cathode lose electrons") and the text after it ("the cathode undergoes oxidation...") are both independent clauses. That means you need a semicolon between them, plus a comma after the transitional phrase "in other words," so B is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C has the right semicolon but leaves out the comma after the transitional phrase. D puts no boundary punctuation between the clauses at all, so it creates a run-on sentence.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤 모두 독립절("cobalt atoms ... lose electrons" / "the cathode undergoes oxidation ...")이므로 세미콜론 + 접속부사구 뒤 쉼표인 B가 정답. advisory.note: 충전 시 양극 산화, 음극 환원이라는 설명은 과학적으로 맞다. 선택지는 세미콜론과 접속부사 문제의 표준 구성이다. A와 C는 부분적으로 맞는 함정이어서 medium 난이도에 적합하다. D는 쉬운 오답이다.

, and it behaves

problem.explanation: 주어 "Mercury" 뒤에 쉼표로 시작한 비필수 관계절(whose ... glass)이 삽입되어 있으므로, 이 절은 쉼표로 닫힌 뒤 바로 본동사 "behaves"가 와야 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론 앞부분이 "Mercury"에 동사가 없는 불완전한 절이라 틀렸다. B는 ", and"가 동사 없는 주어를 새 절과 연결하므로 문장이 완성되지 않는다. C는 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 앞의 쉼표와 짝이 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject "Mercury" is interrupted by a nonessential relative clause (whose ... glass) that opens with a comma, so that clause has to be closed with a comma before the main verb "behaves." That's why D is correct. A is wrong because the part before the semicolon isn't a complete clause: "Mercury" never gets a verb. B uses ", and" to attach a new clause to a subject that still has no verb, so the sentence isn't complete. C leaves out the closing comma, so the comma that opens the interrupting clause has no match.

For example,
Similarly,
Even so,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 첨가제가 오일이 묽어지는 현상을 상당 부분 상쇄한다고 말하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그럼에도 오일이 여전히 확연히 묽어진다고 말하므로 양보 후 반전 관계이며 D가 정답이다. A는 첨가제의 효과에서 결과가 나온다는 뜻이 되지만, 뒤 문장은 첨가제 효과의 결과가 아니라 그 한계를 말한다. B는 10W-30이 멀티그레이드 오일의 한 사례라서 그럴듯하지만, 뒤 문장은 앞의 주장을 예시하는 것이 아니라 오히려 제한한다. C는 두 문장이 유사한 내용을 나열하는 것이 아니므로 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence says the additives offset much of the oil's thinning, and the next sentence says the oil still becomes noticeably thinner anyway. That is a concession followed by a contrast, so D is correct. A would make the continued thinning a consequence of the additives, but the sentence actually describes their limit, not their result. B looks tempting because 10W-30 is one kind of multigrade oil, but the sentence qualifies the earlier claim instead of illustrating it. C doesn't work because the two sentences don't present parallel or similar ideas.

options: produce
producing
produces
having produced
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'This displacement'이며, 'of charges within the crystal's lattice'와 'first documented by the brothers...' 수식어구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있다. 문장에는 아직 정동사가 없으므로 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 와야 하고, 따라서 C 'produces'가 정답이다. A is a finite verb, but it is plural, so it wrongly agrees with nearby plural nouns like "charges" or "brothers." B and D are participle forms, which would leave the sentence without a main verb, making it incomplete.

problem.passage:

The thermal anisotropy of these two layered materials, whose in-plane conductivities can exceed their cross-plane values by a factor of more than fifty, ______ them attractive as heat spreaders that pull warmth sideways away from hot spots in microchips. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Like graphite, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) consists of stacked atomic sheets held together only by weak van der Waals forces, so heat travels far more easily within each sheet than from one sheet to the next. The thermal anisotropy of these two layered materials, whose in-plane conductivities can exceed their cross-plane values by a factor of more than fifty, ______ them attractive as heat spreaders that pull warmth sideways away from hot spots in microchips. Unlike graphite, however, hBN is an electrical insulator, allowing it to sit directly against circuitry.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: make
makes
making
to make
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "anisotropy"이고, "of these two layered materials"와 "whose ... fifty" 관계절은 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 문장에는 단수 정동사가 필요하므로 B "makes"가 정답이다. A "make"는 정동사이기는 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사(materials, values)에 맞춘 복수형이라 단수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C "making"과 D "to make"는 정동사가 아니어서 주어에 맞는 본동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "anisotropy." The phrase "of these two layered materials" and the relative clause "whose ... fifty" only modify it. The sentence therefore needs a singular finite verb, so B, "makes," is correct. A, "make," is a finite verb, but it is plural, matching nearby plural nouns like "materials" and "values" rather than the real subject. C, "making," and D, "to make," are not finite verbs, so with either one the subject would have no main verb and the sentence would be incomplete.

problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

problem.explanation: 두 번째 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'Raman spectroscopy'이고, 콤마 사이의 동격구는 수식어일 뿐이므로 빈칸에는 단수형 정동사가 와야 한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'peaks'나 'shifts'에 맞춘 복수형이라 단수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. B는 분사이고 C는 완료 분사여서, 둘 다 문장에 필요한 정동사를 제공하지 못해 불완전한 문장이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of the second sentence is the singular noun "Raman spectroscopy." The phrase between the commas is just a modifier, so the blank needs a singular finite verb, which makes D correct. A is a finite verb, but it is plural, matching the nearby nouns "peaks" or "shifts" instead of the actual singular subject. B is a participle and C is a perfect participle. Neither gives the sentence the main verb it needs, so both leave it incomplete.

problem.passage:

When engineers twist a nickel-titanium wire into a new shape and then warm it slightly, its crystal structure shifts back to its original arrangement, and the wire ______ its former shape. problem.stimulus: Most metals bent past a certain point stay bent, but shape memory alloys such as nickel-titanium behave differently. When engineers twist a nickel-titanium wire into a new shape and then warm it slightly, its crystal structure shifts back to its original arrangement, and the wire ______ its former shape. Researchers are now testing these alloys in stents that can be compressed for insertion into a blood vessel and then expand on their own once they reach body temperature.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: abandons
regains
imitates
preserves
problem.explanation: 지문은 합금 와이어가 새 모양으로 변형된 뒤 가열되면 결정 구조가 원래 배열로 '돌아간다'고 설명하므로, 잃었던 이전 모양을 '되찾는다'는 B가 정답이다. A는 모양이 바뀐다는 점은 맞지만 원래 모양을 '버린다'는 뜻이라 방향이 정반대다. C는 원래 모양과 비슷해진다는 점은 맞지만 '흉내 낸다'는 말은 실제로 같은 구조로 돌아가는 현상을 정확히 담지 못한다. D는 원래 모양과 관련이 있지만 '유지한다'는 뜻이어서, 와이어가 이미 변형되어 그 모양을 잃었다는 사실과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the wire is twisted into a new shape and then, when warmed, its crystal structure shifts back to the original arrangement, so the wire gets back a shape it had lost. That makes B the right answer. A fits the idea that the shape changes, but "abandons" means giving up the former shape, which is the opposite of what happens. C captures the resemblance to the original shape, but "imitates" suggests only copying it, not truly returning to the same structure. D is tied to the original shape, but "preserves" means keeping it, and the wire had already been deformed and lost that shape.

hardJudge.note: "shifts back to its original arrangement"이 단서이며 "former shape"와 결합해 regains가 유일하게 성립. preserves(원래 모양 관련, 그러나 이미 변형됨)와 imitates(유사성)는 부분적 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하고, abandons는 방향 반대로 그럴듯한 오답. 니티놀 형상기억·스텐트 설명도 사실에 부합. 해설 한·영 일치, 글자 참조 정확.

advisory.note: "shifts back to its original arrangement"와 "former shape"가 바로 regains를 가리켜 한 단계 판단으로 풀린다. abandons는 의미가 정반대라 쉽게 배제되고, preserves도 '변형된 뒤'라는 맥락을 보면 금방 탈락한다. imitates만 어느 정도 매력이 있어, 오답 중 최소 2개가 부분적 근거를 가져야 한다는 medium 기준에 못 미친다.
