problem.stimulus: In the late nineteenth century, physicists observed that certain metals release electrons when struck by ultraviolet light. Classical wave theory predicted that making the light brighter should give each ejected electron more energy. Experiments, however, showed that increasing the light's intensity merely produced more electrons, while their maximum energy remained ______; only raising the light's frequency made the electrons emerge faster.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: negligible
unpredictable
diminished
unchanged
problem.explanation: 지문은 빛의 세기를 높이면 전자의 '수'만 늘고, 최대 에너지는 진동수를 높일 때만 증가했다고 대조한다. 따라서 세기 변화에 대해 에너지가 '변하지 않았다'는 D가 정확하다. A는 에너지가 무시할 만큼 작다는 뜻으로, 변화 여부가 아닌 크기를 말하므로 대조 논리와 맞지 않는다. B는 예측 불가능하다는 뜻이지만 지문은 일관된 실험 결과를 제시한다. C는 에너지가 줄었다는 뜻인데, 지문은 감소가 아니라 세기와 무관함을 말한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text contrasts two results: raising intensity only increased the number of electrons, and only raising frequency made them faster. So with greater intensity, the electrons' maximum energy stayed the same, which makes D precise. A describes the energy as tiny, but the point is whether it changed, not how big it was. B says the energy was unpredictable, but the text describes a consistent experimental pattern. C says the energy decreased, but the text shows the energy was unaffected by intensity, not lowered.

hardJudge.note: "merely produced more electrons, while ... remained ___; only raising frequency made electrons emerge faster"라는 대조 구조에서 D(unchanged)가 유일하게 논리적임. 광전효과 사실 서술 정확. A(negligible)는 'remained'와 결합하면 그럴듯해 보여 비교가 필요하고, C(diminished)는 'remained diminished'가 어색하나 세기 증가에 따른 반대 결과로 오해 가능. B도 말은 됨. 두 단계(대조 파악 + 'only raising frequency' 단서 연결) 요구로 medium 적합. 해설 한·영 일치, 영어 자연스러움.

advisory.note: 광전효과 서술이 정확하다. 'merely… while'의 대조와 예측(더 많은 에너지)을 연결해야 하므로 중간 난이도에 맞다. A와 C는 그럴듯한 오답이다.

problem.question: The student wants to contrast how well two materials resist dielectric breakdown. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Dry air begins to conduct at about 3 million volts per meter, whereas mica can withstand a field of roughly 118 million volts per meter before breaking down.
Dry air has a dielectric strength of about 3 million volts per meter, which is why lightning can form when the field in a storm cloud becomes strong enough.
Mica, a mineral used in capacitors, has a dielectric strength of roughly 118 million volts per meter, the field strength at which it begins to conduct.
Insulators such as air and mica normally block current, but when the electric field becomes strong enough, they undergo dielectric breakdown and begin to conduct.

problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to contrast how well two materials resist breakdown, so the sentence needs both materials' dielectric strengths side by side. A does this, setting dry air (about 3 million V/m) against mica (about 118 million V/m) with "whereas." B gives the figure for air and ties it to lightning, but it never compares air to a second material. C gives only mica's figure. D mentions both materials, but it only describes what they have in common (both break down) and says nothing about how much each one can withstand.

problem.passage:
In microfluidic devices, liquids travel through channels narrower than a human hair. At such tiny scales, viscosity matters far more than inertia, so the fluid moves in smooth, parallel layers instead of swirling ______ two streams flowing side by side in the same channel barely mix at all.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In microfluidic devices, liquids travel through channels narrower than a human hair. At such tiny scales, viscosity matters far more than inertia, so the fluid moves in smooth, parallel layers instead of swirling ______ two streams flowing side by side in the same channel barely mix at all.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: chaotically, as a result,
chaotically
chaotically. As a result,
chaotically, as a result
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "At such tiny scales ... swirling chaotically"와 뒤 "two streams ... barely mix at all"은 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 마침표 등으로 분리해야 하므로 마침표 뒤에 "As a result,"로 새 문장을 시작하는 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다("as a result"는 접속부사로 등위접속사가 아니다). B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("At such tiny scales ... swirling chaotically") and the text after it ("two streams ... barely mix at all") are both independent clauses, each with its own subject and verb. Two independent clauses need to be properly separated, so C is correct: a period ends the first sentence, and "As a result," begins the next one. A and D join the clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice, because "as a result" is a transitional phrase, not a coordinating conjunction. B runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤 모두 독립절이며, C만 마침표로 올바르게 분리. A·D는 쉼표 스플라이스, B는 run-on으로 명확히 배제됨. 해설 한·영 일치, 과학 내용(미세유체·층류)도 사실에 부합. 단일 규칙(독립절 경계)으로 해결되는 easy 수준에 적합.

advisory.note: 쉼표 스플라이스와 접속부사를 구분하는 규칙 하나로 풀 수 있는 전형적인 easy 문항이다. 오답들도 흔히 하는 실수 유형이다.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes a process that reverses the changes introduced earlier in the text.
It describes a drawback of cold working that the text goes on to criticize.
It describes a method that the text later argues is less effective than cold working.
It describes an exception to the general claim made at the end of the text.

problem.explanationEn: The first sentences explain that cold working stretches the grains and makes the metal brittle, and the underlined sentence introduces heating that forms new, defect-free grains to replace the distorted ones, so A is correct. The final sentence confirms this process restores the metal's softness. B is wrong because the underlined sentence presents a remedy, not a drawback of cold working. C is wrong because the text never compares the two methods' effectiveness. D is wrong because the final sentence supports the underlined sentence rather than being contradicted by it.

advisory.note: 메모 하나(산소 없음)만으로 바로 풀리는 문항이다. B는 원인-결과 구조를 흉내 낸 그럴듯한 오답이고, C와 D는 목표와 관계없는 메모를 쓴 전형적인 오답이다. easy 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
Some organic molecules can attach to a single metal ion at two or more points at once, wrapping around it like a claw. This process, called chelation, produces a coordination complex in which the metal ion is held very tightly and cannot easily break free. ______ doctors use chelating agents to capture toxic metals such as lead in a patient's bloodstream so that the body can safely flush them out.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Some organic molecules can attach to a single metal ion at two or more points at once, wrapping around it like a claw. This process, called chelation, produces a coordination complex in which the metal ion is held very tightly and cannot easily break free. ______ doctors use chelating agents to capture toxic metals such as lead in a patient's bloodstream so that the body can safely flush them out.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
For this reason,
In contrast,
Similarly,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 킬레이트화가 금속 이온을 매우 단단히 붙잡아 쉽게 풀려나지 못하게 한다고 설명한다. 뒤 문장은 그 성질 때문에 의사들이 킬레이트제로 독성 금속을 붙잡아 몸 밖으로 내보낸다는 결과를 말하므로, 원인-결과를 나타내는 B가 정답이다. A는 예상과 반대되는 내용을 이끌지만 뒤 문장은 앞 내용과 어긋나지 않는다. C는 대조를 나타내는데 두 문장은 서로 대비되지 않는다. D는 비슷한 다른 사례를 덧붙일 때 쓰지만 뒤 문장은 앞 내용을 응용한 것이지 비슷한 다른 현상이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: The earlier sentence explains that chelation holds a metal ion very tightly so it cannot easily break free. The last sentence describes what follows from that property: doctors use chelating agents to trap toxic metals and remove them from the body. That is a cause-and-effect relationship, so B is correct. A signals something unexpected or opposing, but the last sentence fits naturally with what came before. C signals a contrast, and the two sentences are not being compared as opposites. D adds a similar but separate case, but the last sentence is a use of the same property, not a parallel example.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(금속 이온을 단단히 붙잡음)→뒤 문장(그래서 의사가 킬레이트제로 독성 금속 제거)은 명확한 원인-결과 관계로 B가 유일한 정답. A·C·D는 각각 양보·대조·유사 추가의 전형적 오답으로 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제 가능. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 글자 참조가 일치하고 정확함. 킬레이트 요법 관련 사실 오류 없음. 저작권 의심 없음. easy 난이도에 적합.

advisory.note: 원인-결과 관계가 명확하고 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. 오답 선택지는 전형적인 접속어들이다. 킬레이션 요법으로 납을 제거한다는 내용은 사실과 맞다.

problem.passage:
Most solids melt into a liquid before they turn into a gas. Ice, for instance, becomes water when it warms, and only later does that water evaporate. Some substances, ______ skip the liquid stage entirely in a process called sublimation. Dry ice, which is frozen carbon dioxide, changes directly from a solid into a gas at room temperature, which is why it leaves no puddle behind as it disappears.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Most solids melt into a liquid before they turn into a gas. Ice, for instance, becomes water when it warms, and only later does that water evaporate. Some substances, ______ skip the liquid stage entirely in a process called sublimation. Dry ice, which is frozen carbon dioxide, changes directly from a solid into a gas at room temperature, which is why it leaves no puddle behind as it disappears.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: therefore,
similarly,
however,
for example,
problem.explanation: 앞 문장들은 대부분의 고체가 액체 단계를 거쳐 기체가 된다고 설명하고, 빈칸이 있는 문장은 일부 물질이 액체 단계를 '완전히 건너뛴다'고 말하므로 두 내용은 대조 관계이다. 따라서 대조를 나타내는 C가 정답이다. A는 결과를 나타내지만, 승화는 앞 내용에서 비롯된 결과가 아니라 예외이다. B는 유사함을 나타내지만 두 과정은 서로 다르다. D는 예시를 나타내지만, 승화는 액체를 거치는 녹는 과정의 한 예가 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: The earlier sentences say that most solids melt into a liquid before becoming a gas, while the sentence with the blank says some substances skip the liquid stage entirely. These two ideas contrast, so C, which signals contrast, is correct. A signals a result, but sublimation doesn't follow from the earlier point; it's an exception to it. B signals similarity, but the two processes are different. D signals an example, but sublimation isn't an instance of melting into a liquid first.

quality.seed: physical science — Sublimation solid directly converting vapor phase skipping liquid state

hardJudge.note: 'Most solids melt first' vs. 'some substances skip the liquid stage entirely' is a direct contrast; 'however' is the only logical choice. Distractors (result/similarity/example) are standard plausible misconceptions. Science content (dry ice sublimation) is accurate. Korean and English explanations agree and reference the correct letters. Original passage; difficulty appropriate for easy.

advisory.note: 'most ... Some substances' 대비가 지문에 바로 드러나며, 대조 관계 하나만 알면 풀 수 있다. 빈칸 앞에 콤마가 있어 선택지 끝 콤마와 짝을 이루므로 삽입 위치도 맞다. 사실관계(드라이아이스 승화) 정확.

problem.passage:
In electroplating, an object to be coated is connected to the negative terminal of a power source and placed in a solution containing dissolved metal. When the current is switched on, a thin metal layer begins to form on the object. Pulled through the solution toward the negatively charged spoon, ______ gain electrons at its surface and settle there as a smooth, solid coating of silver.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In electroplating, an object to be coated is connected to the negative terminal of a power source and placed in a solution containing dissolved metal. When the current is switched on, a thin metal layer begins to form on the object. Pulled through the solution toward the negatively charged spoon, ______ gain electrons at its surface and settle there as a smooth, solid coating of silver.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the technicians monitoring the plating bath
the finished silver coatings
the terminals of the power source
the positively charged silver ions
problem.explanation:
정답 D. 문장 앞의 분사구문 "Pulled through the solution toward the negatively charged spoon"은 주절의 주어를 수식한다. 그러니 주어는 실제로 용액 속을 지나 음극(스푼) 쪽으로 끌려가고, 표면에서 전자를 얻어 고체 은으로 쌓이는 대상이어야 한다. 그 대상은 양전하를 띤 은 이온이다.
A: 기술자는 공정과 상관없는 엉뚱한 명사다. 사람이 용액 속을 지나 끌려가 전자를 얻을 수는 없다.
B: 완성된 은 코팅은 이온과 관련은 있지만 범주가 다르다. 이온이 쌓여서 생긴 결과물이라서, 이미 다 만들어진 코팅이 용액을 지나 끌려간 뒤 다시 코팅으로 쌓인다는 말은 논리에 맞지 않는다.
C: 복수형이라 동사 gain과 수는 맞는다. 하지만 전원의 단자는 고정된 장치이므로 용액을 지나 스푼 쪽으로 끌려갈 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is D. The opening phrase "Pulled through the solution toward the negatively charged spoon" modifies the subject of the main clause. That means the subject has to be the thing that actually travels through the solution to the spoon, picks up electrons there, and builds up as solid silver. Only the positively charged silver ions do all of that.
A: The technicians have nothing to do with this step. People aren't pulled through the solution, and they don't gain electrons.
B: The finished coatings are the result of the ions building up, so they're a different kind of thing. A finished coating can't travel through the solution and then turn into a coating.
C: "Terminals" is plural, so it agrees with "gain," but the terminals are fixed parts of the power source. They can't be pulled through the solution toward the spoon.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 타당: 분사구문 "Pulled through the solution toward the negatively charged spoon"의 논리적 주체는 음극으로 끌려가 전자를 얻어 석출되는 양이온(은 이온)이며, 전기도금 원리와도 일치한다. 네 선택지 모두 복수형이라 수일치로는 변별 불가하고, 모두 문법적으로 완전한 문장을 이루며, A(기술자)는 사람 범주 오답으로 체크리스트 전 항목 충족. 해설의 각 오답 배제 근거도 정확하다. 다만 지문 품질 지적: 앞부분에서는 "an object to be coated"라고만 하고 "spoon"을 한 번도 언급하지 않다가 마지막 문장에서 갑자기 "the negatively charged spoon"이 정관사와 함께 등장해 선행 지시 대상이 없다(지문 내 일관성 결함). 정답 판정에는 영향 없으나 출제 전 수정이 권장된다.

advisory.note: 네 선택지가 모두 복수형이라 gain과의 수일치로는 정답을 가를 수 없다. 전기도금 과정을 이해해야 이온이 끌려가 전자를 얻고 쌓인다는 의미 관계를 추론할 수 있다. 다만 지문에서 'an object'로만 소개된 대상이 갑자기 'the spoon'으로 등장해 결속성이 약간 떨어진다. 사소한 문제다.

problem.passage:
In the early 1900s, physicists were puzzled by the photoelectric effect, in which light shining on a metal knocks electrons loose. Classical wave theory predicted that brighter light should deliver more energy to each electron. Experiments showed otherwise: increasing the intensity of the light caused more electrons to be ejected from the metal ______ not make any individual electron leave with greater energy. In 1905, Albert Einstein resolved the puzzle by proposing that light arrives in discrete packets whose energy depends only on frequency.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In the early 1900s, physicists were puzzled by the photoelectric effect, in which light shining on a metal knocks electrons loose. Classical wave theory predicted that brighter light should deliver more energy to each electron. Experiments showed otherwise: increasing the intensity of the light caused more electrons to be ejected from the metal ______ not make any individual electron leave with greater energy. In 1905, Albert Einstein resolved the puzzle by proposing that light arrives in discrete packets whose energy depends only on frequency.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: surface, but it did
surface, so it did
surface, it did
surface but; it did
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 빈칸 앞뒤는 모두 완전한 독립절이다(‘increasing the intensity… caused more electrons to be ejected…’ / ‘it did not make… greater energy’). 앞 문장의 ‘Experiments showed otherwise’에서 보듯 두 절은 대조 관계다. 전자 수는 늘었지만 각 전자의 에너지는 늘지 않았다. 따라서 쉼표+등위접속사 ‘but’이 맞다.
B: 쉼표+등위접속사라는 형식은 맞지만 ‘so’는 인과를 나타낸다. 전자가 더 많이 튀어나온 것이 에너지가 커지지 않은 원인은 아니므로 의미 관계가 맞지 않는다.
C: 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이었기 때문에 콤마 스플라이스다.
D: 세미콜론이 접속사 ‘but’ 뒤에 와서 절 경계가 아닌 곳을 끊고 있다. ‘but’이 앞 절 끝에 고립되어 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, A: The text on each side of the blank is a complete independent clause. The first is "increasing the intensity... caused more electrons to be ejected...," and the second is "it did not make any individual electron leave with greater energy." The phrase "Experiments showed otherwise" signals that the two clauses contrast: more electrons came out, but no single electron gained more energy. Joining them with a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "but" is therefore correct.
B: The structure (comma + coordinating conjunction) is valid, but "so" signals cause and effect. Ejecting more electrons is not the reason the electrons failed to gain energy, so the logic is wrong.
C: This joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes it a comma splice.
D: The semicolon comes after "but," not at the actual boundary between the clauses. That leaves "but" stranded at the end of the first clause and makes the sentence ungrammatical.

hardJudge.note: 두 절 모두 완전한 독립절이며, 'Experiments showed otherwise'와 '전자 수 증가 vs 개별 에너지 불변'의 대조 관계가 문맥상 분명해 A(쉼표+but)가 유일한 정답. B는 접속사 형식은 맞지만 인과(so)로 의미 오류, C는 콤마 스플라이스, D는 세미콜론 오배치. 단순 경계 판별을 넘어 절 간 논리 관계(대조 vs 인과)를 판단해 접속사를 골라야 하므로 medium 이상. 과학 사실(광전효과, 아인슈타인 1905) 정확. 해설 모순 없음.

advisory.note: A를 넣으면 'from the metal surface, but it did not make...'가 되어 문법·의미 모두 맞다. 광전효과 서술도 사실과 맞다. B(so)를 걸러내려면 문맥 속 대조 관계를 추론해야 하므로 형식만 보는 판단을 넘어선다. 다만 C(콤마 스플라이스)와 D(but 뒤 세미콜론)는 쉽게 지워져서 hard 수준으로 보기에는 경계선에 있다.

problem.passage:
In a colloidal suspension such as paint or milk, tiny particles stay dispersed rather than clumping and settling out. Many of these particles carry surface charges of the same sign, so the electrostatic repulsion that builds up whenever two of them drift close together ______ pushes them back apart before the weaker attractive van der Waals forces can bind them into larger aggregates.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In a colloidal suspension such as paint or milk, tiny particles stay dispersed rather than clumping and settling out. Many of these particles carry surface charges of the same sign, so the electrostatic repulsion that builds up whenever two of them drift close together ______ pushes them back apart before the weaker attractive van der Waals forces can bind them into larger aggregates.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; in effect,
, in effect,
, in effect
in effect,
problem.explanation:
정답 B. 빈칸 앞 "the electrostatic repulsion that builds up whenever two of them drift close together"는 주어(repulsion)와 그것을 수식하는 관계절일 뿐이며, 이 주어의 본동사는 빈칸 뒤의 "pushes"이다. "drift close together"에서 끝나 완결된 절처럼 보이지만 이는 whenever절 내부일 뿐이다. 따라서 in effect는 한 절 안의 주어와 동사 사이에 낀 삽입어이므로 양쪽에 쉼표를 하나씩 찍어야 한다.
A: 세미콜론은 두 독립절을 연결할 때 쓰는데, 앞부분은 동사가 없는 주어부일 뿐이다. 삽입어를 절 경계로 잘못 본 경우다.
C: 앞에만 쉼표가 있고 뒤에는 없어서 삽입어를 비대칭으로 처리했다. 그 결과 주어와 동사 사이에 쉼표 하나만 남는다.
D: 뒤에만 쉼표가 있어 역시 비대칭이다. "together in effect"처럼 삽입어가 앞의 관계절에 붙어 버린다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is B. The words before the blank, "the electrostatic repulsion that builds up whenever two of them drift close together," are only a subject plus a modifying clause. The main verb that goes with "repulsion" comes after the blank: "pushes." The phrase "drift close together" may look like the end of a complete clause, but it belongs to the "whenever" clause. So "in effect" is an interrupter placed between a subject and its verb, and it needs a comma on each side.
A is wrong because a semicolon has to join two independent clauses, and the part before the blank has no main verb. This choice treats the interrupter as if it marked a clause boundary.
C is wrong because it puts a comma only before the interrupter. That leaves just one comma between the subject and its verb.
D is wrong because it puts a comma only after the interrupter. That attaches "in effect" to the "whenever" clause, and the interrupter is still not set off evenly on both sides.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 타당: 빈칸 앞은 주어 "the electrostatic repulsion" + 관계절(that builds up whenever ... together)로 동사가 없는 주어부이며, 본동사 "pushes"가 빈칸 뒤에 있으므로 in effect는 주어-동사 사이 삽입어 → 양쪽 쉼표. 해설 논리 일관. 과학 내용(동일 부호 표면전하 간 정전기 반발이 van der Waals 응집을 막음, DLVO 이론)도 사실에 부합. 체크리스트 4 미충족: 앞부분이 독립절이 아니므로 어떤 선택지도 콤마 스플라이스를 만들지 않음(A는 세미콜론 오용, C/D는 비대칭 쉼표). 다만 이는 설계상 불가피하며, "drift close together"가 완결 절처럼 보이는 함정으로 절 경계 판단을 요구해 hard 적합성은 있음.

advisory.note: B가 정답인 것은 맞다. 빈칸 앞부분은 관계절과 whenever절이 붙은 긴 주어부이고 본동사는 pushes이므로, in effect는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 삽입어로서 앞뒤에 쉼표가 필요하다. 'drift close together'가 완결된 절처럼 보이게 만든 함정이 있어서 삽입어와 절 경계를 구분하는 hard 특성이 실제로 작동한다. 다만 오답 중에 콤마 스플라이스가 없다. A는 세미콜론이고 C와 D는 둘 다 쉼표 비대칭 유형이어서 체크리스트 4번을 충족하지 못한다. 앞부분이 독립절이 아니라는 구조상 콤마 스플라이스 오답을 만들기도 어렵다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The enthalpy of combustion is the heat released when a substance burns completely in oxygen.
- In complete combustion, a hydrocarbon fuel's carbon ends up as carbon dioxide and its hydrogen ends up as water.
- Methane releases about 890 kilojoules per mole when it burns completely.
- Octane, a major component of gasoline, releases about 5,470 kilojoules per mole when it burns completely.
- Chemists measure these values with a bomb calorimeter, a sealed steel container submerged in water.
- If oxygen is limited, incomplete combustion produces carbon monoxide and releases less heat.

The student wants to introduce the concept to an audience unfamiliar with it, making clear what the quantity represents and under what chemical conditions it applies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The enthalpy of combustion is the heat released when a substance burns completely in oxygen.
- In complete combustion, a hydrocarbon fuel's carbon ends up as carbon dioxide and its hydrogen ends up as water.
- Methane releases about 890 kilojoules per mole when it burns completely.
- Octane, a major component of gasoline, releases about 5,470 kilojoules per mole when it burns completely.
- Chemists measure these values with a bomb calorimeter, a sealed steel container submerged in water.
- If oxygen is limited, incomplete combustion produces carbon monoxide and releases less heat.
problem.question: The student wants to introduce the concept to an audience unfamiliar with it, making clear what the quantity represents and under what chemical conditions it applies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Octane, a major component of gasoline, releases about 5,470 kilojoules per mole when it burns completely, far more than the roughly 890 kilojoules per mole released by methane.
Many chemical ideas, including heat, oxygen, fuels, and laboratory instruments such as the bomb calorimeter, help scientists understand how substances like methane and octane behave.
Chemists measure the heat released by burning fuels with a bomb calorimeter, a sealed steel container that is submerged in water.
The enthalpy of combustion is the heat a substance releases when it burns completely in oxygen, a process that converts a hydrocarbon's carbon into carbon dioxide and its hydrogen into water.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: 목표는 처음 듣는 독자에게 개념을 소개하면서 그 양이 무엇을 나타내는지(완전 연소 때 방출되는 열)와 어떤 화학적 조건에서 적용되는지(완전 연소: 탄소→CO₂, 수소→H₂O)를 밝히는 것이다. D만 정의와 조건을 함께 담고 있다.
A: 구체적인 수치 비교만 있어 지나치게 세부적이다. 개념이 무엇인지 정의하지 않는다.
B: 열, 산소, 연료, 장비 등을 두루 나열해 지나치게 포괄적이다. 개념이 무엇인지 초점을 잃었다.
C: 측정 장비라는 다른 항목을 부각한다. 그 양의 의미나 연소 조건은 설명하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice D is correct. Your goal is to introduce the concept to newcomers, so the sentence needs to say what the quantity represents (the heat released when a substance burns completely in oxygen) and the condition under which it applies (complete combustion, where carbon becomes carbon dioxide and hydrogen becomes water). D is the only choice that gives both.
Choice A is too detailed. It compares specific values for two fuels but never defines the concept.
Choice B is too broad. It lists many loosely related ideas and loses focus on what the quantity actually is.
Choice C focuses on a different note: how the values are measured. It says nothing about what the quantity means or about the combustion conditions.

hardJudge.note: 목표가 두 요소(양의 의미 + 적용 조건)를 요구하고, D만 노트 1·2를 결합해 둘을 충족. A는 수치 비교로 과도하게 구체적, B는 개념 나열로 과도하게 포괄적, C는 측정 장비로 초점 이탈. 수치(메탄 ~890, 옥탄 ~5,470 kJ/mol) 및 봄베 열량계·불완전 연소 설명 모두 사실과 부합. 해설도 정답을 정확히 뒷받침함.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 정의와 완전연소 조건을 결합해 목표 두 요소를 모두 충족함. 다만 오답이 쉽게 배제됨: A는 수치만, B는 공허한 나열, C는 장비만 다룸. 정의 문구가 들어간 선택지가 D 하나뿐이고, 불완전연소 메모를 활용한 그럴듯한 오답(예: 정의+불완전연소 혼동, 또는 정의만 있고 조건 누락)이 없어 범위 판단(scope calibration)이 실질적으로 요구되지 않음. 전형적 medium 수준.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- When a cell is placed in a hypotonic solution (one with a lower solute concentration than the cell's interior), water moves into the cell by osmosis.
- Animal cells such as red blood cells lack a rigid cell wall, so continued water influx causes them to swell and eventually burst—a process called osmotic lysis.
- In a 2021 study, biophysicist Lena Okafor exposed red blood cells from 40 donors to gradually diluted saline.
- Cells from donors over age 60 tended to lyse at slightly higher saline concentrations than cells from younger donors, but the difference was small and did not hold for every donor.
- Okafor suggested that age-related changes in membrane flexibility might explain the pattern but noted that further testing is needed.
- In a separate 2019 study, Tomás Reyes found that red blood cells stored for more than 35 days lysed at markedly higher saline concentrations than freshly collected cells.

The student wants to present both the well-established mechanism and Okafor's finding, representing each with appropriate confidence. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- When a cell is placed in a hypotonic solution (one with a lower solute concentration than the cell's interior), water moves into the cell by osmosis.
- Animal cells such as red blood cells lack a rigid cell wall, so continued water influx causes them to swell and eventually burst—a process called osmotic lysis.
- In a 2021 study, biophysicist Lena Okafor exposed red blood cells from 40 donors to gradually diluted saline.
- Cells from donors over age 60 tended to lyse at slightly higher saline concentrations than cells from younger donors, but the difference was small and did not hold for every donor.
- Okafor suggested that age-related changes in membrane flexibility might explain the pattern but noted that further testing is needed.
- In a separate 2019 study, Tomás Reyes found that red blood cells stored for more than 35 days lysed at markedly higher saline concentrations than freshly collected cells.
problem.question: The student wants to present both the well-established mechanism and Okafor's finding, representing each with appropriate confidence. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Because red blood cells lack a rigid wall, water entering them in a hypotonic solution makes them swell and burst; Okafor's data suggest that cells from older donors may be somewhat more prone to this rupture, though the reason remains uncertain.

Because red blood cells lack a rigid wall, water entering them in a hypotonic solution makes them swell and burst; Okafor's data prove that stiffer membranes in older donors cause their cells to rupture more easily.

Red blood cells placed in a hypotonic solution may possibly swell and burst under some conditions; Okafor's data suggest that cells from older donors may be somewhat more prone to this rupture, though the reason remains uncertain.

Because red blood cells lack a rigid wall, water entering them in a hypotonic solution makes them swell and burst; Okafor's data suggest that cells stored for over a month may be somewhat more prone to this rupture, though the reason remains uncertain.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 삼투압성 용해의 기전은 확립된 사실이므로 단정적으로 서술하고, Okafor의 결과는 차이가 작고 모든 공여자에게 해당하지 않으며 원인도 추가 검증이 필요하므로 잠정적으로("suggest", "may", "uncertain") 서술했다.
B: Okafor의 잠정적 결과를 "prove"와 "cause"로 과장했다. 막의 유연성 변화는 가설일 뿐이다.
C: 세포벽이 없는 세포가 저장성 용액에서 부풀어 터지는 확립된 기전을 "may possibly", "under some conditions"로 불필요하게 약화했다.
D: 확실성 수준은 알맞지만 저장 기간에 관한 내용은 Reyes의 연구이며, Okafor의 연구(공여자 나이)와 혼동했다. 게다가 Reyes의 결과는 차이가 '뚜렷했다'.
problem.explanationEn:
A is correct. Osmotic lysis is a well-established mechanism, so it is stated as fact. Okafor's age difference was small, didn't hold for every donor, and her explanation still needs testing. That's why her finding is hedged with "suggest," "may," and "uncertain."
B overstates Okafor's tentative result. "Prove" and "cause" turn her proposed explanation about membrane flexibility into established fact.
C needlessly weakens the established mechanism. Cells without a rigid wall do swell and burst in hypotonic solutions, so hedges like "may possibly" and "under some conditions" don't fit.
D hedges at the right level but credits Okafor with the storage-time finding. That finding came from Reyes's separate study, and his difference was actually marked.

hardJudge.note: A는 확립된 기전(단정)과 Okafor의 잠정적 결과(suggest/may/uncertain)를 노트의 확실성 수준에 맞게 구분. B는 과잉 일반화(prove/cause), C는 확정 기전의 과도한 약화(may possibly/under some conditions), D는 Reyes 연구를 Okafor에 귀속시킨 출처 혼동 오답으로 각각 명확히 배제된다. 삼투·용혈 과학 내용은 정확하며 가상의 연구자 설정에 저작권 문제 없음. 기전과 연구 결과를 동시에 통합하고 확실성을 판별해야 하므로 medium 이상의 사고를 요구한다.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 맞고 해설도 일관됨. 다만 선택지가 같은 틀을 공유하고 B('prove/cause'), C('may possibly/under some conditions')의 확실성 표지가 노골적이어서 단어 하나만 보고도 제거할 수 있음. D도 저장 기간이라는 내용 하나만으로 Reyes 연구와 바로 구별됨. 확실성 판별이 전형적인 medium 수준에 머물러 hard 변별력이 부족함.

problem.passage:
Diamond is among the hardest substances known, resisting scratches from nearly every other material. Graphite, by contrast, is so soft that it flakes onto paper when a pencil is dragged across it. Yet chemical analysis shows that both materials consist of nothing but carbon atoms. ______ the striking differences between them must arise not from what they are made of but from how their atoms are arranged: rigid three-dimensional bonds in diamond, loosely stacked sheets in graphite.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Diamond is among the hardest substances known, resisting scratches from nearly every other material. Graphite, by contrast, is so soft that it flakes onto paper when a pencil is dragged across it. Yet chemical analysis shows that both materials consist of nothing but carbon atoms. ______ the striking differences between them must arise not from what they are made of but from how their atoms are arranged: rigid three-dimensional bonds in diamond, loosely stacked sheets in graphite.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Similarly,
Nevertheless,
Thus,
Meanwhile,
problem.explanation:
정답 C(Thus): 지문은 두 관찰을 제시한다. 성질은 극단적으로 다르고(다이아몬드는 단단하고 흑연은 무르다), 구성 원소는 똑같다(둘 다 탄소뿐). 두 사실을 합치면, 차이의 원인은 구성 원소가 아니라 원자 배열에 있다는 결론이 나온다. 마지막 문장은 이 결론이므로 결과·추론을 나타내는 Thus가 알맞다.
A(Similarly): '둘 다 탄소'라는 공통점 한쪽만 보고 유사성을 이어 가는 전환어다. 그런데 마지막 문장은 비슷한 사례를 하나 더 드는 문장이 아니라 결론이다.
B(Nevertheless): 성질 차이와 동일한 구성을 단순한 대립으로만 본 선택이다. 마지막 문장은 앞의 내용에도 불구하고 일어나는 일이 아니라, 앞의 내용에서 바로 도출되는 내용이다.
D(Meanwhile): 동시에 벌어지는 일이나 별개의 화제를 잇는 전환어여서, 추론 관계를 전혀 나타내지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn:
C (Thus) is correct. The passage gives you two observations that seem to clash. First, diamond and graphite have opposite properties: one is extremely hard and the other is soft. Second, they have the same makeup, since both are pure carbon. If you combine these two facts, you get a conclusion: the differences can't come from the material itself, so they must come from how the atoms are arranged. The last sentence states that conclusion, so you need a transition that signals a result, and "Thus" does that.
A (Similarly) only picks up on what the two materials have in common. The last sentence doesn't add a similar example; it draws a conclusion.
B (Nevertheless) treats the two observations as a simple contrast. But the last sentence follows from those facts; it isn't true in spite of them.
D (Meanwhile) signals something happening at the same time or a separate topic. It doesn't show any reasoning, so it doesn't fit here.

hardJudge.note: 두 관찰(성질 극단적 차이 vs 동일 구성 원소)을 'Yet'으로 충돌시킨 뒤 마지막 문장이 두 사실을 종합한 추론 결론이므로 Thus가 유일하게 성립. Similarly는 '동일 구성' 한쪽만, Nevertheless는 단순 대립으로만 처리, Meanwhile은 추론 관계 부재로 각각 배제됨. 다만 'must arise'라는 결론 표지가 비교적 뚜렷해 hard 중에서는 난도가 낮은 편이며, 지정된 hard 특성 중 multi_step_logical_inference만 실질적으로 요구됨. 사실 관계(다이아몬드·흑연 모두 탄소 동소체, 3차원 공유결합 vs 층상 구조) 정확.

advisory.note: 정답과 해설은 문제없다. 다만 'must arise'라는 결론 신호가 강하고, 앞 문장의 Yet이 대비를 이미 처리해 두었다. 그래서 Thus는 전형적인 medium 수준의 결과 전환어 문항이며, 여러 단계의 추론이나 추상적 관계 판별을 실제로 요구하지 않는다. Nevertheless 오답도 약한 함정에 그친다.

problem.passage:
Metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs, are crystals built from metal atoms linked by carbon-based molecules. Chemists often make them through hydrothermal synthesis, heating the ingredients in water inside a sealed container until the crystals form. The resulting structures are full of tiny pores, much like a sponge. In a recent series of tests, a research team made several MOFs this way and measured how much carbon dioxide each one could hold. The samples with the most internal pore space consistently stored the most gas, while denser samples with fewer open spaces stored far less. The team concluded that, for these materials, the amount of empty space inside the crystal is what mainly determines how much gas the material can capture.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs, are crystals built from metal atoms linked by carbon-based molecules. Chemists often make them through hydrothermal synthesis, heating the ingredients in water inside a sealed container until the crystals form. The resulting structures are full of tiny pores, much like a sponge. In a recent series of tests, a research team made several MOFs this way and measured how much carbon dioxide each one could hold. The samples with the most internal pore space consistently stored the most gas, while denser samples with fewer open spaces stored far less. The team concluded that, for these materials, the amount of empty space inside the crystal is what mainly determines how much gas the material can capture.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Tests on several MOFs suggest that a crystal's internal openness largely controls how much carbon dioxide it can take up.
Tests on several MOFs suggest that heating ingredients in sealed water containers is the only way to produce such crystals.
Tests on several MOFs suggest that denser crystals are generally better than open ones at trapping carbon dioxide.
Tests on several MOFs suggest that the type of metal atom chosen matters more than the crystal's structure for storing gas.
problem.explanation: 지문은 MOF의 제조 방식을 소개한 뒤, 내부 기공 공간이 많을수록 이산화탄소를 더 많이 저장한다는 실험 결과와 결론으로 마무리하므로 A가 중심 생각이다. B는 수열 합성을 언급한 세부 내용을 '유일한 방법'으로 과장한 것이다. C는 밀도가 높은 시료가 훨씬 적게 저장했다는 지문 내용과 반대이다. D의 금속 원자 종류는 지문에서 비교된 적이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text introduces how MOFs are made, then reports that samples with more internal pore space stored more carbon dioxide and concludes that empty space mainly determines gas capture, so A is the main idea. B takes a background detail about hydrothermal synthesis and wrongly claims it is the only method. C reverses the finding, since the denser samples stored far less. D brings up the type of metal atom, which the text never compares.

quality.seed: physical science — Hydrothermal synthesis of metal-organic frameworks and porosity-dependent gas adsorption capacity

hardJudge.note: 지문 마지막 문장이 결론을 직접 진술하고 A가 이를 그대로 바꿔 말함. B(세부 과장), C(반대), D(언급 없음)는 전형적 오답 유형으로 쉽게 배제 가능. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 선택지 참조 일치, 모순 없음. MOF 설명(금속+유기 링커, 수열 합성, 다공성)도 사실과 부합.

advisory.note: 결론 문장이 지문에 명시되어 있어 easy 수준에 적합하다. 오답은 세부 과장(B), 내용 반전(C), 지문에 없는 비교(D)로 전형적인 오답 유형이다. 사실관계 오류는 없다. MOF와 수열 합성 설명이 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Capacitors store electrical energy, and engineers often build them from ferroelectric ceramics such as barium titanate. These materials have a very high dielectric constant, a measure of how well a material can hold electric charge when voltage is applied. However, a high dielectric constant alone does not guarantee good energy storage. When a strong voltage is applied, the dielectric constant of many ferroelectric ceramics drops sharply, which limits how much energy the capacitor can actually hold. To address this problem, researchers add small amounts of other elements, such as strontium or bismuth, to the ceramic. These additions make the material's response to voltage more stable, so the dielectric constant stays higher under strong voltage, allowing the capacitor to store more energy.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Capacitors store electrical energy, and engineers often build them from ferroelectric ceramics such as barium titanate. These materials have a very high dielectric constant, a measure of how well a material can hold electric charge when voltage is applied. However, a high dielectric constant alone does not guarantee good energy storage. When a strong voltage is applied, the dielectric constant of many ferroelectric ceramics drops sharply, which limits how much energy the capacitor can actually hold. To address this problem, researchers add small amounts of other elements, such as strontium or bismuth, to the ceramic. These additions make the material's response to voltage more stable, so the dielectric constant stays higher under strong voltage, allowing the capacitor to store more energy.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Ferroelectric ceramics such as barium titanate are rarely used in capacitors because their dielectric constant is too low to store useful amounts of energy.
Adding certain elements to ferroelectric ceramics can keep their charge-holding ability from falling under strong voltage, which improves how much energy capacitors can store.
Strontium and bismuth are able to store more electrical energy on their own than any ferroelectric ceramic can.
Capacitors made from ferroelectric ceramics store the most energy when only a weak voltage is applied to them.
problem.explanation: 지문은 강유전성 세라믹의 유전율이 강한 전압에서 떨어지는 문제를 제시한 뒤, 다른 원소를 첨가하면 유전율이 높게 유지되어 에너지 저장량이 늘어난다고 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 지문에서 이 세라믹들의 유전율이 매우 높다고 했으므로 틀렸다. C는 첨가 원소 자체가 에너지를 저장한다고 하지만, 지문은 그 원소들이 세라믹을 안정시킨다고만 말한다. D는 약한 전압에 대한 주장으로, 지문에서 다루지 않는 내용이며 해결책이라는 중심 내용을 놓친다.
problem.explanationEn: The text first describes a problem, which is that the dielectric constant of ferroelectric ceramics drops under strong voltage. It then gives a solution: adding other elements keeps that value high so the capacitor stores more energy. That makes B the correct answer. A is wrong because the text says these ceramics have a very high dielectric constant, not a low one. C is wrong because the added elements stabilize the ceramic; the text never says they store energy on their own. D makes a claim about weak voltage that the text never makes, and it misses the main point about the solution.

quality.seed: physical science — Dielectric constant manipulation in ferroelectric ceramics for capacitor energy storage applications

hardJudge.note: 지문은 문제(강전압에서 유전율 하락)→해결(Sr/Bi 첨가로 안정화→저장 에너지 증가)의 명확한 구조이며 B가 이를 정확히 요약함. A는 '매우 높은 유전율'과 직접 모순, C는 첨가 원소가 자체 저장한다는 지문 외 주장, D는 약전압에 대한 미언급 주장으로 전형적 오독 선택지. 한·영 해설 모두 정답과 일치하고 글자 참조 정확, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 과학적 내용(BaTiO3 강유전체, 고전압 하 유전율 포화/감소, Sr·Bi 도핑으로 안정화)도 사실과 부합. 단일 개념(중심 생각 파악)으로 풀리며 단서가 직접 드러나므로 easy 적합.

advisory.note: 문제→해결 구조라 중심 내용이 분명하다. 오답 A(유전율 사실 반대), C(원소의 역할 오해), D(지문에 없는 약한 전압 주장)은 모두 전형적인 오답 유형이며 지문에 근거해 바로 배제할 수 있다. 지문의 사실 내용(BaTiO3, Sr/Bi 도핑, 강전계에서의 유전율 저하)도 타당하다.

problem.passage:

problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: force
are forcing
forces
have forced
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "deformation"이고, "known as creep"은 주어를 설명하는 삽입 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 동사가 필요하며, 현재 시제로 일반적 사실을 서술하는 C의 "forces"가 정답이다. A의 "force", B의 "are forcing", D의 "have forced"는 모두 복수 주어에 맞는 형태이므로 단수 주어 "deformation"과 수가 일치하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "deformation"; the phrase "known as creep" is just a modifier describing it. So the sentence needs a singular verb, and C, "forces," correctly states a general fact in the present tense. A ("force"), B ("are forcing"), and D ("have forced") are all plural verb forms, so none of them agrees with the singular subject "deformation."

hardJudge.note: 주어 "This gradual deformation"(단수)에 "known as creep" 삽입 수식어가 붙은 구조로, 단수 현재 동사 "forces"가 유일하게 적합함. A·B·D는 모두 복수형이라 규칙 하나로 배제됨. 한·영 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 오류 없음. 크리프(creep) 관련 공학적 서술도 사실에 부합. 다만 삽입구 내 명사 "creep"도 단수라 복수 오답의 유인력이 다소 약한 편이나, 단일 규칙 기반의 easy 난이도에는 적합함.

advisory.note: 주어-동사 수일치 단일 규칙 문항. 수식어 'known as creep'과 'creep'이 단서가 되며 오답은 모두 복수형이라 전형적 오개념에 해당함. 난이도 easy에 맞음.

The rapid movement of these charges across the tiny gap between the surfaces ______ the surrounding air, causing it to glow for a fraction of a second.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: When certain crystals, such as quartz or sugar, are crushed or split apart, they can give off brief flashes of light. This effect, known as triboluminescence, occurs because the breaking of a crystal separates electric charges along the newly formed surfaces. The rapid movement of these charges across the tiny gap between the surfaces ______ the surrounding air, causing it to glow for a fraction of a second.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: excite
have excited
are exciting
excites
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "movement"이고, "of these charges across the tiny gap between the surfaces"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 동사 "excites"가 필요하며, 현재 시제도 지문의 다른 동사(occurs, separates)와 맞으므로 D가 정답이다. A, B, C는 모두 복수 동사로, 주어 가까이에 있는 복수 명사 "charges"나 "surfaces"를 주어로 착각할 때 고르기 쉬운 오답이다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "movement." The phrase "of these charges across the tiny gap between the surfaces" just describes the subject. So the sentence needs a singular verb, "excites," and its present tense also matches the other verbs in the text (occurs, separates). That makes D correct. A, B, and C are all plural verbs, and they're easy to pick if you mistake a nearby plural noun like "charges" or "surfaces" for the subject.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "movement"(단수) + 전치사구 수식어 뒤 동사 수일치 문항. D "excites"만 단수형이며 A/B/C는 모두 복수형으로 인접 명사(charges, surfaces) 오인 유도 오답으로 적절. 지문 과학 내용(triboluminescence, 전하 분리로 공기 여기·발광)도 사실에 부합. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 단일 규칙(수일치)으로 해결 가능해 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 주어 movement(단수)와 동사의 수 일치를 묻는 문항으로, 두 개의 전치사구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있다. 오답 A·B·C는 모두 복수형이라 끌어당기는 명사(charges/surfaces)에 걸려드는 전형적인 오답이다. 수 일치 규칙 하나만 알면 풀리므로 easy 난이도에 맞다. 지문의 사실관계(마찰발광)도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Protein crystallographers have long struggled to grow crystals that are both large and well ordered. In a typical supersaturated protein solution, many tiny nuclei form at once, and these nuclei then compete for the same dissolved protein, yielding a shower of small, unevenly sized crystals. Biophysicist Lena Haugland and colleagues propose that the problem lies chiefly in the timing of nucleation rather than in growth conditions themselves. They hypothesize that if nucleation is confined to a brief initial burst—for example, by holding a solution at high supersaturation for only a few minutes and then diluting it to a level where existing crystals can grow but new nuclei cannot form—the resulting crystals will be more uniform in size and of higher diffraction quality than crystals grown under constant conditions.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Haugland and colleagues' hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: Protein crystallographers have long struggled to grow crystals that are both large and well ordered. In a typical supersaturated protein solution, many tiny nuclei form at once, and these nuclei then compete for the same dissolved protein, yielding a shower of small, unevenly sized crystals. Biophysicist Lena Haugland and colleagues propose that the problem lies chiefly in the timing of nucleation rather than in growth conditions themselves. They hypothesize that if nucleation is confined to a brief initial burst—for example, by holding a solution at high supersaturation for only a few minutes and then diluting it to a level where existing crystals can grow but new nuclei cannot form—the resulting crystals will be more uniform in size and of higher diffraction quality than crystals grown under constant conditions.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Haugland and colleagues' hypothesis?
options: Lysozyme samples exposed to high supersaturation for five minutes and then diluted produced crystals that varied little in size and diffracted to higher resolution than samples kept at a single constant supersaturation.
Lysozyme samples kept at constant high supersaturation produced more crystals per drop than samples kept at constant low supersaturation, though crystal quality was similar in both groups.
Lysozyme samples exposed to high supersaturation for five minutes and then diluted produced crystals that grew faster during the first hour than crystals in samples kept at constant conditions.
Lysozyme samples diluted after a brief period of high supersaturation produced crystals that diffracted no better than those from samples in which new nuclei continued to form throughout growth.
problem.explanation: 가설은 핵생성을 짧은 초기 구간에 한정하면 일정 조건에서 키운 결정보다 크기가 균일하고 회절 품질이 높은 결정이 생긴다는 것이다. A는 바로 이 처리군과 일정 조건 대조군을 비교해 크기 균일성과 회절 품질이 모두 향상되었음을 보여 주므로 가설을 직접 지지한다. B는 과포화도에 따라 결정 수가 달라짐을 보여 주지만, 핵생성 시점을 조절하는 처리를 시험하지 않았다. C는 같은 처리를 사용하지만 초기 성장 속도만 보고하며, 가설이 다루는 크기 균일성이나 품질은 다루지 않는다. D는 회절 품질이 개선되지 않았음을 보여 주므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다.
problem.explanationEn: The hypothesis says that limiting nucleation to a brief initial burst will produce crystals that are more uniform in size and diffract better than crystals grown under constant conditions. Choice A compares exactly that treatment with constant conditions and reports better size uniformity and better diffraction, so it directly supports the hypothesis. Choice B shows that supersaturation level affects how many crystals form, but it never tests the timed-burst approach. Choice C uses the right treatment but reports only early growth speed, not the size uniformity or quality the hypothesis predicts. Choice D shows no gain in diffraction quality, so it actually weakens the hypothesis.

hardJudge.note: A가 처리군(짧은 고과포화 후 희석)과 일정 조건 대조군을 비교해 크기 균일성·회절 품질 향상을 모두 보고하므로 정답 타당. C는 올바른 처리군이지만 결과 변수가 다르고(성장 속도), B는 처리 자체를 시험하지 않으며, D는 가설을 약화하는 결과로 오답 구성이 적절. 해설 한·영 일치, 선택지 참조 정확, 사실 오류 없음. 가설 내용 파악 + 처리와 결과 변수 두 가지를 모두 확인해야 하는 2단계 판단으로 medium에 부합.

advisory.note: A는 처리 방식, 대조군, 두 가지 예측(크기 균일성, 회절 품질)을 모두 정확히 짚는다. C(처리는 같지만 결과 지표가 다름)와 B(관련 변수지만 처리가 다름)는 부분적으로 그럴듯해 비교가 필요한 오답이다. D는 가설을 약화하는 선택지다. A가 가설 문구를 꽤 직접적으로 되풀이해 medium 중에서도 쉬운 쪽에 속하지만, 허용 범위다.

problem.passage:
Open-cell polymer foams are widely used to absorb sound, but engineers disagree about which mechanism accounts for most of the energy they remove from an incoming wave. One view holds that the dominant loss comes from viscous friction: as air is forced back and forth through the narrow, interconnected pores, it rubs against the pore walls and its kinetic energy is converted to heat. Materials scientist Leena Okafor proposes an alternative. She argues that in foams with relatively flexible struts, the dominant loss instead comes from the solid skeleton itself, which flexes with each pressure cycle and dissipates energy internally, so that the stiffness of the foam's frame—not the size of its pores—chiefly determines how much sound it absorbs.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: Open-cell polymer foams are widely used to absorb sound, but engineers disagree about which mechanism accounts for most of the energy they remove from an incoming wave. One view holds that the dominant loss comes from viscous friction: as air is forced back and forth through the narrow, interconnected pores, it rubs against the pore walls and its kinetic energy is converted to heat. Materials scientist Leena Okafor proposes an alternative. She argues that in foams with relatively flexible struts, the dominant loss instead comes from the solid skeleton itself, which flexes with each pressure cycle and dissipates energy internally, so that the stiffness of the foam's frame—not the size of its pores—chiefly determines how much sound it absorbs.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
options: When two flexible-strut foams with identical frame stiffness but different pore sizes were tested, the foam with narrower pores absorbed noticeably more sound energy.
When two flexible-strut foams with identical pore sizes but different frame stiffness were tested, the foam with the softer frame absorbed noticeably more sound energy.
When a flexible-strut foam was heated slightly during testing, its temperature rose by a measurable amount, showing that absorbed sound energy had been converted to heat.
When flexible-strut foams were compared with rigid-strut foams of similar thickness, both types absorbed more sound at high frequencies than at low frequencies.
problem.explanation: Okafor은 유연한 골격 폼에서 흡음량을 주로 결정하는 것이 기공 크기가 아니라 골격의 강성이라고 주장한다. B는 기공 크기를 같게 고정하고 강성만 바꿨을 때 흡음량이 달라졌음을 보여 주므로 이 주장을 가장 직접적으로 뒷받침한다. A는 기공 크기가 흡음을 좌우한다는 결과이므로 오히려 경쟁 견해인 점성 마찰 쪽을 지지한다. C의 열 변환은 두 메커니즘 모두에서 일어나므로 둘을 구별하지 못한다. D는 두 종류의 폼이 비슷하게 행동했다는 결과일 뿐 강성의 역할을 따로 떼어 보여 주지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Okafor claims that in flexible-strut foams, the stiffness of the frame, not pore size, mainly determines how much sound is absorbed. B keeps pore size fixed and changes only stiffness, and absorption changes, so it most directly supports her claim. A shows pore size controlling absorption, which actually supports the competing viscous-friction view. C shows conversion to heat, but both mechanisms produce heat, so it can't tell them apart. D only shows the two foam types behaving similarly across frequencies, so it doesn't isolate the role of stiffness.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 검산: Okafor의 주장은 '기공 크기가 아니라 골격 강성이 흡음을 결정'이며, B는 기공 크기를 통제하고 강성만 변화시켜 흡음량 차이를 보였고, 더 유연한 골격이 더 많이 흡수한다는 방향도 가설(골격이 휘며 에너지 소산)과 일치한다. A는 구조가 B와 평행하여 훑어 읽으면 혼동되는 매력적 오답이며 실제로는 경쟁 견해를 지지한다. C는 열 변환이 두 메커니즘 공통이므로 구별 불가, D는 강성을 분리하지 못함. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조이며 한글 혼입 없음. 가상의 연구자명 사용, 저작권 의심 없음. 두 단계 판단(주장 파악 + 통제 변인 확인)이 요구되어 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: B는 기공 크기를 고정한 채 강성만 바꾼 통제 비교이고, 더 부드러운 골격이 더 많이 휘어 에너지를 더 잃는다는 방향도 가설과 맞으므로 정답으로 타당하다. A는 반대 견해를 지지하는 함정으로 잘 작동한다. 사소한 점: C의 'heated slightly during testing'은 외부에서 가열했다는 뜻으로 읽힐 수 있다. 그러면 온도 상승이 당연한 결과가 되어 선택지 논리가 어색하다. 'its temperature rose slightly during testing' 정도가 더 자연스럽다. 정답 판정에는 영향이 없다.

problem.passage:
In a press interview, physical chemist Lena Okafor described her team's simulations of dissolved ions as "nothing that would surprise a first-year student": water molecules turn their oppositely charged ends toward each ion, forming a hydration shell, and this attraction releases energy. The paper's data, however, tell a more complicated story. For several large ions, the simulations showed that forming the hydration shell absorbed slightly more energy than it released. Dissolution happened only because the breakup of the orderly crystal raised entropy enough to make up the difference. Okafor's team gave this entropy analysis the longest section of the paper, and the paper's final figure sets its results directly beside the energy diagram printed in a widely used introductory chemistry textbook.

Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about Okafor's remark in the interview?
problem.stimulus: In a press interview, physical chemist Lena Okafor described her team's simulations of dissolved ions as "nothing that would surprise a first-year student": water molecules turn their oppositely charged ends toward each ion, forming a hydration shell, and this attraction releases energy. The paper's data, however, tell a more complicated story. For several large ions, the simulations showed that forming the hydration shell absorbed slightly more energy than it released. Dissolution happened only because the breakup of the orderly crystal raised entropy enough to make up the difference. Okafor's team gave this entropy analysis the longest section of the paper, and the paper's final figure sets its results directly beside the energy diagram printed in a widely used introductory chemistry textbook.
problem.question: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about Okafor's remark in the interview?
options: It accurately sums up the paper's central conclusion that water molecules turn toward each ion to form an energy-releasing hydration shell.
It shows that Okafor viewed the entropy findings as a minor detail that the textbook's energy diagram already explains.
It reflects the well-established principle that dissolving any ionic substance in water releases energy into its surroundings.
It understates results that the paper itself presents as a challenge to a standard introductory explanation of why ions dissolve.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: Okafor는 인터뷰에서 연구 결과가 "1학년 학생도 놀라지 않을 것"이라고 말했다. 그러나 논문을 보면 일부 큰 이온에서는 수화 껍질이 형성될 때 오히려 에너지가 흡수되었고, 용해는 엔트로피 증가 덕분에 일어났다. 또 논문은 이 엔트로피 분석에 가장 긴 절을 할애했고, 마지막 그림에서 결과를 입문 교과서의 에너지 도표와 바로 나란히 비교했다. 이런 구성은 논문 스스로 교과서 설명에 이의를 제기하고 있음을 보여 준다. 따라서 인터뷰 발언은 결과의 의미를 축소해 말한 것이다.
A(지문 문장 그대로 가져옴): 인터뷰에서 한 말을 그대로 옮겼을 뿐이다. 논문 데이터는 에너지를 방출한다는 그 설명과 어긋나므로 논문의 핵심 결론이라고 볼 수 없다.
B(어긋남을 반대로 해석): 논문은 엔트로피 분석을 가장 길게 다루고 교과서 도표와 직접 대조했다. 따라서 Okafor가 이를 사소한 세부로 여겼다거나 교과서가 이미 설명한다고 보았다는 추론은 근거가 반대 방향을 가리킨다.
C(지문과 무관한 일반 상식): 모든 용해가 에너지를 방출한다는 통념을 답으로 만든 것이다. 지문의 데이터는 오히려 이 통념에 맞는 반례를 제시한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, D: In the interview, Okafor says her results would not surprise a first-year student. But the paper shows something different. For some large ions, forming the hydration shell actually absorbed energy, and the ions dissolved only because entropy increased. The paper also gives this entropy analysis its longest section, and its final figure puts the results right beside a textbook energy diagram. That setup shows the paper is challenging the textbook explanation. So her interview remark plays down how significant the findings are.
A is wrong because it simply repeats what Okafor said in the interview. The paper's data contradict that energy-releasing account, so it can't be the paper's central conclusion.
B is wrong because it reads the mismatch backward. The paper gives the entropy findings the most space and compares them directly with the textbook. That doesn't suggest Okafor saw them as minor or as already explained by the textbook.
C is wrong because it turns a general belief into the answer. The passage's data actually contradict that belief: in some cases, dissolving absorbed energy.

hardJudge.note: 인터뷰의 '놀랄 것 없다'는 표면 진술과 논문의 실제 데이터(큰 이온의 흡열 수화, 엔트로피 주도 용해)·구성(엔트로피 절이 가장 김, 교과서 도표와 직접 대비) 사이의 어긋남을 종합해야만 D가 도출되며, 어떤 문장도 '축소했다'고 명시하지 않는다. A는 인터뷰 문장 그대로, B는 어긋남의 방향을 뒤집음, C는 외부 통념이라 오답 설계가 레시피에 부합한다. 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하고 모순 없음. 과학적으로 수화 껍질 형성 자체가 흡열이라는 설정은 다소 이례적이나 가상 시뮬레이션 결과로 제시되어 사실 오류로 보지 않음. C 해설의 '통념에 맞는 반례'는 '통념에 대한 반례'가 더 자연스러운 표현이나 논리에는 영향 없음.

advisory.note: 정답은 D다. 인터뷰 발언과 논문 데이터가 어긋나는 데다 논문이 엔트로피 분석에 가장 긴 절을 할애하고 결과를 교과서 도표와 나란히 대조하므로, 발언이 결과를 축소한다는 점이 추론으로만 도출된다. A는 인터뷰 진술을 옮긴 선택지이고, B는 어긋남의 방향을 뒤집은 선택지다. 오답들은 잘 설계되어 있다.

problem.passage:
Researchers testing semiconductor photocatalysts, such as titanium dioxide particles that break down organic pollutants in water when exposed to light, often compare materials by reporting how much of a dye disappears in a fixed time. Chemist Lena Okafor argues that such comparisons can be misleading unless they are based on quantum efficiency: the number of pollutant molecules degraded per photon actually absorbed by the catalyst. A slurry that scatters much of the incoming light, for example, may appear sluggish simply because fewer photons are absorbed, not because the material is chemically inferior. In Okafor's experiments, two catalysts that differed nearly threefold in dye removal per hour turned out to have almost identical quantum efficiencies once the absorbed light in each reactor was measured with chemical actinometry.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: Researchers testing semiconductor photocatalysts, such as titanium dioxide particles that break down organic pollutants in water when exposed to light, often compare materials by reporting how much of a dye disappears in a fixed time. Chemist Lena Okafor argues that such comparisons can be misleading unless they are based on quantum efficiency: the number of pollutant molecules degraded per photon actually absorbed by the catalyst. A slurry that scatters much of the incoming light, for example, may appear sluggish simply because fewer photons are absorbed, not because the material is chemically inferior. In Okafor's experiments, two catalysts that differed nearly threefold in dye removal per hour turned out to have almost identical quantum efficiencies once the absorbed light in each reactor was measured with chemical actinometry.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Judging photocatalysts by how quickly they remove pollutants can misrepresent their performance, so their activity should instead be evaluated relative to the light they actually absorb.
When two photocatalysts differ in how quickly they remove dye, the slower one typically scatters more light than it absorbs.
Removal rates are unreliable for comparing any chemical process, so measurements of quantum efficiency should replace them across chemistry.
Photocatalysts that scatter light degrade pollutants more slowly per absorbed photon, which is why quantum efficiency is a better standard than removal rate.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 지문의 넓은 주장(제거 속도 비교는 오해를 낳을 수 있으니 흡수된 광자 기준의 양자효율로 비교해야 한다)을 적절한 범위로 진술하며, 산란 예시와 실험은 이를 뒷받침하는 세부이다.
B(과잉축소·과잉일반화): 산란 예시라는 하나의 세부를 전체 요지로 삼고, 느린 촉매가 '대체로' 산란이 많다는 지문에 없는 일반화까지 한다.
C(과잉확장): 지문은 광촉매 비교만 다루며 화학 전반의 모든 공정으로 확장하지 않는다.
D(범위 혼합·왜곡): 넓은 주장과 세부를 뒤섞으면서, 산란이 흡수 광자당 효율을 낮춘다고 잘못 진술한다. 지문은 산란 때문에 흡수되는 광자 수가 줄어 느려 '보일' 뿐이며, 화학적으로 열등한 것은 아니라고 한다.
problem.explanationEn:
A is correct because it states the text's broad claim at the right scope: comparing photocatalysts by how fast they remove pollutants can be misleading, so they should be compared by quantum efficiency, which is measured per absorbed photon. The scattering example and Okafor's experiment are details that support this claim.
B is too narrow. It treats the scattering example as if it were the whole point. It also adds a generalization the text never makes: that slower catalysts usually scatter more light.
C goes too far. The text is only about comparing photocatalysts, not about every chemical process in chemistry.
D mixes the claim with a detail and gets the detail wrong. According to the text, scattering lowers the number of photons absorbed, which makes a catalyst look slow. It does not lower the efficiency per absorbed photon.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 넓은 주장(제거 속도 비교는 오해 소지가 있으므로 흡수 광자 기준 양자효율로 평가해야 함)과 세부(산란 예시, 3배 차이 촉매의 동일 양자효율 실험)를 모두 갖추고 있으며, A가 이를 적절한 범위로 포괄한다. B는 산란 세부에 '대체로'라는 지문 외 일반화를 더한 과잉축소, C는 화학 전반으로의 과잉확장, D는 '느려 보이는 것'과 '화학적 열등'을 혼동한 왜곡으로 각각 기능한다. 특히 D는 표면 진술(느린 제거 속도)과 실제 의미(흡수 광자 부족일 뿐 효율은 동일)의 차이를 인식해야 배제되므로 단순 요약을 넘어선 사고를 요구한다. 해설은 정답·오답 근거를 정확히 제시하며 모순 없음. TiO2 광촉매·화학 광량계 등 사실관계도 문제없고, 가상의 연구자를 사용한 창작 지문으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: D는 '느려 보임 vs 실제 효율 동일'이라는 표면-실제 구분을 이해해야 배제 가능한 매력적 오답. C는 비교적 쉽게 걸러지는 과잉확장.

problem.passage:
Engineers have long ranked ceramics for thermal shock resistance by a single test: heat a sample, plunge it into cold water, and record the temperature difference at which it first cracks. By this measure, dense alumina outperforms many porous ceramics, since its high strength lets it survive larger sudden drops. __Yet a material that survives one severe quench may still fail after hundreds of milder ones, because each cycle can extend microscopic flaws without producing any visible crack.__ Porous ceramics, whose pores blunt the tips of growing cracks, often outlast dense alumina in furnace linings that are heated and cooled daily. For such applications, then, a ranking based on a single quench may point engineers toward precisely the wrong material.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Engineers have long ranked ceramics for thermal shock resistance by a single test: heat a sample, plunge it into cold water, and record the temperature difference at which it first cracks. By this measure, dense alumina outperforms many porous ceramics, since its high strength lets it survive larger sudden drops. __Yet a material that survives one severe quench may still fail after hundreds of milder ones, because each cycle can extend microscopic flaws without producing any visible crack.__ Porous ceramics, whose pores blunt the tips of growing cracks, often outlast dense alumina in furnace linings that are heated and cooled daily. For such applications, then, a ranking based on a single quench may point engineers toward precisely the wrong material.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It identifies a limitation of the single-quench test that the following evidence about porous ceramics illustrates and that leads to the text's closing judgment.
It explains why dense alumina performs well in the single-quench test that the text describes in its opening sentences.
It presents evidence that porous ceramics blunt crack tips, a property that allows them to last longer in furnace linings.
It states the text's main purpose, which is to recommend porous ceramics over dense alumina for all high-temperature uses.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 단일 급랭 시험의 한계(반복 사이클에서 미세 결함 누적)를 제기하고, 이어지는 다공성 세라믹 사례가 이를 구체화하며, 마지막 문장의 결론(단일 급랭 순위는 잘못된 재료를 고르게 할 수 있음)으로 이어진다. 두 단계 이상을 연결해야 하는 역할이다.
B(한 단계만 본 역할): 알루미나가 급랭 시험에 강한 이유는 앞 문장(높은 강도)에서 설명되며, 밑줄 문장은 오히려 그 평가를 제한한다.
C(인접 문장과 혼동): 기공이 균열 끝을 무디게 한다는 근거는 다음 문장의 내용이다.
D(전체 목적과 문장 기능 뒤바꿈/과장): 밑줄 문장은 전체 결론 자체가 아니며, 지문은 '모든' 고온 용도가 아니라 매일 가열·냉각되는 용도에 한정해 말한다.
problem.explanationEn:
A is correct. The underlined sentence starts with "Yet" and points out a limitation of the single-quench test: repeated mild cycles can slowly extend flaws even when a sample survives one severe quench. The next sentence about porous ceramics gives a concrete example of this, and the final sentence draws the conclusion that a single-quench ranking can point engineers to the wrong material. To see the sentence's role, you have to connect all three steps.
B is wrong because the reason alumina does well on the test (its high strength) appears in the sentence before. The underlined sentence actually limits how much that result should count.
C is wrong because the evidence that pores blunt crack tips comes in the sentence after the underlined one.
D is wrong because the underlined sentence is not the text's overall conclusion. The text also never recommends porous ceramics for all uses. It only discusses applications like furnace linings that are heated and cooled daily.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 '기존 단일 시험 → 알루미나 우위(근거) → Yet 한계 제기(밑줄) → 다공성 세라믹 사례(근거) → 단일 시험 순위가 잘못될 수 있음(결론)'의 다단계 구조를 갖추고 있다. 정답 A는 밑줄 문장이 뒤따르는 근거와 최종 결론을 연결하는 전환점임을 정확히 기술하며, 밑줄 문장만 읽어서는 확정되지 않고 이후 두 문장과의 관계를 통합해야 한다. B는 앞 문장의 역할(알루미나의 강점 설명)을, C는 뒤 문장의 역할(기공의 균열 무디게 하기)을 밑줄 문장에 귀속시킨 인접 단계 혼동형이고, D는 지문 전체 목적을 문장 기능으로 바꾸면서 'all'로 범위를 과장한 오답이다. 해설은 각 오답의 기각 이유를 정확히 제시하며 모순이 없다. 과학적 내용(반복 열사이클에 의한 미세 결함 성장, 다공성 내화재의 열충격 저항성)도 일반적으로 타당하다. 문장 길이는 적정하며 난이도는 논리 단계 연결에서 나온다. hard 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 한계 제기→사례→결론의 3단계 연결을 요구함. B는 앞 문장, C는 뒤 문장의 역할을 가져온 오답이고, D는 범위를 과장하고 전체 목적과 뒤바꾼 오답. 다만 'Yet' 신호어 때문에 정답이 다소 쉽게 드러날 수 있음.

problem.passage:
When two different metals are bonded and heated, their atoms migrate across the interface, and they rarely do so at equal rates. In copper–zinc couples, for example, zinc atoms diffuse into copper faster than copper atoms diffuse into zinc, so vacancies pile up on the zinc-rich side and can merge into tiny pores known as Kirkendall voids. Materials engineer Priya Raman treats these voids strictly as defects: in solder joints for electronics, she argues, they concentrate stress and cause cracks, so alloy pairs should be chosen to keep diffusion rates as balanced as possible. Chemist Tomás Ibarra studies the same imbalance for a different purpose. By deliberately heating metal nanoparticles coated with a second element, his team lets the faster-moving core atoms escape outward, leaving behind hollow nanospheres whose large interior surfaces are useful in catalysis. __For Ibarra, then, an unequal diffusion rate is not a mismatch to be engineered away but a parameter to be tuned.__

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: When two different metals are bonded and heated, their atoms migrate across the interface, and they rarely do so at equal rates. In copper–zinc couples, for example, zinc atoms diffuse into copper faster than copper atoms diffuse into zinc, so vacancies pile up on the zinc-rich side and can merge into tiny pores known as Kirkendall voids. Materials engineer Priya Raman treats these voids strictly as defects: in solder joints for electronics, she argues, they concentrate stress and cause cracks, so alloy pairs should be chosen to keep diffusion rates as balanced as possible. Chemist Tomás Ibarra studies the same imbalance for a different purpose. By deliberately heating metal nanoparticles coated with a second element, his team lets the faster-moving core atoms escape outward, leaving behind hollow nanospheres whose large interior surfaces are useful in catalysis. __For Ibarra, then, an unequal diffusion rate is not a mismatch to be engineered away but a parameter to be tuned.__
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It suggests that Ibarra would agree with Raman's recommendation to balance diffusion rates, since hollow nanospheres also form most reliably when atoms migrate evenly.
It implies that Ibarra would reject Raman's recommendation as a general rule, since the very imbalance she seeks to minimize is what his technique depends on.
It indicates that Raman's concern about stress in solder joints is the main reason Ibarra began controlling diffusion in nanoparticles.
It proposes that Raman and Ibarra should collaborate to develop solder joints containing hollow nanospheres that resist cracking.
problem.explanation:
정답 B: Raman은 확산 속도 불균형을 결함 원인으로 보고 균형을 맞추라고 권하지만, 밑줄 문장은 Ibarra에게 그 불균형이 '제거할 것'이 아니라 '조절할 변수'임을 밝힌다. 따라서 Ibarra는 Raman의 권고를 보편 원칙으로 받아들이지 않을 것임을 간접적으로 드러낸다.
A(입장 뒤바꿈): Ibarra의 기법은 불균형에 의존하므로 균등 확산에 동의한다는 것은 반대 서술이다.
C(한쪽 입장만 사용): Raman의 응력 우려만 근거로 삼아 Ibarra 연구의 동기를 꾸며냈으며, 지문은 두 연구의 인과관계를 말하지 않는다.
D(새 반응 날조): 협업이나 나노구체 솔더 개발은 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer B: Raman sees unequal diffusion rates as a cause of defects and recommends balancing them. The underlined sentence shows that, for Ibarra, the imbalance is a variable to adjust, not something to eliminate. So it indirectly signals that Ibarra would not accept Raman's recommendation as a universal rule, because his hollow nanospheres depend on that imbalance.
A reverses the stances. Ibarra's method requires uneven migration, so he wouldn't endorse even diffusion for his own work.
C relies only on Raman's position to invent a reason for Ibarra's research. The text never links the two lines of work causally.
D makes up a new response. The text says nothing about collaboration or solder joints containing nanospheres.

hardJudge.note: Raman(불균형=결함, 균형 권고)과 Ibarra(불균형=조절 변수) 두 입장이 명확히 대비되고, 밑줄 문장은 "engineered away"로 Raman의 권고를 직접 환기하며 Ibarra의 암묵적 반응을 드러낸다. B의 "as a general rule" 한정은 솔더 접합 맥락에서의 동의 가능성을 배제하여 정답을 방어 가능하게 만든다. A는 입장 뒤바꿈, C는 Raman 쪽만 근거로 삼은 인과 날조, D는 지문 밖 협업 날조로 체크리스트 전부 충족. Kirkendall 효과(Cu–Zn에서 Zn가 더 빨리 확산, 나노스케일 Kirkendall로 중공 나노입자 합성)는 과학적으로 정확. 연구자는 가상 인물로 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 밑줄 문장은 Raman의 '균형화' 권고와 대비해 Ibarra가 이를 보편 원칙으로 받아들이지 않을 것임을 함축하므로 B가 타당하다. 반면 C·D는 지문과의 연결이 약해 쉽게 제외되어 변별력이 다소 낮다. 판정의 실질은 A(입장 역전)와 B의 구분에 있다.

problem.passage:
Materials scientists often report a liquid's contact angle—the angle a droplet forms where it meets a solid—as if it were a fixed property of the solid's chemistry. Yet the same chemistry can produce very different angles depending on surface texture. Physicist Lena Okafor and colleagues tested how far texture matters by coating silicon wafers with an identical fluoropolymer and then etching them to different roughness levels. __On the smoothest wafers, water beaded at about 110 degrees, but on wafers etched to the highest roughness, the angle climbed above 150 degrees, even though the coating's chemistry was unchanged across all samples.__ The team cautions that this finding concerns water-repelling coatings specifically; for surfaces whose chemistry attracts water, theory predicts that roughness should instead lower the angle. Still, the researchers argue, any contact angle reported without a description of surface texture cannot be taken as a reliable measure of a coating's chemistry alone.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Materials scientists often report a liquid's contact angle—the angle a droplet forms where it meets a solid—as if it were a fixed property of the solid's chemistry. Yet the same chemistry can produce very different angles depending on surface texture. Physicist Lena Okafor and colleagues tested how far texture matters by coating silicon wafers with an identical fluoropolymer and then etching them to different roughness levels. __On the smoothest wafers, water beaded at about 110 degrees, but on wafers etched to the highest roughness, the angle climbed above 150 degrees, even though the coating's chemistry was unchanged across all samples.__ The team cautions that this finding concerns water-repelling coatings specifically; for surfaces whose chemistry attracts water, theory predicts that roughness should instead lower the angle. Still, the researchers argue, any contact angle reported without a description of surface texture cannot be taken as a reliable measure of a coating's chemistry alone.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a result showing that roughness raises contact angles on every kind of surface, regardless of whether the coating attracts or repels water.
It presents a result showing only that the fluoropolymer coating produced a high contact angle, leaving the role of etching unaddressed.
It presents a result showing that texture alone can substantially alter a measured contact angle, which supports the researchers' warning that unreported texture undermines such measurements.
It presents a result showing that a coating's chemistry determines how rough the wafer becomes during etching, which explains the changes in contact angle.
problem.explanation: 정답 C: 밑줄 문장은 화학 조성을 고정하고 거칠기만 바꿨을 때 접촉각이 약 110°에서 150° 이상으로 달라졌다는 결과를 보여 준다. 따라서 질감만으로도 측정값이 크게 바뀔 수 있음을 보여 주며, 마지막 문장의 결론(질감 정보 없이 보고된 접촉각은 화학적 특성의 신뢰할 만한 척도가 아니다)과 범위가 정확히 일치한다. A(과장): 지문은 이 결과가 발수 코팅에만 해당한다고 명시하고, 친수 표면에서는 거칠기가 접촉각을 오히려 낮춘다고 예측하므로 '모든 표면'으로 일반화할 수 없다. B(좁은 해석): 이 문장의 핵심은 매끈한 웨이퍼와 거친 웨이퍼의 비교인데, B는 코팅이 높은 각도를 만들었다는 점만 보고 거칠기의 역할을 빠뜨린다. D(인과 역전): 실험은 거칠기를 독립적으로 조절했고 화학 조성은 고정했다. 화학 조성이 거칠기를 결정한다는 설명은 지문에 없으며 인과 관계를 잘못 설정한 것이다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct. The underlined sentence describes an experiment in which the chemistry stayed fixed and only the roughness changed. The contact angle still rose from about 110 degrees to above 150 degrees. This shows that texture alone can shift the measurement substantially, which is exactly what supports the final claim: a contact angle reported without texture information can't be trusted as a measure of chemistry alone. The scope of the evidence matches the scope of the conclusion. A is wrong because it overstates the result. The text limits the finding to water-repelling coatings and notes that roughness should lower the angle on water-attracting surfaces. B is wrong because it reads the evidence too narrowly. The key point is the comparison between smooth and rough wafers, and B ignores the role of etching. D is wrong because it reverses the cause and effect. The researchers controlled roughness directly while keeping the chemistry constant, and nothing in the text suggests that chemistry determines roughness.

advisory.note: A는 지문의 단서(발수 코팅에 한정되고, 친수 표면에서는 거칠기가 접촉각을 낮춘다는 예측)를 이용한 범위 과장 함정으로 잘 설계되었다. 반면 B는 밑줄 문장이 거칠기를 직접 비교하고 있어 쉽게 배제되므로 오답으로서의 매력이 약하다. D는 인과를 잘못 설정한 오답으로는 기능하지만, 엄밀한 의미의 방향 역전은 아니다.

problem.passage:
From the fifteenth to the seventeenth century, Venice's silk guild imposed strict rules on its members: weavers had to use a fixed number of warp threads per cloth, dye only with approved materials, and submit finished pieces to inspectors who stamped those that met the standard. Historians once treated these regulations mainly as tools for shutting out competitors and keeping prices high. Economic historian Luca Molà, however, argues that the rules served a different purpose. Because buyers in distant markets such as Constantinople and Antwerp could not examine every bolt before purchase, the guild's stamp functioned as a guarantee of quality, allowing Venetian silk to command trust—and premium prices—far from the city where it was made. In Molà's view, the restrictions that seem to limit producers actually created the reputation on which their foreign sales depended.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Venetian silk guild regulations mainly kept outside competitors from entering the luxury textile trade, which allowed members to keep prices high.
Venetian silk guild regulations required weavers to follow detailed technical rules, which made production slower and more costly than in rival cities.
Venetian silk guild regulations were enforced most strictly on goods bound for Constantinople and Antwerp, which were the city's most demanding markets.
Venetian silk guild regulations, though they restricted weavers, gave distant buyers a reliable signal of quality that supported the city's export trade.
problem.explanation: 지문은 길드 규제를 경쟁 차단 수단으로 보던 기존 견해를 소개한 뒤, 몰라가 이 규제와 검사 도장이 먼 시장의 구매자에게 품질 보증 역할을 하여 수출을 뒷받침했다고 주장한다고 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 지문이 반박하는 과거 역사가들의 견해일 뿐 글의 중심 생각이 아니다. B는 세부 기술 규칙은 맞게 언급하지만 생산이 느려지고 비용이 늘었다는 내용은 지문에 없다. C는 지문에 나온 시장 이름을 쓰지만 그 시장으로 가는 물품에 규제가 더 엄격했다는 내용은 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text introduces an older view that the guild's rules were meant to shut out competitors, then presents Molà's argument that the rules and inspection stamps assured distant buyers of quality and so supported Venice's export trade, which makes D correct. A just restates the earlier historians' view, which the text sets up in order to challenge it, so it isn't the main idea. B correctly mentions the technical rules, but the text never says they made production slower or more costly. C names markets that appear in the text, but nothing suggests the rules were enforced more strictly for goods headed there.

quality.seed: economics and business — Venetian silk monopoly and guild regulation of luxury textile production fifteenth to seventeenth centuries

hardJudge.note: 지문 구조(기존 견해 → Molà의 반론)와 D가 정확히 일치. A는 지문에 등장하는 기존 역사가 견해라 훑어 읽으면 고를 수 있는 강한 오답, B·C는 지문의 세부(기술 규칙, 시장 이름)를 차용했으나 근거 없는 추가 주장으로 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 글자 참조가 일치하고 영어 자연스러움. Luca Molà의 실제 연구(베네치아 르네상스 비단 산업)와 부합하며 지문은 독자적 서술로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: A는 기존 견해를 담은 강한 함정이고 B와 C는 지문 세부를 활용한 오답이다. 정답 D를 고르려면 기존 견해와 몰라의 반론을 대비해 읽어야 하므로 medium 난이도에 적합하다. 몰라는 베네치아 비단 산업을 연구한 실존 역사가이며, 품질 보증이라는 해석도 그럴듯한 내용이다.

problem.passage:
From 1716 to 1845, Scotland had no central bank and no single authority controlling the supply of paper money. Instead, dozens of private banks issued their own notes, which circulated side by side. Some economists have assumed that such an arrangement would invite reckless overissue, since each bank could profit by printing more notes. Historian Lawrence H. White argues, however, that the Scottish system largely policed itself. Banks routinely accepted one another's notes and then, through a regular note exchange, presented them back to the issuing bank for payment in gold or silver. A bank that issued too many notes therefore quickly found its reserves drained by its rivals, giving every bank a strong incentive to issue cautiously. White points out that Scottish bank failures in this period imposed relatively small losses on noteholders compared with failures in England, where note issue was more tightly restricted.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although Scottish banks during the free banking era issued notes without central oversight, they frequently overissued them, leading to more failures than occurred in England.

problem.explanation: 이 지문은 중앙 권한 없이도 경쟁 은행들이 서로의 지폐를 상환 요구하며 과잉 발행을 억제했다는 White의 주장이 핵심이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 '경제학자들의 추정'을 사실로 오인했고, 지문은 오히려 손실이 더 작았다고 말한다. C는 상환 관행이 언급되지만 그 목적을 경쟁자 퇴출로 왜곡했으며, 지문에서 그것은 신중한 발행의 유인으로 제시된다. D는 잉글랜드와의 비교를 거꾸로 해석했는데, 지문은 스코틀랜드의 손실이 더 작았다고 한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text's central point is White's argument that, even without a central authority, competition among Scottish banks, especially returning one another's notes for redemption, kept note issue in check, so B is correct. A takes the economists' assumption as fact, but the text says Scottish failures actually caused smaller losses. C mentions the redemption practice but misstates its purpose. In the text, this practice gives banks a reason to issue cautiously, not a way to drive competitors out of business. D reverses the comparison with England: the text says noteholders lost less in Scotland.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B는 지문의 핵심(White의 주장: 상호 상환 관행이 과잉 발행 억제)을 정확히 요약. A는 경제학자 추정을 사실로, D는 잉글랜드 비교를 역전, C는 상환 관행의 목적을 왜곡 — 각 오답이 지문 일부를 근거로 삼아 비교가 필요하므로 medium 적합. 해설 한/영 일치, 글자 참조 정확. 역사적 내용(White의 스코틀랜드 자유은행 연구)도 사실과 부합.
