problem.passage:
When the United Nations imposed sanctions on Rhodesia in the late 1960s, the country's tobacco growers lost open access to their largest buyers almost overnight. Many observers predicted that the industry would collapse, since tobacco had been the colony's leading export. Instead, production continued for more than a decade. The government created a state agency that bought the entire crop each season at guaranteed prices and then sold it abroad through intermediaries who disguised its origin, often relabeling it as tobacco from neighboring countries. At the same time, the agency paid some farmers to plant maize, cotton, and wheat instead of tobacco, shrinking a surplus that could no longer be sold easily. These measures kept farms operating, but they came at a cost: secret sales typically fetched well below prewar prices, and the industry survived largely because the state absorbed the losses.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.explanationEn: The text says that, contrary to predictions of collapse, the industry kept going thanks to a state agency that bought the whole crop, sold it secretly, and paid some farmers to switch crops. It also notes the cost: lower prices and losses covered by the state. B captures both parts, so it is correct. A repeats the observers' prediction, but the text says production actually continued. C stretches a detail about some farmers switching crops, and the text never says those crops became leading exports. D gets the disguised sales right, but the text says those sales earned well below prewar prices, not more.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B는 '유지되었으나 대가(낮은 가격·국가 손실 부담)'라는 지문의 두 축을 모두 포착하여 타당. A는 예측(실제와 반대), C는 세부 과장, D는 가격 진술과 모순으로 모두 적절히 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 글자 참조가 일치하고 한글 혼입 없음. 역사적 사실(1960년대 후반 UN 제재, 담배가 주요 수출품, 국가 기관 매입 및 원산지 위장 판매, 작물 다각화)과 부합. 사소한 표현상 문제: 지문의 "prewar prices"는 제재 상황을 다루는 맥락에서 "pre-sanction"이 더 자연스러우며, 독립선언(1965) 이후 시기를 "colony"로 칭한 점도 다소 느슨함(채점에 영향 없음).

advisory.note: 정답 B가 옳다. 지문은 산업이 살아남았다는 점과 그 대가(낮은 가격, 국가의 손실 부담)를 함께 말하며, B만 두 부분을 모두 담고 있다. 오답 C와 D는 지문의 세부 내용(작물 전환, 원산지 위장 판매)을 일부 맞게 쓰면서 핵심을 왜곡하고, A는 관찰자들의 예측을 그대로 옮긴 그럴듯한 함정이다. 그래서 medium 난이도에 적합하다. 다만 오답의 핵심 표현(collapsed, replaced, prospered)이 지문과 정면으로 어긋나 비교적 쉽게 배제되므로, 하한선 수준의 medium으로 판정한다. 사소한 점으로, 지문의 'prewar prices'는 제재 이전 가격을 뜻하려는 것으로 보이지만 전쟁 맥락이 없어 어색하다. 'pre-sanctions prices'로 쓰는 편이 정확하다. 역사적 개요(1960년대 후반 UN 제재, 국가 기관의 일괄 매입, 원산지 위장 판매, 작물 다각화 장려)는 대체로 사실과 맞다.

problem.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, Antwerp dominated the world's diamond trade not because any single firm controlled the business but because thousands of small, specialized firms operated within a few city blocks. Cutters, polishers, brokers, and dealers worked within walking distance of one another, so a rough stone could pass through several independent hands in a single day, and reputations built through repeated face-to-face dealings allowed deals worth millions to be sealed with a handshake. Economists have often cited this arrangement as a textbook example of how geographic clustering can substitute for the coordination that a large, vertically integrated company would otherwise provide internally.

Since the 1990s, however, that model has come under strain. Major mining companies have increasingly sought to control their stones from mine to retail counter, sending rough diamonds directly to their own cutting facilities, many of them in India, where labor costs are lower. As a result, the advantages that Antwerp's dense network once offered have mattered less, and the city's role has shifted toward trading and certification rather than cutting itself.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

quality.seed: economics and business — Belgian diamond cutting industry clustering in Antwerp and vertical integration of supply chains

hardJudge.note: C는 두 단락(클러스터가 수직 통합 기업의 조정 기능을 대체 → 광산 기업의 공급망 통제로 이점 약화)을 정확히 종합한다. A는 지문에 있는 악수 거래 세부 사항을 근거로 하되 '정식 계약보다 효율적'이라는 비교를 덧붙여 과잉 진술, B는 인도·1990년대라는 지문 요소를 포함하되 원인(기술 우위)을 잘못 제시, D는 둘째 단락과 정면 배치된다. 오답 중 둘이 부분 근거를 가지며, 정답 도출에 두 단락의 연결이 필요하므로 medium에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조와 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 앤트워프 다이아몬드 산업 서술(소규모 전문 업체 집적, 1990년대 이후 광산 기업의 수직 통합과 인도 연마 이전, 거래·감정 중심으로 전환)은 실제 역사와 부합. 지문은 독창적 서술로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: C는 두 단락을 모두 요약한다. A와 B는 지문 속 세부 사항(악수 거래, 인도)에 지문에 없는 주장을 덧붙였다. D는 둘째 단락과 정면으로 모순되어 다소 쉽게 배제되지만, 전체적으로 medium에 적합하다. 다만 '1990s'를 B에 넣어 훑어 읽는 응시자를 유인하려는 장치는 약한 편이다.

problem.passage:
In the early twentieth century, the Philippines became one of the world's leading suppliers of copra, the dried coconut meat pressed for oil used in soap, margarine, and explosives. Colonial-era trade rules gave Philippine coconut oil tariff-free access to the United States, and by the 1920s a small number of mills in Manila controlled much of the export trade. Many observers assumed that this concentration would let the mill owners dictate prices and shield the industry from outside shocks. Yet the mills' control extended only to processing within the islands. The price they could charge abroad was set by competition with palm oil from West Africa, soybean oil from Manchuria, and whale oil from Norwegian fleets, all of which buyers could substitute when coconut oil grew expensive. When a postwar boom collapsed in 1920, export prices fell by more than half within two years, and the Manila mills, despite their dominance at home, could do nothing to halt the decline.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: In the early twentieth century, the Philippines became one of the world's leading suppliers of copra, the dried coconut meat pressed for oil used in soap, margarine, and explosives. Colonial-era trade rules gave Philippine coconut oil tariff-free access to the United States, and by the 1920s a small number of mills in Manila controlled much of the export trade. Many observers assumed that this concentration would let the mill owners dictate prices and shield the industry from outside shocks. Yet the mills' control extended only to processing within the islands. The price they could charge abroad was set by competition with palm oil from West Africa, soybean oil from Manchuria, and whale oil from Norwegian fleets, all of which buyers could substitute when coconut oil grew expensive. When a postwar boom collapsed in 1920, export prices fell by more than half within two years, and the Manila mills, despite their dominance at home, could do nothing to halt the decline.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Tariff-free access to the United States allowed Philippine coconut oil mills to outcompete rival producers of palm, soybean, and whale oil during the 1920s.
Philippine coconut oil exporters suffered after 1920 mainly because a few Manila mills held so much of the trade that smaller producers were driven out.
Philippine coconut oil prices fell sharply after 1920 because buyers in the United States lost interest in soap, margarine, and explosives after the war.
Although a few Manila mills dominated Philippine coconut oil processing, they could not protect prices abroad, where rival oils served as ready replacements.
problem.explanation: 지문은 마닐라의 소수 제분소가 국내 가공을 장악했지만, 해외 가격은 대체 가능한 다른 기름과의 경쟁으로 정해졌기 때문에 1920년 이후의 가격 폭락을 막지 못했다는 점을 핵심으로 다루므로 D가 정답이다. A는 관세 혜택이라는 세부 정보는 맞지만, 경쟁 기름을 이겼다는 주장은 지문 내용과 반대다. B는 시장 집중이라는 사실은 맞게 언급하지만, 그 집중이 소규모 생산자를 몰아내 피해를 줬다는 인과관계는 지문에 나오지 않는다. C는 가격 하락이라는 사실은 맞지만, 그 원인을 수요 상실로 돌린 것은 근거가 없다. 지문이 제시하는 원인은 전후 호황의 붕괴와 대체재와의 경쟁이다.
problem.explanationEn: D is correct because the passage's main point is that the Manila mills controlled processing at home but could not set prices abroad. Overseas, coconut oil competed with substitute oils, so the mills couldn't stop prices from collapsing after 1920. A gets the tariff detail right, but the passage never says the mills outcompeted rival oils; it says buyers switched to those oils whenever coconut oil got expensive. B correctly mentions that the trade was concentrated in a few mills, but it invents a cause the passage never states, namely that smaller producers were driven out. C correctly notes that prices fell, but it blames lost demand for soap and other products, which the passage doesn't say. The passage instead points to the end of the postwar boom and competition from substitute oils.

quality.seed: economics and business — Philippine coconut oil production monopoly and commodity price volatility in global markets

hardJudge.note: 지문의 핵심(국내 가공 장악 vs. 해외 가격 통제 불가, 대체재 경쟁)을 D가 정확히 요약함. A는 관세 세부는 맞으나 결론이 반대, B는 집중이라는 사실에 지문에 없는 인과를 붙임, C는 가격 하락은 맞으나 원인을 수요 상실로 왜곡함. 세 오답 모두 부분적 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하며 "Yet" 이후 전환을 정독해야 D가 확정되므로 medium에 적합. 한·영 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 역사적 사실(필리핀 코프라 수출, 무관세 접근, 1920년 전후 호황 붕괴, 팜유·대두유·고래기름 경쟁)도 타당함.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 지문의 대조 구조(국내 가공은 장악했지만 해외 가격은 통제하지 못함)와 정확히 맞는다. A, B, C는 각각 지문의 세부 정보(관세 혜택, 시장 집중, 가격 하락)를 일부 맞게 가져와서 잘못된 주장이나 지문에 없는 인과관계로 이어 붙인 오답이라 중간 난이도에 맞다. 지문은 약 170단어로 SAT 기준보다 다소 길다.

problem.passage:
Economists have long debated why South Korea's manufacturing sector expanded so rapidly between the 1960s and 1980s. One common account credits the chaebol, large family-controlled conglomerates such as Hyundai and Samsung, whose founders could move capital quickly from one affiliate to another and enter new industries without waiting for outside investors. __Yet the chaebol's ability to shift resources so freely depended heavily on the state, which directed low-interest loans from government-controlled banks toward firms that met strict export targets.__ Economist Alice Amsden has argued that this arrangement worked because support was conditional: firms that missed their targets could lose access to credit. On this view, Korea's growth reflected neither family ownership nor government planning alone but the discipline that each imposed on the other.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Economists have long debated why South Korea's manufacturing sector expanded so rapidly between the 1960s and 1980s. One common account credits the chaebol, large family-controlled conglomerates such as Hyundai and Samsung, whose founders could move capital quickly from one affiliate to another and enter new industries without waiting for outside investors. __Yet the chaebol's ability to shift resources so freely depended heavily on the state, which directed low-interest loans from government-controlled banks toward firms that met strict export targets.__ Economist Alice Amsden has argued that this arrangement worked because support was conditional: firms that missed their targets could lose access to credit. On this view, Korea's growth reflected neither family ownership nor government planning alone but the discipline that each imposed on the other.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that the chaebol's founders were reluctant to move into new industries without government approval.
It complicates an explanation introduced earlier by pointing to a condition on which the advantage that explanation emphasizes relied.
It rejects an explanation introduced earlier by showing that family ownership played no meaningful role in Korea's industrial growth.
It summarizes an explanation introduced earlier by restating the advantage that family control gave the chaebol in entering new industries.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 앞에서 소개한 설명(재벌의 신속한 자본 이동이 성장을 이끌었다)이 강조한 장점이 사실 국가의 조건부 신용 지원에 의존했음을 지적하여 그 설명을 복잡하게 만든다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 창업자들이 정부 승인 없이는 진출을 꺼렸다고 하지만 지문은 오히려 신속한 진출을 말한다. C는 가족 소유가 아무 역할도 없었다고 하지만 마지막 문장은 양쪽 모두의 역할을 인정하므로 지나치다. D는 앞 설명을 단순히 반복한다고 보지만 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 새로운 조건을 덧붙인다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and shows that the advantage stressed by the earlier account (the chaebol's quick movement of capital) actually depended on state-directed, conditional loans. That complicates the earlier explanation, so B is correct. A is wrong because the text says founders entered new industries quickly, and it never mentions them being reluctant. C goes too far: the final sentence credits family ownership and government together, so the text doesn't say ownership played no role. D misses the contrast signaled by "Yet," because the sentence adds a new condition and does more than repeat the earlier point.

quality.seed: economics and business — Korean chaebol family business structure and government industrial policy in manufacturing development

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 앞의 재벌 중심 설명을 보완·조건화하며, 마지막 문장이 양자의 상호 규율을 결론으로 제시하므로 '복잡하게 만든다(complicates)'가 정확. A는 지문과 반대(신속 진출), C는 과장(가족 소유 역할 부정은 마지막 문장과 모순), D는 'Yet'의 전환 무시. C·D는 부분적 근거(국가 역할 강조, 앞 설명 언급)를 가져 비교 필요. 아삼든(Amsden)의 조건부 지원 논지는 실제 학설과 일치. 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: B가 정답이다. 'Yet' 뒤 문장은 앞 설명의 장점인 자본의 자유로운 이동이 국가의 수출 조건부 대출에 의존했다고 밝힌다. 그래서 앞 설명을 뒤집지 않고 복잡하게 만든다. 앰스던의 상호 규율(reciprocity) 논지 설명은 사실과 맞다. 오답 C는 '반박'이라는 점에서 그럴듯한 함정이고, D는 앞 설명을 다시 언급한다는 점에서 부분적으로 맞는 근거가 있다. A는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 전체적으로 medium 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, Finland's paper and pulp companies outcompeted rivals in countries with far larger forests. Economists often attribute this success to vertical integration: firms such as UPM and Stora Enso came to control every stage of production, from timber harvesting to sawmills, pulp plants, and paper machines. __Yet integration alone cannot explain the industry's durability, since Swedish and Canadian firms adopted similar structures without matching Finland's consistency over decades.__ Historian Markku Kuisma points instead to the country's forest management regime, under which hundreds of thousands of small private landowners, guided by state-funded advisers, replanted harvested land on predictable cycles. This steady, renewable timber supply, Kuisma argues, is what allowed integrated mills to operate at full capacity year after year.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: For much of the twentieth century, Finland's paper and pulp companies outcompeted rivals in countries with far larger forests. Economists often attribute this success to vertical integration: firms such as UPM and Stora Enso came to control every stage of production, from timber harvesting to sawmills, pulp plants, and paper machines. __Yet integration alone cannot explain the industry's durability, since Swedish and Canadian firms adopted similar structures without matching Finland's consistency over decades.__ Historian Markku Kuisma points instead to the country's forest management regime, under which hundreds of thousands of small private landowners, guided by state-funded advisers, replanted harvested land on predictable cycles. This steady, renewable timber supply, Kuisma argues, is what allowed integrated mills to operate at full capacity year after year.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that Finnish firms copied an organizational structure first developed by competitors in Sweden and Canada.
It explains how the integrated structure described in the previous sentence helped Finnish firms achieve full production capacity.
It raises a limitation of a commonly offered account, setting up the introduction of an additional factor discussed afterward.
It identifies a weakness in Kuisma's argument by noting that other countries also had small private landowners.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작하여 경제학자들의 일반적 설명(수직 통합)만으로는 부족하다고 지적하고, 이어지는 문장에서 Kuisma의 산림 관리 체제라는 추가 요인이 소개되므로 C가 정답이다. A는 스웨덴·캐나다 기업이 언급되긴 하지만 핀란드가 이를 모방했다는 내용은 없다. B는 통합과 가동률을 연결하지만 그 연결은 마지막 문장의 Kuisma 논지이며, 밑줄 문장은 통합의 설명력을 오히려 제한한다. D는 밑줄 문장이 Kuisma보다 앞에 나오며 그의 주장을 비판하지 않고, 소규모 토지 소유자 이야기도 하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and points out that the common explanation, vertical integration, can't fully account for Finland's success, and the next sentence brings in Kuisma's forest-management factor. That makes C correct. A mentions Swedish and Canadian firms, but the text never says Finland copied them. B connects integration to full capacity, but that link comes from Kuisma in the last sentence, while the underlined sentence actually limits how much integration can explain. D is wrong because the underlined sentence comes before Kuisma's argument, doesn't criticize it, and says nothing about small landowners.

quality.seed: economics and business — Finnish paper and pulp industry dominance through forest management and vertical integration strategy

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 수직 통합 설명의 한계를 제시하고, 다음 문장에서 Kuisma의 산림 관리 체제라는 추가 요인으로 이어지므로 C가 정답임을 직접 확인. A(모방 주장 없음), B(통합→가동률 연결은 마지막 문장의 Kuisma 논지), D(밑줄 문장이 Kuisma보다 앞서며 비판 아님) 모두 올바르게 배제됨. 한·영 해설이 동일한 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. Stora Enso를 '핀란드 기업'으로 단순화한 점은 헬싱키 본사 기준으로 허용 범위. 'Yet' 신호어 파악 + 뒤 문장과의 연결이라는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 B·D가 본문 요소를 부분적으로 차용해 비교가 필요하므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 C가 명확하다. 오답 B는 통합과 가동률을 연결하고, A는 스웨덴·캐나다라는 실제 언급을 끌어와 그럴듯하며, D는 Kuisma를 끌어들여 부분적 근거를 가진다. medium 난이도에 적합하다. 다만 Kuisma 실존 인물의 구체적 주장은 지문 설정으로 보는 것이 무방하다.

problem.passage:
In the early twentieth century, the mining company LKAB built Kiruna, a town in Sweden's far north, to house the workers who extracted its iron ore. Like many company towns, Kiruna gave its employer unusual control: LKAB owned the land, designed the streets, and financed the schools and churches. Historians have often assumed that such arrangements left workers with little bargaining power. __Yet Kiruna's miners organized one of the longest strikes in modern Swedish history in 1969–1970, winning concessions on pay structure and working conditions without the backing of their national union.__ Some scholars now argue that the town's very isolation and the shared dependence of residents on a single employer fostered a tight solidarity that made such collective action possible.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In the early twentieth century, the mining company LKAB built Kiruna, a town in Sweden's far north, to house the workers who extracted its iron ore. Like many company towns, Kiruna gave its employer unusual control: LKAB owned the land, designed the streets, and financed the schools and churches. Historians have often assumed that such arrangements left workers with little bargaining power. __Yet Kiruna's miners organized one of the longest strikes in modern Swedish history in 1969–1970, winning concessions on pay structure and working conditions without the backing of their national union.__ Some scholars now argue that the town's very isolation and the shared dependence of residents on a single employer fostered a tight solidarity that made such collective action possible.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a case that complicates a widely held view about the position of workers in settlements like Kiruna.
It presents a consequence of the company's control over Kiruna's land, streets, and public institutions.
It presents evidence that national unions played a central role in improving conditions for Kiruna's miners.
It presents the explanation that some scholars offer for the solidarity among Kiruna's residents.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작하며, 회사 도시 노동자는 교섭력이 거의 없었다는 역사가들의 통념과 달리 키루나 광부들이 장기 파업으로 성과를 얻은 사례를 제시하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 회사의 통제를 언급한 앞 문장과 연결되지만, 파업은 그 통제의 결과로 제시되지 않고 오히려 예상과 어긋나는 사례로 제시된다. C는 파업이 전국 노조의 지원 '없이' 이루어졌다는 내용과 반대된다. D의 연대에 대한 설명은 밑줄 문장이 아니라 그 뒤 마지막 문장이 제시한다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and describes Kiruna's miners winning a long strike, which runs against historians' assumption that workers in company towns had little bargaining power, so A is correct. B links the sentence to the company's control, but the strike is presented as something that contradicts what that control would lead you to expect, not as its result. C reverses the text, which says the strike succeeded without the backing of the national union. D describes the role of the final sentence, which gives scholars' explanation for the solidarity; the underlined sentence only reports the strike.

quality.seed: economics and business — Swedish iron ore production and Kiruna mining town labor relations company town model

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 역사가들의 통념(회사 도시 노동자의 낮은 교섭력)에 반하는 사례(1969–70 파업 성공)를 제시하므로 A가 정답. B는 앞 문장의 '통제'와 마지막 문장의 '의존→연대' 논리를 결합하면 부분적으로 그럴듯해 비교가 필요하고, D는 마지막 문장의 기능이라 위치 확인이 필요하며, C는 'without the backing'과 정반대. 역사적 사실(LKAB가 1900년경 건설한 키루나, 1969–70년 전국 노조 지원 없는 장기 와일드캣 파업) 부합. 한·영 해설 모두 선택지 참조·결론 일치, 자연스러움. medium 적합.

advisory.note: 1969–70 키루나(LKAB) 파업은 노조 승인 없이 일어난 와일드캣 파업이라 사실과 맞다. B는 마지막 문장(고립·의존이 연대를 낳았다는 학자 견해) 때문에 부분적으로 그럴듯해서 변별력이 있다. C는 쉽게 배제된다.

problem.passage:
Histories of Irish whiskey often blame its twentieth-century collapse on outside shocks: Prohibition shut off the American market, and a trade war with Britain in the 1930s closed off much of the British Empire. Yet the industry's weakness arguably started decades earlier. __When the phylloxera insect devastated French vineyards in the late nineteenth century and British drinkers turned away from scarce brandy, Scottish firms won them over with cheaper blended whisky made in column stills, while many leading Dublin distillers dismissed blends as inferior and stayed with traditional pot-still spirits.__ By the time the later shocks arrived, Scotch had already become the whisky most consumers knew. Only after the few remaining Irish producers merged into a single company, Irish Distillers, in 1966 did the industry begin to recover, by closing old plants and putting its marketing behind a small number of internationally promoted brands.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Histories of Irish whiskey often blame its twentieth-century collapse on outside shocks: Prohibition shut off the American market, and a trade war with Britain in the 1930s closed off much of the British Empire. Yet the industry's weakness arguably started decades earlier. __When the phylloxera insect devastated French vineyards in the late nineteenth century and British drinkers turned away from scarce brandy, Scottish firms won them over with cheaper blended whisky made in column stills, while many leading Dublin distillers dismissed blends as inferior and stayed with traditional pot-still spirits.__ By the time the later shocks arrived, Scotch had already become the whisky most consumers knew. Only after the few remaining Irish producers merged into a single company, Irish Distillers, in 1966 did the industry begin to recover, by closing old plants and putting its marketing behind a small number of internationally promoted brands.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes a market shift that the text presents as the direct cause of most Irish distillery closures in the 1920s and 1930s.
It describes an earlier episode that the text uses to qualify a widely accepted explanation of the industry's decline.
It describes a business approach that the text presents as the model for the strategy Irish Distillers later adopted.
It describes an alternative view that the text raises only to dismiss in favor of the usual explanation.
problem.explanation: 지문은 먼저 금주법과 무역 전쟁이라는 통상적 설명을 제시한 뒤, "Yet ... started decades earlier"로 그 설명을 보완한다. 밑줄 문장은 필록세라 시기에 아일랜드 증류업자들이 블렌디드 위스키 시장을 놓친 더 이른 사건을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. A는 이 사건을 1920~30년대 폐업의 '직접' 원인으로 과장한다. 지문은 이후 충격도 인정한다. C는 1966년 이후의 전략(통합, 브랜드 마케팅)을 이 시기의 스카치 전략과 연결하지만, 지문은 그런 연결을 하지 않는다. D는 방향이 반대다. 지문은 이 관점을 기각하지 않고 받아들인다.
problem.explanationEn: The text starts with the usual explanation, Prohibition and the trade war, and then qualifies it with "Yet ... started decades earlier." The underlined sentence gives that earlier episode: Irish distillers missed the blended-whisky market during the phylloxera crisis. That makes B correct. A overstates the sentence's role by calling it the "direct" cause of the 1920s–30s closures, while the text still gives weight to the later shocks. C links Scotland's approach to Irish Distillers' strategy after 1966, but the text never makes that connection. D gets the direction backward: the text accepts this earlier explanation and doesn't dismiss it.

quality.seed: economics and business — Irish whiskey distillery consolidation and brand marketing recovery after phylloxera crisis decline

hardJudge.note: 지문 구조("Histories often blame..." → "Yet ... started decades earlier" → 밑줄 문장 → "By the time the later shocks arrived")가 B를 명확히 뒷받침한다. A는 '직접 원인'·'폐업'을 지문이 말하지 않아 과장, C는 1966년 전략과의 연결을 지문이 하지 않음, D는 방향 반대. 역사적 사실(필록세라, 블렌디드 스카치의 부상, 더블린 증류업자의 포트스틸 고수, 1966년 Irish Distillers 설립, 1930년대 영-아 경제전쟁)도 정확. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하며 모순 없음. 두 단계 판단(담화 표지 인식 + 전체 맥락 확인)이 필요하고 A·C가 부분적 근거를 가져 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: B는 'Yet ... arguably started decades earlier'로 통상 설명을 보완(qualify)하는 구조와 맞음. A(직접 원인 과장), C(1966년 전략과 연결 안 됨, 다만 브랜드 집중이라는 표면적 유사성으로 그럴듯함), D(방향 반대)는 각각 부분 근거가 있어 medium 난이도에 적합. 역사적 사실(필록세라, 연속식 증류기, 1966년 Irish Distillers 설립)도 정확함.

problem.passage:
Kuapa Kokoo, a farmer-owned cooperative founded in Ghana in 1993, challenged a long-standing arrangement in the country's cocoa trade. Instead of selling beans to licensed buying companies that passed them along to foreign exporters, member farmers pooled their harvests and negotiated directly with chocolate makers abroad. The cooperative's approach, which also gave farmers a share of the profits from a chocolate brand they partly ______ an unusual degree of control over how their crop was priced and marketed.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Kuapa Kokoo, a farmer-owned cooperative founded in Ghana in 1993, challenged a long-standing arrangement in the country's cocoa trade. Instead of selling beans to licensed buying companies that passed them along to foreign exporters, member farmers pooled their harvests and negotiated directly with chocolate makers abroad. The cooperative's approach, which also gave farmers a share of the profits from a chocolate brand they partly ______ an unusual degree of control over how their crop was priced and marketed.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: own; granted growers
own, granted growers
own—granted growers
own: granted growers
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The cooperative's approach"이고 동사는 "granted"이며, 그 사이의 "which also gave ... partly own"은 쉼표로 시작된 비필수 관계절이다. 삽입절은 시작한 부호와 같은 부호로 닫아야 하므로 쉼표를 쓴 B가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. C는 대시로 삽입절을 닫아 여는 쉼표와 짝이 맞지 않는다. D의 콜론도 주어와 동사 사이에 올 수 없고 앞부분이 완전한 절이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: Here the subject is "The cooperative's approach" and its verb is "granted." The clause "which also gave ... partly own" sits between them as a nonessential relative clause that opens with a comma. A nonessential clause has to close with the same mark it opened with, so B, which uses a comma, is correct. A puts a semicolon between the subject and the verb, and what comes before the semicolon isn't an independent clause. C closes the clause with a dash, which doesn't match the opening comma. D puts a colon between the subject and the verb, which isn't allowed, and what comes before the colon isn't a complete clause either.

quality.seed: economics and business — Ghanaian cocoa farming cooperatives and direct trade relationships bypassing middleman exporters model

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The cooperative's approach"와 동사 "granted" 사이의 비필수 관계절(which ... partly own)은 여는 쉼표와 짝을 이루는 쉼표로 닫아야 하므로 B가 정답. 세미콜론·콜론은 앞부분이 독립절이 아니어서 불가, 대시는 여는 부호와 불일치. 긴 삽입절로 인해 주어-동사 관계 파악이 필요하며 C가 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능하므로 medium 적합. Kuapa Kokoo(1993, 가나, Divine Chocolate 지분) 사실관계 정확.

advisory.note: 주어-삽입절-동사 구조로, 삽입절을 쉼표로 닫는 표준 문항이다. Kuapa Kokoo(1993년 설립, Divine Chocolate 공동 소유) 관련 사실도 대체로 정확하다. 학생은 긴 삽입절 끝을 찾아낸 뒤 여는 부호와 짝을 맞춰야 하므로 두 단계 판단이 필요하다.

problem.passage:
In rural Anatolia, carpet weavers working from home have long passed motifs from one generation to the next, treating them as shared village heritage rather than private property. When export firms began registering some of these traditional patterns as their own designs, economist Elif Kaya argued that copyright law, built to reward individual creators, was poorly suited to such crafts. Because a motif may have been refined by hundreds of weavers over centuries, she noted, any attempt to ______ it to a single author is largely arbitrary.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In rural Anatolia, carpet weavers working from home have long passed motifs from one generation to the next, treating them as shared village heritage rather than private property. When export firms began registering some of these traditional patterns as their own designs, economist Elif Kaya argued that copyright law, built to reward individual creators, was poorly suited to such crafts. Because a motif may have been refined by hundreds of weavers over centuries, she noted, any attempt to ______ it to a single author is largely arbitrary.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: attribute
restrict
reveal
adapt
problem.explanation: 지문은 하나의 문양을 수백 명의 직조공이 수 세기에 걸쳐 다듬었기 때문에 이를 한 명의 저자에게 돌리려는 시도가 자의적이라고 말하므로, '~의 것으로 돌리다'라는 뜻의 A가 정답이다. B는 수출 기업의 등록이 문양 사용을 제한한다는 맥락과 맞아 보이지만, 'restrict it to a single author'는 누가 만들었는지가 아니라 누가 쓸 수 있는지에 관한 말이어서 '여러 창작자'라는 근거와 이어지지 않는다. C는 문양을 한 저자에게 '드러낸다'는 뜻이 되어 논리가 맞지 않는다. D는 공예 전통에서 문양을 변형한다는 말로 그럴듯하지만, 저작자를 정하는 일이 자의적이라는 논점과 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says a motif was refined by hundreds of weavers over centuries, so trying to credit it to one author would be arbitrary. That makes A, "attribute," the right answer. B might seem to fit because registering a design does limit who can use it, but "restrict it to a single author" is about who may use the motif, not who made it, so it doesn't connect to the point about many creators. C would mean "revealing" the motif to an author, which doesn't make sense here. D fits the general idea of crafts changing designs, but it has nothing to do with the claim that naming a single author is arbitrary.

quality.seed: economics and business — Turkish carpet weaving cottage industry and design copyright protection in handicraft markets

hardJudge.note: "attribute ... to a single author"는 '수백 명의 직조공이 수 세기에 걸쳐 다듬었다'는 근거와 정확히 연결되어 정답이 명확하다. B(restrict)는 수출 기업의 등록·독점 맥락에서 부분적 매력을 지니고, D(adapt)도 공예 변형 맥락에서 그럴듯하여 비교가 필요하며, C(reveal)도 문장 구조상 말은 된다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 같은 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 영어는 자연스럽고 한글이 없다. 가상 인물(Elif Kaya) 사용으로 저작권·사실 오류 위험은 낮다.

advisory.note: 정답은 'attribute ... to a single author'다. 이 연어 관계와 '수백 명의 직조공'이라는 근거를 연결해야 풀 수 있다. B(restrict)는 등록 맥락과 'to a single author' 구문이 함께 맞아 보여 매력적인 오답이다. C는 다소 쉽게 배제되지만 D는 그럴듯해서 중간 난이도에 맞는다.

problem.passage:
Many companies buy their materials from one business, have another business make their products, and use stores owned by others to sell them. The Austrian crystal maker Swarovski, founded in 1895, took a different path for much of its history. It controlled nearly every step of its business itself, a strategy called vertical integration. __For example, the company mixed its own glass, designed and ran the machines that cut the crystals, and sold finished pieces in shops that carried its own name.__ By handling each stage, Swarovski could keep close watch on the quality of its crystals from start to finish.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Many companies buy their materials from one business, have another business make their products, and use stores owned by others to sell them. The Austrian crystal maker Swarovski, founded in 1895, took a different path for much of its history. It controlled nearly every step of its business itself, a strategy called vertical integration. __For example, the company mixed its own glass, designed and ran the machines that cut the crystals, and sold finished pieces in shops that carried its own name.__ By handling each stage, Swarovski could keep close watch on the quality of its crystals from start to finish.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a problem that Swarovski faced because it relied on other businesses for materials.
It describes the approach most companies use, which the text then contrasts with Swarovski's.
It gives specific cases showing how Swarovski carried out the strategy introduced in the previous sentence.
It explains a result of Swarovski's strategy that the text goes on to question.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작해 바로 앞 문장에서 소개한 수직 계열화가 실제로 어떻게 이루어졌는지(유리 제조, 커팅 기계, 자체 매장) 구체적 사례를 든다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 틀렸다. 이 문장은 문제점이 아니라 스와로브스키가 모든 단계를 직접 맡았다는 내용이다. B는 틀렸다. 대부분 회사의 방식은 첫 문장에서 설명되며, 밑줄 문장은 스와로브스키에 관한 것이다. D는 틀렸다. 지문은 이 전략에 의문을 제기하지 않고, 결과(품질 관리)는 마지막 문장에 나온다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "For example" and lists concrete cases (making its own glass, running its own cutting machines, selling in its own shops) of the vertical integration strategy named in the sentence right before it. So C is correct. A is wrong because the sentence describes no problem; it shows Swarovski doing every step itself instead of relying on others. B is wrong because the first sentence is the one that describes what most companies do, while the underlined sentence is about Swarovski. D is wrong because the text never questions the strategy, and the result (quality control) comes up in the last sentence, not this one.

quality.seed: economics and business — Austrian crystal manufacturer Swarovski and vertical integration from raw materials to retail

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작해 앞 문장의 수직 계열화 전략을 구체 사례로 뒷받침하므로 C가 정답. A(문제 제기), B(대부분 회사의 방식—첫 문장 내용), D(의문 제기되는 결과—지문에 없음)는 신호어와 문장 위치만 알면 바로 배제되나 전형적 오개념으로 그럴듯함. 한·영 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 스와로브스키 1895년 오스트리아 설립·수직 계열화 역사 사실에 부합. 단일 개념·한 단계 추론·평이한 어휘로 easy 적합.

advisory.note: "For example"라는 직접적 단서가 있어 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. 오답들은 지문의 다른 문장(첫 문장=B, 마지막 문장=D)의 기능을 끌어온 전형적인 오개념이라 easy에 적합하다. 스와로브스키가 1895년에 설립되었고 역사적으로 수직 계열화를 해 온 점은 대체로 사실에 부합한다.

problem.passage:
Every week in Mombasa, Kenya, buyers gather to bid on tea grown across East Africa. Much of this tea comes from smallholder farmers, who each tend only a small plot of land. Many people assume that such small growers have little say in what their crop is worth. __In fact, because smallholders sell their leaves through factories they jointly own, the prices set at the auction flow back to them as monthly and yearly payments.__ This arrangement links even a farmer with a few hundred tea bushes directly to the price that global buyers are willing to pay.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Every week in Mombasa, Kenya, buyers gather to bid on tea grown across East Africa. Much of this tea comes from smallholder farmers, who each tend only a small plot of land. Many people assume that such small growers have little say in what their crop is worth. __In fact, because smallholders sell their leaves through factories they jointly own, the prices set at the auction flow back to them as monthly and yearly payments.__ This arrangement links even a farmer with a few hundred tea bushes directly to the price that global buyers are willing to pay.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes how buyers at the Mombasa auction decide which tea to bid on each week.
It presents evidence that smallholder farmers grow more tea than large estates do.
It explains why the Mombasa auction meets only once a week rather than every day.
It challenges a common assumption by showing how small growers are connected to auction prices.
problem.explanation: 바로 앞 문장은 소규모 농민이 작물 가격에 거의 영향력이 없다는 흔한 가정을 제시하고, 밑줄 문장은 "In fact"로 시작해 공동 소유 공장을 통해 경매 가격이 농민에게 돌아온다고 설명하며 그 가정을 반박한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 구매자의 입찰 결정 방식을 다루지 않으므로 틀리다. B는 소농과 대농장의 생산량 비교가 지문에 없으므로 틀리다. C는 경매가 주 1회 열리는 이유를 설명하지 않으므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the underlined one states a common assumption: small growers have little say in what their crop is worth. The underlined sentence begins with "In fact" and explains that auction prices flow back to smallholders through factories they jointly own, which pushes back on that assumption. So D is correct. A is wrong because the sentence doesn't explain how buyers choose which tea to bid on. B is wrong because the text never compares how much tea smallholders and large estates produce. C is wrong because the sentence doesn't explain why the auction is held weekly.

quality.seed: economics and business — Kenyan tea auction system and smallholder farmer participation in commodity price discovery mechanisms

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "Many people assume..." 뒤에 "In fact"로 이어져 가정을 반박하는 구조가 지문에 명시적으로 드러나므로 D가 정답임이 분명하다. 오답 A·B·C는 지문의 세부 요소(구매자, 소농, 주 1회 경매)를 활용해 그럴듯하지만 밑줄 문장의 내용과 무관해 규칙(앞뒤 문맥에서 기능 파악)을 알면 바로 배제된다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하며 한글 혼입 없음. 몸바사 차 경매·소농 공동소유 공장(KTDA 모델) 서술은 사실과 부합. 원문 그대로 복제 흔적 없음.

advisory.note: "Many people assume" 다음에 "In fact"가 와서 단서가 분명하므로 easy 난이도에 맞음. 오답은 지문의 세부 내용(매주 입찰, 소농, 주 1회 경매)을 그럴듯하게 비튼 것. 굳이 꼽자면 "little say"(가격 결정권)와 "connected to prices"(가격과 연결됨)가 정확히 같은 말은 아니지만, 정답 판정에는 영향이 없음.

problem.passage:
For years, small cocoa farmers in the Dominican Republic sold their beans to middlemen who mixed harvests from many farms, so buyers rarely knew where any single bag came from. Recently, several farmer cooperatives have begun recording each farm's harvest dates, fermentation methods, and prices paid, then sharing those records directly with small chocolate makers abroad. __For example, one cooperative in the province of Duarte now gives each sack a code that lets a roaster in Oregon look up the exact family farm that grew the beans.__ Supporters say this kind of transparency helps farmers earn higher prices for carefully grown cocoa.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: For years, small cocoa farmers in the Dominican Republic sold their beans to middlemen who mixed harvests from many farms, so buyers rarely knew where any single bag came from. Recently, several farmer cooperatives have begun recording each farm's harvest dates, fermentation methods, and prices paid, then sharing those records directly with small chocolate makers abroad. __For example, one cooperative in the province of Duarte now gives each sack a code that lets a roaster in Oregon look up the exact family farm that grew the beans.__ Supporters say this kind of transparency helps farmers earn higher prices for carefully grown cocoa.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives a specific instance of the record-sharing practice described in the previous sentence.
It gives a specific reason why middlemen mixed harvests from many farms in the past.
It gives a specific objection to the claim that transparency helps farmers earn more.
It gives a specific conclusion that summarizes the overall argument of the text.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작하며, 앞 문장에서 설명한 협동조합의 기록 공유 관행을 Duarte 협동조합의 자루 코드라는 구체적 사례로 보여 준다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 틀렸다. 밑줄 문장은 과거에 중개상이 수확물을 섞은 이유를 설명하지 않는다. C는 틀렸다. 이 문장은 투명성의 이점을 반박하지 않고 오히려 뒷받침한다. D는 틀렸다. 이 문장은 결론이 아니며, 주장을 요약하는 역할은 마지막 문장에 가깝다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "For example." It shows the record-sharing practice described in the sentence before it through one concrete case: a cooperative in Duarte that puts a code on each sack. That makes A the correct answer. B is wrong because the sentence doesn't explain why middlemen used to mix harvests. C is wrong because the sentence supports the benefits of transparency instead of arguing against them. D is wrong because the sentence isn't a conclusion; the last sentence comes closer to summing up the text.

quality.seed: economics and business — Dominican cocoa farmer networks and supply chain transparency initiatives for direct roasters

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "For example"로 시작하며 앞 문장의 기록 공유 관행(수확일·발효법·가격 기록을 해외 초콜릿 제조사와 공유)을 Duarte 협동조합의 자루 코드 사례로 구체화하므로 A가 정답임을 직접 확인함. B(중개상이 섞은 이유), C(투명성 주장에 대한 반박), D(전체 요약 결론)는 모두 본문과 불일치하나 구조 단서를 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯한 전형적 오개념 수준. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 A를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조가 선택지와 일치하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 명시적 담화 표지 하나로 풀리는 easy 난이도에 적합. Duarte가 도미니카공화국의 카카오 생산 지역이라는 점도 사실과 부합. 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 'For example'라는 명시적 단서가 있고 한 단계 추론으로 풀 수 있다. 오답들은 지문의 다른 요소(과거 중개상 관행, 투명성 주장, 결론)를 활용한 전형적인 기능 오개념이다. 다만 D 해설에서 마지막 문장이 '요약에 가깝다'고 한 표현은 다소 느슨하지만, 오류로 볼 정도는 아니다.

problem.passage:
In the southern Indian city of Tiruppur, often called the knitwear capital of Tamil Nadu, few firms handle every stage of production under one roof. Instead, work moves among hundreds of specialized workshops. Relying on dense networks of small subcontractors for dyeing, printing, and stitching, ______ able to fill large overseas orders far faster than a single vertically integrated factory could.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In the southern Indian city of Tiruppur, often called the knitwear capital of Tamil Nadu, few firms handle every stage of production under one roof. Instead, work moves among hundreds of specialized workshops. Relying on dense networks of small subcontractors for dyeing, printing, and stitching, ______ able to fill large overseas orders far faster than a single vertically integrated factory could.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Tiruppur's knitwear exports are
Tiruppur's garment exporters are
the subcontracting networks themselves are
European fashion retailers are
problem.explanation:
정답 B. 분사구 "Relying on dense networks of small subcontractors..."의 의미상 주어는 하청 네트워크에 의존해 주문을 처리하는 행위자여야 하므로 '의류 수출업체(exporters)'가 맞다. 
A: 수출업체 대신 그들의 산출물인 '수출품(exports)'을 주어로 둔 범주 혼동. 상품은 하청업체에 의존하거나 주문을 처리할 수 없다. 
C: 복수형이라 are와 수일치는 맞지만, 네트워크가 '하청업체 네트워크에 의존한다'는 것은 자기 자신에 의존하는 셈이 되어 논리적으로 맞지 않는다. 
D: 유럽 소매업체는 주문을 하는 쪽이지 Tiruppur의 하청업체에 의존해 주문을 처리하는 주체가 아니다. 문맥과 무관한 명사다.
problem.explanationEn:
B is correct. The introductory phrase "Relying on dense networks of small subcontractors..." needs a subject that can actually do the relying and fill the orders. That subject is the garment exporters, so B gives the modifier the right subject.
A is wrong because it uses the exporters' product, their exports, instead of the exporters. Products can't rely on subcontractors or fill orders.
C is wrong even though "networks are" agrees in number. The networks can't be the ones relying on networks of subcontractors, because that would mean they rely on themselves.
D is wrong because European retailers place the orders. They aren't the ones who use Tiruppur's subcontractors to fill them.

hardJudge.note: 문두 분사구 "Relying on dense networks of small subcontractors..."의 논리적 주어는 하청망에 의존해 해외 주문을 처리하는 행위자이므로 B(garment exporters)가 유일하게 적합. A는 사물(수출품)로 범주 오류, C는 '네트워크가 하청 네트워크에 의존'하는 순환 논리, D는 주문을 '하는' 쪽이지 '처리하는' 쪽이 아님. 네 선택지 모두 복수+are로 수일치만으로는 판별 불가하며 문법적으로 완결되어 의미적 수식 대상 추론이 필수. 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하고 모순 없음. 지문은 창작 원문으로 보이며 Tiruppur 관련 사실(니트웨어 수도, 하청 생산 구조)도 실제와 부합.

advisory.note: 선택지 4개가 모두 복수 주어+are라서 수일치로는 정답을 가릴 수 없다. 정답을 고르려면 분사구의 행위 주체(하청업체에 의존하면서 주문을 처리하는 쪽)를 의미적으로 추론해야 한다. A(사물/산출물), C(자기 자신에 의존하게 되는 논리 모순), D(문맥상 주문을 처리하지 않는 행위자)는 서로 다른 유형의 함정이어서 변별력이 있다. 지문에 나온 사실(Tiruppur가 니트웨어 중심지이고 하청 네트워크로 운영된다는 점)도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
For decades, the Croatian government poured subsidies into shipyards such as Uljanik in Pula and 3. Maj in Rijeka, hoping to protect the thousands of maritime jobs concentrated in a few Adriatic port towns. The payments kept the yards operating through repeated financial ______ to make the yards competitive with lower-cost builders in Asia, and several of them collapsed into bankruptcy once European Union rules limited further state aid.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: For decades, the Croatian government poured subsidies into shipyards such as Uljanik in Pula and 3. Maj in Rijeka, hoping to protect the thousands of maritime jobs concentrated in a few Adriatic port towns. The payments kept the yards operating through repeated financial ______ to make the yards competitive with lower-cost builders in Asia, and several of them collapsed into bankruptcy once European Union rules limited further state aid.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: crises, so they did little
crises, they did little
crises, but they did little
crises but they did; little
problem.explanation:
빈칸 앞 "The payments kept the yards operating through repeated financial crises"와 뒤 "they did little to make the yards competitive..."는 둘 다 독립절이다. 앞 절은 보조금 덕분에 조선소가 계속 돌아갔다는 성과이고, 뒤 절은 경쟁력은 거의 높이지 못했다는 한계이므로 둘은 대조 관계다. 따라서 쉼표와 등위접속사 but을 쓴 C가 정답이다.
A: 쉼표+등위접속사라는 구두점 형식은 맞다. 하지만 so는 인과를 나타내므로 '조선소를 유지시켰기 때문에 경쟁력을 높이지 못했다'는 뜻이 되어 논리가 맞지 않는다.
B: 독립절 두 개를 쉼표만으로 이었으므로 콤마 스플라이스다.
D: 세미콜론이 절 경계가 아니라 "did"와 목적어 "little" 사이에 들어가 동사와 목적어를 갈라 놓는다. 또 세미콜론 뒤 "little to make..."는 독립절이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn:
The text before the blank ("The payments kept the yards operating through repeated financial crises") and the text after it ("they did little to make the yards competitive...") are both independent clauses. The first clause gives what the subsidies achieved: they kept the yards running. The second gives their limit: they barely made the yards more competitive. That's a contrast, so the best way to join the clauses is a comma plus "but," which is choice C.
A: The comma plus a coordinating conjunction is the right punctuation, but "so" signals cause and effect. It would mean the yards failed to become competitive *because* the subsidies kept them running, and that's not the logic of the text.
B: This joins two independent clauses with only a comma, so it's a comma splice.
D: The semicolon doesn't fall at the boundary between the clauses. Instead, it splits the verb "did" from its object "little," and what follows the semicolon isn't an independent clause.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤 모두 완전한 독립절이며, '유지시켰다(성과) vs 경쟁력은 못 높였다(한계)'의 대조 관계가 명확하여 ", but"이 정답으로 성립. B는 콤마 스플라이스, D는 did/little 사이 세미콜론으로 체크리스트 충족. A(so)는 구두점·문법은 맞지만 인과 논리가 어긋나는 오답으로, 절 관계(대조/인과) 판단이라는 추가 사고를 요구해 hard 특성에 부합. 다만 실제 SAT 'conventions' 문항에서는 문법적으로 성립하는 오답(A)을 두는 경우가 드물어 논리 판단이 섞인 설계라는 점은 참고. 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하며 모순 없음. 'they'가 payments, 'them'이 yards를 가리키는 점은 문맥상 해석 가능.

advisory.note: C는 대조 관계(조선소를 유지시킴 vs 경쟁력은 거의 높이지 못함)를 바르게 표시한다. A는 쉼표+등위접속사라는 형식은 맞지만 so 때문에 인과 관계가 되어 논리가 맞지 않는다. 그래서 구두점이 필요한지만 보는 수준을 넘어, 절 사이의 논리적 관계까지 따져야 풀 수 있다. B는 콤마 스플라이스이고, D는 세미콜론이 동사 did와 목적어 little을 갈라 놓는 잘못된 위치에 있다. 사실관계(Uljanik·3. Maj 파산, EU의 국가 보조 규제)는 대체로 정확하다. 다만 결정적 변별 요소가 so와 but의 의미 차이여서 transitions 유형과 일부 겹친다.

problem.passage:
Founded in 2011 by two Estonian entrepreneurs, the money-transfer company Wise undercut traditional banks by avoiding the international wire networks that banks rely on. When a customer in Germany sends euros to a relative in Mexico, the euros remain in Wise's German account______ pesos are paid out to the relative from a reserve that Wise already holds in Mexico.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Founded in 2011 by two Estonian entrepreneurs, the money-transfer company Wise undercut traditional banks by avoiding the international wire networks that banks rely on. When a customer in Germany sends euros to a relative in Mexico, the euros remain in Wise's German account______ pesos are paid out to the relative from a reserve that Wise already holds in Mexico.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , in effect,
; in effect
; in effect;
; in effect,
problem.explanation:
정답 D. 빈칸 앞 "the euros remain in Wise's German account"와 뒤 "pesos are paid out ... in Mexico"는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 따라서 두 절 사이에 경계(세미콜론)가 필요하고, 삽입어 "in effect"는 뒤 절을 이끄는 도입어이므로 그 뒤에 쉼표를 둔다. "; in effect,"가 맞다.
A: 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어서 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. "in effect"를 단순 삽입어로 보고 양쪽에 쉼표를 찍으면 맞다고 착각하기 쉽지만, 앞뒤가 모두 완전한 절이다.
B: 세미콜론으로 경계는 맞게 두었지만, 도입어 "in effect" 뒤에 쉼표가 없어 삽입어와 절이 구분되지 않는다(삽입어 구두점 비대칭).
C: 삽입어 자체를 또 하나의 절 경계로 오인해 뒤에 불필요한 세미콜론을 넣었다. 세미콜론 뒤의 "in effect"는 혼자서 독립절이 될 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
The answer is D. "The euros remain in Wise's German account" is an independent clause, and so is "pesos are paid out to the relative from a reserve that Wise already holds in Mexico." Two independent clauses need a strong boundary, such as a semicolon. "In effect" is an introductory phrase that belongs to the second clause, so it should be followed by a comma: "; in effect,".
A is wrong because it joins two independent clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. It can look correct if you read "in effect" as a simple interruption inside a single clause, but the words on both sides of it are complete clauses.
B is wrong because it places the semicolon correctly but leaves out the comma after the introductory phrase "in effect," so the punctuation around the phrase is unbalanced.
C is wrong because it treats the phrase itself as a clause boundary and adds a second semicolon. "In effect" can't stand alone as an independent clause, so that second semicolon is unnecessary.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞 "the euros remain in Wise's German account"와 뒤 "pesos are paid out ..."는 모두 주어+동사를 갖춘 독립절이므로 세미콜론 경계가 필요하고, 뒤 절 도입 전환어 "in effect" 뒤에 쉼표를 두는 D가 유일한 관습적 정답. A는 "in effect"를 양쪽 쉼표 삽입어로 위장한 콤마 스플라이스로, 삽입어 함정을 간파해야 하는 hard 수준의 사고를 요구함. C는 전환어 뒤에 세미콜론을 둔 명백한 오류. 사실관계(2011년 에스토니아 창업자, 현지 계좌 기반 송금 모델)도 정확. 다만 B("; in effect" 쉼표 생략)는 일반 영어에서는 허용 범위에 가까워 D와의 변별이 다소 약한 편이나, SAT 관습상 전환어 뒤 쉼표가 표준이므로 정답 판정에는 지장 없음.

advisory.note: 빈칸 앞뒤가 모두 독립절이라 세미콜론이 필요하고, 'in effect'는 뒤 절을 이끄는 도입어라서 뒤에 쉼표를 둬야 한다. 따라서 D가 맞다. A는 콤마 스플라이스, B는 도입어 뒤 쉼표가 빠진 비대칭, C는 삽입어를 절 경계로 잘못 본 오답이다. 오답 설계는 전형적이지만, 'in effect'가 두 절 사이에 끼어 있어서 삽입어인지 절 경계인지 가려내는 사고가 필요하므로 medium보다 한 단계 높다고 본다. 다만 hard 상단이라고 하기에는 패턴이 익숙한 편이다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Tanzania is one of Africa's largest producers of raw cashew nuts.
- In the 2017–2018 season, Tanzania exported most of its cashew harvest unprocessed, largely to India and Vietnam for shelling.
- In that season, only about 10 percent of Tanzania's cashew crop was processed domestically.
- Processing cashews (shelling, peeling, and grading kernels) can multiply the export value of each ton several times over.
- The Tanzanian government has announced a target of processing 60 percent of the national cashew crop within the country by 2025.

The student wants to emphasize how far Tanzania's cashew industry would need to change to meet its stated ambition. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Tanzania is one of Africa's largest producers of raw cashew nuts.
- In the 2017–2018 season, Tanzania exported most of its cashew harvest unprocessed, largely to India and Vietnam for shelling.
- In that season, only about 10 percent of Tanzania's cashew crop was processed domestically.
- Processing cashews (shelling, peeling, and grading kernels) can multiply the export value of each ton several times over.
- The Tanzanian government has announced a target of processing 60 percent of the national cashew crop within the country by 2025.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize how far Tanzania's cashew industry would need to change to meet its stated ambition. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Although only about 10 percent of Tanzania's cashew crop was processed domestically in the 2017–2018 season, the government aims to process 60 percent of it within the country by 2025.
Tanzania, one of Africa's largest producers of raw cashew nuts, has set a goal of processing 60 percent of its national cashew crop domestically by 2025.
Although Tanzania is one of Africa's largest producers of raw cashew nuts, it sent most of its 2017–2018 harvest unprocessed to India and Vietnam for shelling.
Although only about 10 percent of Tanzania's cashew crop was processed domestically in the 2017–2018 season, a government ban on raw exports is expected to raise that share to 60 percent by 2025.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 목표는 야심(목표치)과 현재 상황 사이의 격차를 강조하는 것이다. A는 2017–2018년 국내 가공률 약 10%와 2025년 목표 60%라는 서로 다른 두 사실을 하나로 묶어 격차를 직접 보여 준다.
B: 60% 목표만 담고 출발점이 되는 현재 가공률이 없다. 그래서 얼마나 바뀌어야 하는지 알 수 없어 목표의 절반만 달성한다.
C: 두 사실(주요 생산국이라는 점, 원물 수출)을 결합했지만 정부 목표를 언급하지 않아 '야심'과의 격차라는 목표와 관련이 없다.
D: 10%와 60%는 노트와 맞지만, 노트에 없는 '원물 수출 금지'를 추가하고 목표를 예상 결과처럼 바꿔 사실을 왜곡한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice A is correct. The goal is to show how big the gap is between where the industry stands now and what Tanzania is aiming for. Choice A puts two separate facts side by side: only about 10 percent of the crop was processed at home in 2017–2018, and the target is 60 percent by 2025. Seeing both numbers together makes the size of the change clear.
Choice B gives only the 60 percent target. Without the starting point, you can't tell how much has to change, so it only does half the job.
Choice C combines two facts from the notes (Tanzania is a major producer, and it exports most of its cashews raw), but it never mentions the government's target. Without the target, there is no ambition to compare against.
Choice D adds a ban on raw exports, which does not appear in the notes. It also presents the target as an expected outcome, which changes what the notes actually say.

hardJudge.note: A는 현재치(10%)와 목표치(60%)를 결합해 '얼마나 바뀌어야 하는가'를 직접 드러내므로 정답 타당. B는 목표만(한쪽 사실), C는 목표 미언급으로 과제 불충족, D는 노트에 없는 '수출 금지'와 목표를 예측으로 변환한 확실성 왜곡. 특히 D는 10%/60% 수치가 정확해 표면적으로 그럴듯하므로 claim_certainty_discrimination과 노트 외 정보 식별을 동시에 요구해 medium 이상. 다만 B/C 제거는 비교적 쉬워 난이도는 hard 하한선 수준. 해설 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 정답은 맞다. 다만 전형적인 medium 수준의 '격차 = 현재치 + 목표치' 조합 문제다. A만 10%와 60%를 함께 담고 있고, D는 노트에 없는 수출 금지라는 단서가 눈에 띄어 쉽게 걸러진다. B와 C는 한쪽 정보만 담고 있다. 확실성 수준(목표 vs 예상)을 가르는 요소가 D에 일부 있지만 결정적이지 않아 hard 특성을 충족한다고 보기 어렵다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Hanseatic League was a network of merchant guilds and towns that dominated trade in Northern Europe from the 1200s to the 1600s.
- In Hanseatic trading centers such as Bruges and London, sworn inspectors examined bolts of cloth before the cloth could be sold.
- Inspectors checked each bolt's length, weave density, and dye, then attached a lead seal marking its grade.
- A seal from a recognized town let a buyer in a distant port judge a cloth's quality without unrolling and examining it.
- Cloth that failed inspection could be cut up or burned, and the weaver could be fined.
- The League also negotiated trading privileges, such as reduced tolls, with foreign rulers.

The student wants to emphasize why the League's grading practice mattered to merchants trading across long distances. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Hanseatic League was a network of merchant guilds and towns that dominated trade in Northern Europe from the 1200s to the 1600s.
- In Hanseatic trading centers such as Bruges and London, sworn inspectors examined bolts of cloth before the cloth could be sold.
- Inspectors checked each bolt's length, weave density, and dye, then attached a lead seal marking its grade.
- A seal from a recognized town let a buyer in a distant port judge a cloth's quality without unrolling and examining it.
- Cloth that failed inspection could be cut up or burned, and the weaver could be fined.
- The League also negotiated trading privileges, such as reduced tolls, with foreign rulers.
problem.question: The student wants to emphasize why the League's grading practice mattered to merchants trading across long distances. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Hanseatic inspectors measured each bolt's length, weave density, and dye before attaching a lead seal that marked its grade.
Because a recognized town's seal certified a bolt's grade, a buyer in a faraway port could trust the cloth's quality without having to unroll and examine it.
From the 1200s to the 1600s, the Hanseatic League, a network of guilds and towns, dominated Northern European trade through cloth inspection, trading privileges, and other practices.
In addition to inspecting cloth, the Hanseatic League gained trading privileges, such as reduced tolls, from foreign rulers, which made long-distance trade cheaper for its merchants.
problem.explanation:
정답 B: 목표는 등급 판정 관행이 원거리 상인에게 왜 중요했는지 강조하는 것이다. B는 봉인이 품질을 보증했다는 점과, 그 덕분에 멀리 있는 구매자가 직접 펼쳐 보지 않고도 품질을 믿을 수 있었다는 결과를 함께 제시하므로 '왜 중요했는가'에 답한다.
A(지나치게 세부적): 검사 절차만 자세히 설명할 뿐, 그 관행이 원거리 거래에 왜 중요했는지는 말하지 않는다.
C(지나치게 포괄적): 동맹 전체를 개관하며 등급 판정을 여러 관행 중 하나로만 언급해 초점이 흐려진다.
D(다른 항목 강조): 원거리 교역을 언급해 그럴듯하지만, 등급 판정이 아니라 통행세 감면이라는 다른 관행의 이점을 강조한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer B: Your goal is to emphasize why the grading practice mattered to long-distance merchants. B links the seal, which certified a bolt's grade, to the payoff: a buyer in a faraway port could trust the cloth's quality without examining it. That answers the "why it mattered" part.
A (too detailed): It lays out the inspection steps but never explains why the practice mattered for long-distance trade.
C (too broad): It gives an overview of the whole League and mentions cloth inspection only as one practice in a list, so the focus is lost.
D (wrong item): It mentions long-distance trade, which sounds relevant, but it emphasizes a different practice, toll privileges, instead of the grading system.

hardJudge.note: 목표(등급 관행이 '원거리' 상인에게 '왜' 중요했는가)에 B만 정확히 부합. B는 노트 3(봉인=등급 표시)과 노트 4(원거리 구매자가 펼쳐 보지 않고 판단)를 결합해 인과를 서술함. A는 절차 세부(과잉 구체), C는 동맹 개관(과잉 포괄), D는 '원거리 교역 비용 절감'이라는 키워드로 유인하지만 통행세 감면이라는 다른 관행을 강조하므로 목표의 초점(등급 판정)을 정확히 구분해야 함. 역사적 사실(한자동맹의 직물 검사·납 봉인·통행세 특권)도 무리 없음. 다만 B가 노트 4를 거의 그대로 재진술하는 수준이라 hard로서는 경계선에 가까움.

advisory.note: 정답 B가 옳다. 노트 4번 항목을 거의 그대로 옮긴 문장이라 여러 정보를 종합할 필요가 거의 없다. 'distant port'와 'faraway port'가 그대로 대응해 표면 매칭만으로 풀린다. D는 'long-distance'라는 단어로 유인하지만 등급 판정이 아닌 다른 관행이라 쉽게 제거된다. 전형적인 medium 수준이다.

problem.passage:
In the early 1900s, inspectors at American silk mills routinely judged the best Italian raw silk to be finer and more lustrous, skein for skein, than anything arriving from Japan. Yet over the same decades, those mills shifted their purchases decisively toward Japanese silk, which Japanese cooperatives had begun sorting by standardized cocoon grades so that every bale of a given grade matched the others closely. ______ the factor that won American buyers was evidently not the excellence of any single skein but the assurance that thread from one shipment would run on high-speed power looms just like thread from the last.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In the early 1900s, inspectors at American silk mills routinely judged the best Italian raw silk to be finer and more lustrous, skein for skein, than anything arriving from Japan. Yet over the same decades, those mills shifted their purchases decisively toward Japanese silk, which Japanese cooperatives had begun sorting by standardized cocoon grades so that every bale of a given grade matched the others closely. ______ the factor that won American buyers was evidently not the excellence of any single skein but the assurance that thread from one shipment would run on high-speed power looms just like thread from the last.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Taken together,
Nevertheless,
In other words,
Similarly,
problem.explanation:
정답 A: 지문은 서로 어긋나 보이는 두 관찰을 제시한다. 하나는 이탈리아산 실이 타래 하나하나로 보면 품질이 더 높았다는 것이고, 다른 하나는 그런데도 미국 공장들이 표준화된 일본산 실로 구매를 옮겼다는 것이다. 마지막 문장은 두 관찰을 합쳐 얻는 결론이다. 구매자가 중시한 것은 최고 품질이 아니라 균일성이었다는 것이므로 종합을 나타내는 'Taken together,'가 알맞다.
B 오답: 'Nevertheless'는 두 관찰이 상반된다는 점만 보고 단순 대조로 처리한 것이다. 마지막 문장은 둘째 관찰과 대립하지 않는다. 오히려 두 관찰의 긴장을 풀어 주는 설명이다.
C 오답: 'In other words'는 둘째 관찰(표준화된 등급)만 다시 말하는 것으로 본 선택이다. 첫째 관찰(이탈리아산이 더 우수함)과 대비해야 나오는 'not the excellence of any single skein'이라는 부분을 반영하지 못한다.
D 오답: 'Similarly'는 앞 내용과 비슷한 다른 사례를 덧붙일 때 쓴다. 마지막 문장은 새로운 유사 사례가 아니라 결론이므로 맥락과 관계없다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer A: The passage gives two observations that seem to clash. First, inspectors judged Italian silk finer, skein for skein. Second, American mills still shifted toward Japanese silk that was sorted into standardized grades. The last sentence draws a conclusion that only works when you combine both points: buyers valued consistency more than peak quality. "Taken together," signals exactly that kind of synthesis.
B is wrong: "Nevertheless," treats the final sentence as a simple contrast because the two observations look opposed. But the final sentence doesn't contradict the second observation. It explains why the two observations fit together.
C is wrong: "In other words," treats the final sentence as a restatement of the second observation alone. That ignores the part about "not the excellence of any single skein," which depends on the first observation about Italian quality.
D is wrong: "Similarly," would introduce a parallel example. The final sentence is a conclusion, not a new comparable case.

hardJudge.note: 두 관찰(이탈리아산 개별 품질 우위 vs. 표준화된 일본산으로의 구매 이동)이 긴장 관계로 제시되고, 마지막 문장은 'evidently'와 'not the excellence of any single skein but the assurance…' 구조로 두 관찰을 모두 끌어와 결론을 도출하므로 'Taken together,'가 가장 논리적이다. B는 둘째 문장과 대립하지 않는 결론에 단순 대조를 적용한 오답, C는 둘째 관찰의 재진술로만 보는 오답(첫째 관찰 대비 요소를 놓침), D는 유사 사례 추가가 아니므로 오답. 다만 C가 비교적 그럴듯한 매력적 오답이어서 변별 근거('evidently'의 추론 표지, 첫 문장 참조)가 수험생에게 명확히 보이는지 검토 가치는 있으나 정답 타당성은 유지됨. 1900년대 초 일본산 생사의 표준화·균일성으로 미국 시장 점유가 확대된 역사적 사실과도 부합.

advisory.note: 두 관찰(이탈리아산 실의 품질이 더 높음, 그런데도 일본산 실로 구매가 옮겨감)을 합쳐야 균일성이라는 결론이 나온다. 'In other words'가 그럴듯한 오답 역할을 하지만, 마지막 문장은 둘째 관찰만 다시 말한 것이 아니라 두 관찰을 종합한 추론이므로 정답은 A 하나로 정해진다. 역사적 배경도 대체로 사실에 맞다.

problem.passage:
In France's Bordeaux region, négociants (merchant shippers) long controlled how wine moved from estates to buyers around the world. The official ranking of the region's top estates, drafted in 1855 largely from these merchants' sales records, ______ a major reason that some Bordeaux wines sell for many times the price of wines made just a few miles away.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In France's Bordeaux region, négociants (merchant shippers) long controlled how wine moved from estates to buyers around the world. The official ranking of the region's top estates, drafted in 1855 largely from these merchants' sales records, ______ a major reason that some Bordeaux wines sell for many times the price of wines made just a few miles away.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: remain
have remained
remains
are remaining
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'ranking'이므로 동사도 단수형이어야 하고, 그래서 C가 정답이다. 주어와 동사 사이의 'of the region's top estates'와 삽입구 'drafted in 1855 … records'는 수식어일 뿐이라 동사의 수에 영향을 주지 않는다. A, B, D는 모두 복수형 동사이다. 이 선택지들은 동사 바로 앞에 있는 복수 명사 'estates'나 'records'를 주어로 착각하게 만든다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "ranking," so the verb also has to be singular. That makes C the correct answer. The phrase "of the region's top estates" and the inserted phrase "drafted in 1855 ... records" are just modifiers that sit between the subject and the verb, so they don't change the verb's number. A, B, and D are all plural verb forms. They tempt you to treat a nearby plural noun like "estates" or "records" as the subject.

quality.seed: economics and business — French Bordeaux wine négociant system and shipper control of classification driving price premium differentiation

hardJudge.note: 주어 'ranking'(단수) + 긴 수식어(of the region's top estates, drafted … records) 뒤의 동사 수 일치 문항. 'remains'만 단수형이므로 C가 유일한 정답. A/B/D는 모두 복수형으로, 인접한 복수 명사 'estates'/'records'에 이끌리는 전형적 오개념 선택지. 한·영 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 1855 보르도 등급(négociants 거래 기록 기반)은 사실과 부합. 단일 규칙(주어-동사 수 일치)으로 풀리는 easy 난이도 적합.

advisory.note: 주어 'ranking'(단수)과 동사 'remains'가 일치한다. 사이에 긴 수식어가 있지만 풀이 규칙은 주어-동사 일치 하나뿐이다. 오답 3개는 모두 복수형으로, 가까운 복수 명사에 끌리게 하는 전형적인 함정이다.

problem.passage:
Founded in Sweden in 1907, the ball-bearing manufacturer SKF quickly grew by allowing other companies to use its designs. According to economic historians, the licensing agreements signed by SKF ______ an important reason that advanced bearing technology appeared in factories across Europe during the early twentieth century.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Founded in Sweden in 1907, the ball-bearing manufacturer SKF quickly grew by allowing other companies to use its designs. According to economic historians, the licensing agreements signed by SKF ______ an important reason that advanced bearing technology appeared in factories across Europe during the early twentieth century.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: is
was
has been
are
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "agreements"이고, "signed by SKF"는 짧은 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 동사도 복수형이어야 하므로 D "are"가 정답이다. A "is", B "was", C "has been"은 모두 단수 동사로, 바로 앞의 단수 명사 "SKF"에 동사를 맞추는 흔한 실수를 노린 선택지이다. 이 오답들은 복수 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "agreements." The phrase "signed by SKF" is just a short modifier, so the verb has to be plural, which makes D, "are," the correct answer. Choices A ("is"), B ("was"), and C ("has been") are all singular verbs. They play on a common mistake: matching the verb to the nearby singular noun "SKF." None of them agrees in number with the plural subject.

quality.seed: economics and business — Swedish ball-bearing manufacturer SKF and licensing agreements spreading manufacturing technology across European firms

hardJudge.note: 주어 "the licensing agreements"(복수) + 짧은 수식어 "signed by SKF" 구조로, 복수 동사 "are"(D)만이 유일한 복수 선택지이므로 정답이 명확하다. 과거 사건을 다루지만 "According to economic historians"가 현재의 역사적 평가를 나타내므로 현재형 "are"는 자연스럽다(SAT 관행에 부합). 오답 A·B·C는 모두 단수형으로, 가까운 단수 명사 "SKF"에 끌리는 전형적 오개념을 반영해 easy 난이도에 적합하다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하며, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. SKF 1907년 스웨덴 설립은 사실에 부합한다.

advisory.note: 주어 'agreements'(복수)와 동사의 수 일치를 묻는 문항으로, 복수형 선택지는 D뿐이다. 'According to economic historians'가 역사가들의 현재 견해를 나타내므로 현재 시제도 자연스럽다. 정답의 근거가 하나뿐이고 오답들은 가까운 명사 SKF에 동사를 맞추는 전형적인 오개념을 노리므로 easy 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
In the early nineteenth century, much of the indigo grown in Bengal was sold through a small group of London brokerage houses. Economic historian Mira Sandhu argues that these houses operated as an informal cartel: rather than competing, they coordinated their bids at the quarterly London auctions to hold down the prices paid to Bengal planters. Sandhu notes that a cartel of this kind would leave a specific signature in auction records. If the houses were truly competing, the price per chest should have risen in years when the Bengal harvest was small, since scarcity would push buyers to outbid one another. Under coordination, however, prices would stay nearly flat regardless of harvest size, while the share of chests bought by the leading houses would remain consistently high. Sandhu has compiled auction records that report, for each year from 1815 to 1830, both the size of the Bengal harvest and the average price per chest paid at auction.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Sandhu's claim about the London brokerage houses?
problem.stimulus: In the early nineteenth century, much of the indigo grown in Bengal was sold through a small group of London brokerage houses. Economic historian Mira Sandhu argues that these houses operated as an informal cartel: rather than competing, they coordinated their bids at the quarterly London auctions to hold down the prices paid to Bengal planters. Sandhu notes that a cartel of this kind would leave a specific signature in auction records. If the houses were truly competing, the price per chest should have risen in years when the Bengal harvest was small, since scarcity would push buyers to outbid one another. Under coordination, however, prices would stay nearly flat regardless of harvest size, while the share of chests bought by the leading houses would remain consistently high. Sandhu has compiled auction records that report, for each year from 1815 to 1830, both the size of the Bengal harvest and the average price per chest paid at auction.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Sandhu's claim about the London brokerage houses?
options: In years when the Bengal harvest fell well below average, the average auction price per chest stayed within a few percent of its level in abundant years.
Across the period, the average auction price per chest changed by only a few percent from one year to the next.
In several years, the Bengal harvest was less than half the size of the harvest in the preceding year.
Over the period, the cost of shipping a chest of indigo from Calcutta to London rose more steeply than the auction price per chest.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: Sandhu는 경쟁 시장이라면 흉작인 해에 가격이 올라야 하지만 담합이 있으면 수확량과 관계없이 가격이 거의 그대로일 것이라고 예측한다. A는 수확량(흉작)과 가격(거의 변화 없음)을 함께 보여 주므로 이 예측과 바로 맞아떨어진다.
B(가격만 봄): 가격이 해마다 안정적이었다는 것만으로는 부족하다. 그 기간에 수확량 자체가 안정적이었다면 경쟁 시장에서도 가격은 평탄하게 나온다. 수확량과 연결해야 의미가 생긴다.
C(수확량만 봄): 수확량이 크게 변했다는 사실만 있고 그때 가격이 어땠는지가 없다. 따라서 경쟁인지 담합인지 가려낼 수 없다.
D(제3의 변수): 운송비는 Sandhu가 정한 신호(수확량 대비 가격)에 들어 있지 않고 자료에도 없는 변수이므로 주장을 직접 뒷받침하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, A: Sandhu predicts that if the market were competitive, prices would rise in years with small harvests. Under a cartel, prices would stay nearly flat no matter how big the harvest was. Choice A links the two variables together: harvests were low, yet prices barely moved. That is exactly the pattern Sandhu says a cartel would leave.
B (looks only at price): Steady prices from year to year don't prove anything by themselves. If harvests were also steady, a competitive market would produce flat prices too. You need to tie price to harvest size before the pattern means anything.
C (looks only at harvest size): This tells you harvests varied a lot, but it says nothing about how prices responded. Without that, you can't tell competition from coordination.
D (brings in an outside variable): Shipping costs aren't part of Sandhu's test or her data, so this finding can't directly support her claim.

hardJudge.note: 지문이 담합의 '서명'을 수확량-가격의 조건부 관계로 명시하고, 정답 A만이 흉작(수확량 변수)과 가격 평탄(가격 변수)을 결합한다. B는 가격만, C는 수확량만 본 단일 변수 오답이며 B는 '가격 안정 = 담합'이라는 직관 함정으로 기능한다. D는 자료에 없는 운송비를 끌어온 외부 변수 오답. 해설은 각 선택지의 결함을 변수 관점에서 정확히 짚으며 정답과 모순 없음. 지문에 언급된 '선도 가맹점의 점유율'은 자료 범위(수확량·가격)에 포함되지 않지만 질문이 '가장 직접적으로'를 묻고 선택지에 점유율 관련 항목이 없어 혼선 없음.

advisory.note: 수확량과 가격 두 변수를 함께 봐야 정답이 나온다. B는 가격만 보는 강한 함정이다. 지문에서 언급한 점유율 신호는 자료에 없고 선택지에서도 쓰이지 않지만, 문제 될 정도는 아니다. 실제 SAT 이 유형은 보통 실제 데이터를 제시하는데, 이 문항은 가상 결과를 구성하는 형식이다.

problem.passage:
In the late nineteenth century, many steel firms in Germany's Ruhr district bought coal mines of their own instead of purchasing coal on the open market. Economic historian Lena Brandt notes that the vertically integrated firms, which owned both mines and mills, reported much lower costs for negotiating, monitoring, and enforcing coal deliveries than steel firms that bought from independent mines did. Brandt argues that integration itself caused these savings: once a mill owned its supplier, it no longer had to haggle over prices, write detailed contracts, or guard against a supplier withholding coal at critical moments. Critics point out, however, that the firms that integrated tended to be the largest and best-managed in the region to begin with.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Brandt's argument?
problem.stimulus: In the late nineteenth century, many steel firms in Germany's Ruhr district bought coal mines of their own instead of purchasing coal on the open market. Economic historian Lena Brandt notes that the vertically integrated firms, which owned both mines and mills, reported much lower costs for negotiating, monitoring, and enforcing coal deliveries than steel firms that bought from independent mines did. Brandt argues that integration itself caused these savings: once a mill owned its supplier, it no longer had to haggle over prices, write detailed contracts, or guard against a supplier withholding coal at critical moments. Critics point out, however, that the firms that integrated tended to be the largest and best-managed in the region to begin with.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Brandt's argument?
options: Across the Ruhr district, steel firms that owned coal mines consistently reported lower coal-procurement costs than steel firms of every size that did not own mines.

When individual steel firms acquired coal mines, their spending on contract negotiation and delivery enforcement fell sharply within a few years, even for firms whose size and management staff did not change.
Steel firms that had already achieved unusually low coal-procurement costs were later much more likely than other firms to acquire coal mines of their own.
During the period when integration spread, new railway lines across the Ruhr lowered transport costs for coal shipped from both independent and firm-owned mines.
problem.explanation:
정답 B: 같은 기업을 인수 전과 후로 비교하므로, 비판자들이 제기한 대안 설명(원래 크고 경영이 잘된 기업이라는 점)을 규모와 경영진이 변하지 않았다는 조건으로 통제한다. 비용 감소가 인수 뒤에 나타나므로 인과 방향도 '통합→절감'으로 맞는다. 따라서 통합 자체가 비용 절감을 낳았다는 Brandt의 주장을 직접 지지한다.
A(상관을 인과로 오해): 기업 규모를 맞춰 비교해도 결국 통합 기업과 비통합 기업을 한 시점에서 비교한 상관관계일 뿐이다. 통합 기업은 경영 능력처럼 다른 점에서도 달랐을 수 있으므로 통합이 원인임을 보여 주지 못한다.
C(인과 방향 반대): 비용이 낮은 기업이 나중에 통합했다는 것은 낮은 비용이 통합을 낳았음을 시사한다. 이는 오히려 Brandt의 주장을 약화한다.
D(무관한 제3의 원인): 철도는 독립 광산의 석탄과 기업 소유 광산의 석탄 모두의 비용을 낮췄다. 또 이는 운송비일 뿐 협상·감시·이행 같은 거래비용이 아니다. 통합의 효과를 가려내지 못하며, 오히려 다른 원인이 있었음을 보여 준다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, B: This finding compares the same firms before and after they acquired mines. Because their size and management stayed the same, it rules out the critics' alternative explanation that integrated firms were simply bigger and better run. The savings also came after the acquisition, so the cause runs from integration to lower costs. That directly supports Brandt's claim that integration itself caused the savings.
A mistakes correlation for causation. Even when firms of similar size are compared, it's still a snapshot of integrated firms versus non-integrated ones. The integrated firms could have differed in other ways, such as management quality, so this doesn't show that integration was the cause.
C reverses the direction of cause. If firms that already had low costs were the ones that later integrated, then low costs led to integration, not the other way around. That actually weakens Brandt's argument.
D offers an unrelated third cause. The railways cut costs for coal from both independent and firm-owned mines, and they affected transport costs, not the costs of negotiating, monitoring, and enforcing deliveries. So this finding can't single out integration as the cause of the savings.

hardJudge.note: 지문의 데이터(통합 기업의 낮은 거래비용)는 상관 사실이며, Brandt의 인과 주장은 검증 대상 가설로 제시되고 비판자가 선택편향(규모·경영) 대안을 명시함. B는 동일 기업 전후 비교 + 규모·경영진 불변 조건으로 교란요인을 통제하고 시간 순서로 인과 방향을 확정하므로 정답 타당. A는 규모만 통제한 횡단면 상관(경영 능력 미통제)으로 매력적 오답, C는 역인과, D는 제3 변수(운송비, 거래비용과 무관)로 역할 구분이 명확함. 해설의 논리·선택지 대응 모두 정확하며, 가상 Ruhr 경제사 설정으로 저작권·사실오류 우려 없음.

advisory.note: B는 같은 기업의 인수 전후를 비교하면서 규모와 경영진을 통제하고 시간 순서도 확보하므로, 비판자들이 제기한 교란 요인을 정확히 배제한다. A는 규모를 통제해 매력적인 오답이지만, 한 시점의 횡단 비교라서 경영 능력 같은 교란 요인이 남는다. C는 인과 방향이 반대이고, D는 운송비 이야기로 거래비용과 무관하다.

problem.passage:
Because cork oaks can be stripped of their bark only once every nine years, analysts long assumed that Portugal's cork industry would be held back by a supply too slow to keep pace with global demand. Recent studies of the cluster around Santa Maria da Feira, however, show that the nine-year harvesting cycle has in fact made supply highly predictable: processors know years in advance how much bark each estate will yield and plan their investments accordingly. Far from limiting the industry, the slow cycle has proved ______ to its long-term stability.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Because cork oaks can be stripped of their bark only once every nine years, analysts long assumed that Portugal's cork industry would be held back by a supply too slow to keep pace with global demand. Recent studies of the cluster around Santa Maria da Feira, however, show that the nine-year harvesting cycle has in fact made supply highly predictable: processors know years in advance how much bark each estate will yield and plan their investments accordingly. Far from limiting the industry, the slow cycle has proved ______ to its long-term stability.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: detrimental
somewhat inconvenient
incidental
integral
problem.explanation: 정답 D(integral): 'however'와 'Far from limiting' 뒤에서 느린 수확 주기가 공급을 예측 가능하게 만들어 산업 안정에 기여했다고 말하므로, 안정성에 '필수적인/핵심적인'이라는 뜻이 들어가야 한다. A(detrimental, 해로운)는 반박된 통념을 그대로 되풀이한 말이다. B(somewhat inconvenient, 다소 불편한)는 통념과 같은 부정적 방향이고 강도만 약하게 한 것이라 전환어와 맞지 않는다. C(incidental, 부수적인)는 해롭다/이롭다는 논점과 상관없이 '관련이 적다'는 제3의 의미여서, 주기 덕분에 투자 계획이 가능해졌다는 근거와 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: D (integral) is correct. The words "however" and "Far from limiting" signal a reversal: the slow harvesting cycle made supply predictable and allowed processors to plan their investments. That means the cycle is essential to the industry's stability. A (detrimental) just repeats the old assumption that the text rejects. B (somewhat inconvenient) points in the same negative direction as that assumption, only more weakly, so it ignores the reversal. C (incidental) brings in an unrelated idea, that the cycle barely matters, which contradicts the evidence that the cycle directly made planning possible.

hardJudge.note: 통념(공급 지연이 산업 발목) → however/in fact → 'Far from limiting' 부정 구조로 역전. 정답 integral은 통념 정반대 방향이며 예측가능성·투자계획 근거와 일치. A는 통념 방향, B는 통념 방향 약화형, C는 제3방향 오답으로 설계 충족. 'Far from limiting'의 부정 재구성이 추가 사고를 요구. 코르크 수확 주기 9년, Santa Maria da Feira 코르크 산업 클러스터는 사실과 부합.
