advisory.note: 정답 D는 맞고, 해설도 정답을 일관되게 뒷받침한다. 사실관계(9년 주기, Santa Maria da Feira 코르크 클러스터)에도 문제가 없다. 다만 'however', 'in fact', 'Far from limiting'이 한꺼번에 들어가 있어 빈칸의 방향이 지나치게 드러난다. 그래서 통념을 뒤집는 추론이 거의 자동으로 끝나 버린다. 오답 A와 B는 둘 다 부정적인 방향이라 바로 지워지고, 그럴듯한 오답은 C(incidental) 하나뿐이다. 이 정도면 전형적인 medium 수준이며 hard 특성은 사실상 발휘되지 않는다. 형식 면에서도 B만 구(phrase)이고 나머지는 단어라 선택지가 다소 고르지 않다.

problem.passage:
In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, much Swiss watchmaking ran on a cottage system. Merchants sent parts to farm families in the Jura Mountains, and each district specialized in a single stage of production: some valleys made rough movements, while workshops in Geneva finished cases and dials. It might seem that spreading production across so many households would have multiplied expenses. Economic historians argue, however, that the arrangement did not add to merchants' costs; instead, concentrating each task in one district ______ those costs. Neighbors shared specialized tools, trained one another's apprentices, and sent finished parts only short distances.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, much Swiss watchmaking ran on a cottage system. Merchants sent parts to farm families in the Jura Mountains, and each district specialized in a single stage of production: some valleys made rough movements, while workshops in Geneva finished cases and dials. It might seem that spreading production across so many households would have multiplied expenses. Economic historians argue, however, that the arrangement did not add to merchants' costs; instead, concentrating each task in one district ______ those costs. Neighbors shared specialized tools, trained one another's apprentices, and sent finished parts only short distances.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: pared
swelled
propped up
paired
problem.explanation:
정답 A(pared): 'did not add to costs; instead … ______ those costs' 구조에서 빈칸에는 '비용을 늘리다'와 극성이 반대인 말이 들어가야 한다. 이웃끼리 공구를 함께 쓰고, 서로의 견습생을 가르치고, 부품을 짧은 거리만 보냈다는 마지막 문장도 비용 절감을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 '깎아 줄이다'라는 뜻의 pared가 맞다.
B(swelled): '부풀리다'는 부정된 개념인 add to와 같은 뜻이다. 'not'을 무시한 오답이다.
C(propped up): '떠받쳐 유지하다'는 비용을 높은 수준으로 지탱한다는 뜻이다. 부정 뒤의 대조를 한 번 더 뒤집어 다시 비용을 높이는 쪽으로 읽은 오답이다.
D(paired): pared와 발음·철자가 비슷하지만 '짝짓다'라는 뜻이다. 비용에 대한 대조 구조와 아무 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice A, "pared," is correct. The sentence says the arrangement "did not add to" costs and that "instead" concentration ______ them. So the blank needs the opposite of increasing costs. The last sentence supports this: neighbors shared tools, trained one another's apprentices, and shipped parts only short distances. All of these save money, so "pared" (cut down) fits.
B, "swelled," means the same as "add to." It ignores the word "not."
C, "propped up," means holding costs at a high level. It reverses the contrast a second time, so the meaning goes back to costs staying high instead of falling.
D, "paired," looks and sounds like "pared" but means "matched in twos." That makes no sense with costs.

hardJudge.note: 'did not add to … costs; instead … ______ those costs' 구조가 부정+대조를 한 문장에 담고 있고, 앞의 'It might seem … multiplied expenses' 통념을 'however'로 뒤집는 2단계 구조까지 겹쳐 극성 역산을 요구한다. 정답 pared(비용 삭감)는 마지막 문장의 공구 공유·짧은 운송 거리 근거와 일치하며, 'pare costs'는 관용적으로 자연스럽다. B swelled는 부정어 무시 오답, C propped up은 비용을 높게 지탱한다는 이중 반전 오답, D paired는 철자 유사 오답으로 역할이 분명하다. 스위스 쥐라 지역 가내공업식 시계 생산(établissage)과 제네바 마감 공정은 역사적 사실과 부합한다. 해설에 모순이나 오류 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 pared(비용을 깎다)는 옳고 해설도 일관됨. 다만 'did not add to costs; instead ___ those costs'가 극성을 그대로 알려 주고, 마지막 문장도 비용 절감을 직접 뒷받침해 부정어 처리가 한 단계에 그친다. 이중부정 재구성이나 여러 단서 종합이 필요 없음. 'It might seem…however' 통념 반박 구조가 있지만 빈칸 판단에는 쓰이지 않음. 오답 중 swelled는 부정어를 무시한 단어로 전형적이고, paired는 철자만 비슷할 뿐 의미상 바로 배제되는 약한 오답이며, propped up은 극성을 이중으로 뒤집은 오답으로 보기에 다소 억지스럽다. 전체적으로 medium 수준임.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Norway's open-net salmon pens let sea lice and escaped farm fish spread into surrounding waters, imposing costs on wild salmon stocks and the river fisheries that depend on them. Because farm operators do not pay for this damage, some economists argue that the government should levy a per-tonne tax on farmed salmon output, so that the price of farmed fish reflects the harm it causes.

Text 2
In 2017, Norway divided its coast into production zones and began adjusting each zone's allowed growth according to measured lice levels on nearby wild salmon. Researchers studying the system note that the damage from a pen depends heavily on its location: a farm near a major salmon river's migration route can do far more harm than an equally large farm in a fjord that wild fish rarely pass through.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the proposal described in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Norway's open-net salmon pens let sea lice and escaped farm fish spread into surrounding waters, imposing costs on wild salmon stocks and the river fisheries that depend on them. Because farm operators do not pay for this damage, some economists argue that the government should levy a per-tonne tax on farmed salmon output, so that the price of farmed fish reflects the harm it causes.

Text 2
In 2017, Norway divided its coast into production zones and began adjusting each zone's allowed growth according to measured lice levels on nearby wild salmon. Researchers studying the system note that the damage from a pen depends heavily on its location: a farm near a major salmon river's migration route can do far more harm than an equally large farm in a fjord that wild fish rarely pass through.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the proposal described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that because farm operators do not pay for lice and escapes, farmed salmon is priced below its true cost to society
By maintaining that allowed growth in each production zone should be adjusted according to lice levels measured on wild salmon
By suggesting that a charge set only by the amount of salmon produced would fail to track how much harm a given farm actually causes
By arguing that a tax on farmed salmon would raise prices for consumers and weaken Norway's position in export markets
problem.explanation: 정답 C: Text 2의 전제는 피해가 생산량이 아니라 위치(야생 연어 이동 경로와의 거리)에 따라 크게 달라진다는 것이다. 따라서 톤당 일률 과세는 같은 생산량이라도 피해가 다른 양식장을 똑같이 취급하게 되어 실제 피해를 반영하지 못한다고 반응할 것이다. A: Text 1의 논거(외부비용 미지불)를 되풀이할 뿐 Text 2의 관점에서 나오는 반응이 아니다. B: Text 2가 소개한 제도(구역별 성장 조정)를 반복할 뿐, 톤당 세금이라는 제안에 대한 평가가 담겨 있지 않다. D: 소비자 가격·수출 경쟁력은 Text 2가 전혀 다루지 않은 쟁점이다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct. Text 2's key premise is that the harm a pen causes depends mainly on where it sits: a farm on a major river's migration route does far more damage than an equally large farm in a fjord that wild fish rarely pass through. A tax based only on tonnes produced would charge those two farms the same amount, so it wouldn't track the harm each one actually causes. A just repeats Text 1's own reasoning about unpaid costs, so it isn't a response that comes from Text 2's perspective. B restates the zone system Text 2 describes, but it never evaluates the per-tonne tax proposal. D brings in consumer prices and export markets, which Text 2 never discusses.

hardJudge.note: Text 2는 Text 1의 톤당 과세 제안을 언급하지 않으며, 정답 C는 Text 2의 '피해는 생산량이 아닌 위치에 좌우된다'는 전제를 Text 1의 제안에 적용해야만 도출된다. A는 Text 1 논거 반복, B는 Text 2 내용의 단순 재진술(제안에 대한 평가 없음), D는 본문 외 쟁점(소비자 가격·수출)으로 오답 구조가 레시피에 부합한다. 노르웨이 2017년 생산구역(신호등) 제도 서술도 사실과 일치한다. 해설은 정답과 오답 근거를 정확히 뒷받침한다.

advisory.note: Text 2는 톤당 세금을 언급하지 않는다. 피해가 위치에 따라 달라진다는 전제에서 생산량 기준 과세가 실제 피해를 반영하지 못한다는 반응을 추론해야 한다. B는 Text 2 내용을 반복하는 그럴듯한 오답이다. A는 Text 1을 반복하고 D는 본문에 없는 쟁점을 끌어온다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
For roughly a century and a half, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) kept cloves and nutmeg scarce and expensive in European markets. Company fleets made regular "extirpation" voyages to burn unauthorized clove trees on outlying islands, and garrisons on the Banda Islands guarded the nutmeg groves. Historian Pieter Lindqvist argues that this enforcement was what confined spice cultivation to Dutch-held islands. So when the company's naval patrols thinned in the 1760s and agents of the French administrator Pierre Poivre slipped seedlings out of the region, the monopoly's days were numbered.

Text 2
Botanist Amara Siregar's review of colonial garden records from Mauritius complicates the story of the smuggled seedlings. Most of the trees that Poivre's agents carried out died within months. Nutmeg in particular proved hard to grow: it needs specific soils, shade, and steady humidity, and it requires both male and female trees, which cannot be told apart until they flower years later. Profitable plantations outside the Moluccas appeared only after decades of repeated failed attempts.

Based on the texts, the author of Text 2 would most likely take issue with which element of the argument presented in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
For roughly a century and a half, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) kept cloves and nutmeg scarce and expensive in European markets. Company fleets made regular "extirpation" voyages to burn unauthorized clove trees on outlying islands, and garrisons on the Banda Islands guarded the nutmeg groves. Historian Pieter Lindqvist argues that this enforcement was what confined spice cultivation to Dutch-held islands. So when the company's naval patrols thinned in the 1760s and agents of the French administrator Pierre Poivre slipped seedlings out of the region, the monopoly's days were numbered.

Text 2
Botanist Amara Siregar's review of colonial garden records from Mauritius complicates the story of the smuggled seedlings. Most of the trees that Poivre's agents carried out died within months. Nutmeg in particular proved hard to grow: it needs specific soils, shade, and steady humidity, and it requires both male and female trees, which cannot be told apart until they flower years later. Profitable plantations outside the Moluccas appeared only after decades of repeated failed attempts.
problem.question: Based on the texts, the author of Text 2 would most likely take issue with which element of the argument presented in Text 1?
options: The claim that the VOC's control of the spice trade could not be sustained indefinitely once the late eighteenth century arrived
The claim that garrisons were stationed on the Banda Islands to protect the nutmeg groves
The claim that agents working for Poivre managed to carry spice seedlings out of Dutch-held territory
The claim that Dutch policing was the main obstacle that kept the spices from being grown in other places
problem.explanation:
정답 D: Text 1의 논증은 '단속(나무 소각·순찰)이 재배를 네덜란드 영토에 묶어 두었다'는 가정에 기대고 있으며, 그래서 단속이 약해지자 독점이 끝났다고 결론짓는다. Text 2는 밀반출된 묘목 대부분이 죽었고, 육두구는 토양·그늘·습도 조건이 까다로우며 암수 구별에도 수년이 걸려 수십 년간 재배에 실패했다고 보고한다. 즉 다른 지역에서 재배되지 못한 주된 이유는 단속이 아니라 원예적인 어려움일 수 있다는 것이므로, 바로 이 가정을 약화한다.
A(오답): Text 1의 결론에 해당한다. Text 2는 독점이 결국 끝났다는 사실 자체를 부정하지 않고, 이유를 설명하는 방식에만 문제를 제기한다.
B(오답): 부수적인 세부 사항이다. Text 2는 반다 제도의 수비대에 대해 아무 언급도 하지 않는다.
C(오답): Text 2가 오히려 전제로 받아들이는 내용이다. 묘목이 반출되었다는 사실은 인정하고, 반출된 묘목이 대부분 죽었다는 점만 덧붙인다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, D: Text 1's argument depends on an assumption: Dutch enforcement (burning trees and running patrols) was what kept spice growing limited to Dutch-held islands. That is why Text 1 concludes the monopoly ended once enforcement weakened. Text 2 reports that most smuggled seedlings died. Nutmeg needs particular soils, shade, and humidity, and growers had to wait years to tell male trees from female ones, so attempts failed for decades. This points to the difficulty of growing the plants, not policing, as the real barrier, which weakens exactly that assumption.
A is wrong: This is Text 1's conclusion. Text 2 never denies that the monopoly eventually ended. It only questions why.
B is wrong: This is a side detail. Text 2 says nothing about the garrisons on Banda.
C is wrong: Text 2 actually accepts this point. It agrees the seedlings were taken out and then explains that most of them died.

hardJudge.note: Text 1은 결론(독점의 종말)과 근거(단속이 재배를 묶어 둠, Lindqvist)가 명확히 구분됨. Text 2는 밀반출 사실(C)을 전제로 받아들이고, 독점이 결국 끝났다는 결론(A)도 부정하지 않으며, 수비대(B)는 언급하지 않음. 오직 '단속이 주된 장벽'이라는 가정만 원예적 난점으로 약화 → D 정답 타당. 실존 인물 Poivre의 밀반출 시기는 엄밀히 1769–1772년이지만 '1760년대'는 허용 범위의 근사로 판단, 가공 학자명 사용은 문제 없음. 결론과 가정을 구분하고 Text 2 관점에서 Text 1의 논증 요소를 평가해야 하므로 hard 적합.

advisory.note: Text 1의 결론('독점의 날이 얼마 남지 않았다')과 근거(단속이 재배를 묶어 두었다는 Lindqvist의 주장)가 분명히 나뉘어 있다. Text 2는 원예적 어려움을 들어 이 근거 가정을 겨냥하지만, Text 1을 직접 언급하지는 않는다. 그래서 반응을 추론해야 한다. A는 결론에 해당하고, C는 Text 2가 인정하는 사실을 담은 오답이다. A가 매력적인 오답으로 작동하려면 결론과 가정을 구분해야 한다. 다만 D의 핵심 단서가 Text 1에 거의 그대로 나와 있어서('this enforcement was what confined...') 난이도는 hard 하한선에 가깝다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Economists studying risk management in Australian agriculture often ask whether a hedging strategy "worked." In my view, a strategy should be judged not by whether it produced gains in a particular season but by whether it reduced the variability of a producer's income across many seasons. A hedge that loses money in a year when prices happen to rise has still done its job if it made earnings more predictable over time.

Text 2
When several grazier cooperatives in New South Wales began selling futures contracts on wool grease in 2019, they hoped to protect members from sudden price drops. That year, however, lanolin demand from cosmetics manufacturers surged, and spot prices for wool grease climbed sharply. The cooperatives, locked into lower contract prices, earned considerably less than unhedged neighbors. Many members concluded that the futures program had been a costly mistake, and two cooperatives abandoned it the following year.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the conclusion reached by the cooperative members described in Text 2?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Economists studying risk management in Australian agriculture often ask whether a hedging strategy "worked." In my view, a strategy should be judged not by whether it produced gains in a particular season but by whether it reduced the variability of a producer's income across many seasons. A hedge that loses money in a year when prices happen to rise has still done its job if it made earnings more predictable over time.

Text 2
When several grazier cooperatives in New South Wales began selling futures contracts on wool grease in 2019, they hoped to protect members from sudden price drops. That year, however, lanolin demand from cosmetics manufacturers surged, and spot prices for wool grease climbed sharply. The cooperatives, locked into lower contract prices, earned considerably less than unhedged neighbors. Many members concluded that the futures program had been a costly mistake, and two cooperatives abandoned it the following year.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the conclusion reached by the cooperative members described in Text 2?
options: As premature, because a single season's shortfall relative to unhedged producers says little about whether the program steadied members' earnings over a longer span
As reasonable, because the program left members earning substantially less than neighboring producers who chose not to hedge in 2019
As partly justified, because the program should be retained only if it eventually yields higher average profits than remaining unhedged would
As understandable, because unexpected shifts in cosmetics demand make wool grease prices too unpredictable for any financial strategy to manage
problem.explanation:
정답 A: Text 1 저자의 기준은 특정 시즌의 이익이 아니라 여러 시즌에 걸친 소득 변동성 감소이다. Text 2의 조합원들은 한 해(2019)의 손실만 보고 실패라 판단했으므로, Text 1 저자는 이를 성급한 결론으로 볼 것이다.
B: Text 2 조합원들의 기준(그해 이웃 대비 수익)으로 평가한 것으로, Text 1 저자가 명시적으로 거부한 기준이다.
C: 장기 관점(Text 1)과 수익 기준(Text 2)을 섞은 평가. Text 1 저자는 평균 이익이 아니라 예측 가능성을 기준으로 삼는다.
D: '가격이 너무 예측 불가하면 헤지가 무의미하다'는 일반 상식적 평가로, 오히려 변동성이 클수록 헤지의 의의가 있다는 Text 1 관점과 어긋나고 지문에 근거도 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
A is correct: The author of Text 1 judges a hedge by whether it reduces income variability across many seasons, not by results in one season. The members in Text 2 decided the program failed based only on 2019, when they earned less than unhedged neighbors. By Text 1's standard, that's a premature verdict, since one year can't show whether earnings became more predictable over time.
B is wrong because it uses the members' own standard (profit compared with neighbors in a single year), which is exactly the standard Text 1 rejects.
C is wrong because it blends the two views: it takes a long-term timeframe from Text 1 but keeps a profit-based test from Text 2. Text 1 cares about predictability, not higher average profits.
D is wrong because it relies on a general assumption that very volatile prices can't be managed. Text 1 actually implies that volatility is what hedging is meant to address, and neither text supports D's claim.

hardJudge.note: Text 1 기준(여러 시즌에 걸친 소득 변동성 감소, 단일 시즌 손익 무시)이 명시되어 있고, Text 2 조합원의 결론(한 해 손실로 'costly mistake' 판정)은 그 기준으로 '성급함'으로 판정 가능. A는 Text 1 기준에서만 도출됨. B는 Text 2 조합원의 기준(그해 이웃 대비 수익) 그대로, C는 장기 관점+평균 수익 기준 혼합(Text 1은 '예측 가능성'이지 '높은 평균 이익'이 아님), D는 지문 밖 일반 논리이며 Text 1과 충돌. 해설도 정답과 일관되고 모순 없음. 가상의 2019 wool grease 사례이나 사실 오류로 볼 만한 단정적 허위 진술은 없음. C가 'partly justified'라는 미묘한 강도 차이를 갖춰 calibrated_claim_strength도 요구함.

advisory.note: Text 1의 기준(여러 시즌에 걸친 변동성 감소)을 그대로 적용하면 '한 시즌 결과로 판단했다'는 점에서 A가 유일하게 성립한다. B는 Text 2 조합원들의 기준을 따른 것이고, C는 장기 관점과 수익 기준을 섞은 혼합형 오답이다. D는 헤지의 존재 이유와 정면으로 어긋난다. 문항이 전형적인 형태라 오답 매력도가 아주 높지는 않지만 hard 기준은 충족한다.

problem.passage:
In the early twentieth century, several German makers of optical lenses agreed to share their patents with one another. Before this arrangement, each firm used its own measurements for lens threads and mounts, so a lens from one company often would not fit a microscope from another. By pooling their patents, the firms were able to ______ these measurements, so that parts from different makers could finally be used together.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In the early twentieth century, several German makers of optical lenses agreed to share their patents with one another. Before this arrangement, each firm used its own measurements for lens threads and mounts, so a lens from one company often would not fit a microscope from another. By pooling their patents, the firms were able to ______ these measurements, so that parts from different makers could finally be used together.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: diversify
standardize
conceal
multiply
problem.explanation: 지문은 회사마다 측정 기준이 달라 부품이 서로 맞지 않았는데, 특허 공유 이후 여러 제조사의 부품을 함께 쓸 수 있게 되었다고 말한다. 따라서 측정 기준을 '통일하다'는 뜻의 B가 정답이다. A는 '다양화하다'로, 기준이 더 제각각이 되면 호환성 문제가 오히려 커진다. C는 '숨기다'로, 측정값을 숨기면 부품을 함께 쓸 수 있게 된다는 결과와 이어지지 않는다. D는 '늘리다'로, 기준의 수를 늘리는 것은 호환성을 높이는 것과 반대된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says each firm used different measurements, so parts did not fit together, and that after the patent pool, parts from different makers could finally be used together. That means the firms made the measurements uniform, so B is correct. A means "make more varied," which would make the fit problem worse. C means "hide," and hiding measurements would not let parts work together. D means "increase in number," and having more sets of measurements is the opposite of making parts compatible.

quality.seed: economics and business — German optical lens manufacturing and patent pools for precision instrument industry standardization early twentieth century

hardJudge.note: 지문 단서("each firm used its own measurements... would not fit", "could finally be used together")가 명시적이며 한 단계 추론으로 B(standardize)가 도출된다. 오답 A·D는 '다양화/늘리기'라는 반대 방향, C는 무관한 의미로 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제되나 표면적으로는 그럴듯하다. 역사적 배경(독일 광학 제조사 특허 공유)은 허구적 일반화 수준이라 사실 오류로 보기 어렵다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 영어 자연스러움.

advisory.note: 지문의 단서('각자 다른 측정 기준' → '마침내 함께 사용 가능')가 직접 드러나 한 단계 추론으로 standardize를 고를 수 있음. 오답 C(conceal), D(multiply)는 다소 쉽게 배제되지만 특허 공유 맥락에서 그럴듯해 보일 수 있어 easy 수준에 적합함.

problem.passage:
In the late 1500s, Spanish colonial officials in Peru forced Indigenous workers to labor in the silver mines of Potosí through a system called the mita. Workers were paid wages far below what they needed to survive, and many had to rely on their families to send food. Historians argue that these low wages were not accidental: officials deliberately kept pay ______ so that more of the mines' wealth would flow to Spain.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In the late 1500s, Spanish colonial officials in Peru forced Indigenous workers to labor in the silver mines of Potosí through a system called the mita. Workers were paid wages far below what they needed to survive, and many had to rely on their families to send food. Historians argue that these low wages were not accidental: officials deliberately kept pay ______ so that more of the mines' wealth would flow to Spain.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: generous
steady
meager
public
problem.explanation: 지문은 임금이 생존에 필요한 수준보다 훨씬 낮았고, 관리들이 부를 스페인으로 보내려고 일부러 임금을 낮게 유지했다고 말한다. 따라서 '아주 적은'이라는 뜻의 C(meager)가 정답이다. A(generous, 후한)는 지문 내용과 정반대이다. B(steady, 꾸준한)는 임금에 쓸 수는 있지만 금액이 적다는 핵심을 담지 못한다. D(public, 공개된)는 임금이 얼마나 낮았는지와 아무 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the wages were far below what workers needed to survive, and that officials kept pay low on purpose so more wealth would go to Spain. So C (meager), meaning very small, is the correct answer. A (generous) means the opposite of what the text describes. B (steady) can describe pay, but it doesn't say anything about the pay being small, which is the main point. D (public) has nothing to do with how low the wages were.

quality.seed: economics and business — Peruvian silver mining labor exploitation and encomienda system extracting colonial wealth through forced wage suppression

hardJudge.note: 지문에 'far below what they needed', 'low wages'가 직접 제시되어 한 단계 추론으로 C(meager)를 고를 수 있음. 오답은 반의어(generous), 임금에 어울리나 핵심 누락(steady), 무관(public)으로 전형적 오개념 구성. 역사적 사실(포토시 미타, 저임금) 정확. 한·영 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치. easy 적합.

advisory.note: Potosí mita 역사 서술은 대체로 정확함(1570년대 톨레도 개편). 단서 'far below what they needed to survive'가 직접 드러나 easy에 적합. D(public)는 다소 약한 오답이나 허용 범위.

problem.passage:
In his treatises on Noh theatre, the fifteenth-century actor and playwright Zeami Motokiyo praised moments he described as "where nothing is done." Between a dance and a chant, or between two gestures, a performer may stand completely still, and audiences often find these pauses more moving than the movements around them. Some modern commentators have treated such pauses as simple rests, breaks that let the actor recover and the audience absorb what came before. Zeami, however, insisted that the interval, later linked to the concept of ma, works only when the actor's inner concentration never slackens. If the performer's attention drifts during the stillness, he warned, the pause turns into mere emptiness and the audience loses interest. In Zeami's view, then, what spectators respond to in these moments is not the absence of action but a focused intensity that the actor keeps up without showing it outwardly.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: In his treatises on Noh theatre, the fifteenth-century actor and playwright Zeami Motokiyo praised moments he described as "where nothing is done." Between a dance and a chant, or between two gestures, a performer may stand completely still, and audiences often find these pauses more moving than the movements around them. Some modern commentators have treated such pauses as simple rests, breaks that let the actor recover and the audience absorb what came before. Zeami, however, insisted that the interval, later linked to the concept of ma, works only when the actor's inner concentration never slackens. If the performer's attention drifts during the stillness, he warned, the pause turns into mere emptiness and the audience loses interest. In Zeami's view, then, what spectators respond to in these moments is not the absence of action but a focused intensity that the actor keeps up without showing it outwardly.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Zeami held that the still intervals in Noh move audiences because the performer stays fully focused within them, not because they offer a break from action.
Zeami held that the still intervals in Noh move audiences because they give spectators time to reflect on the dances and chants that come before them.
Zeami held that the still intervals in Noh move audiences more than any dance or chant, so performers should lengthen them whenever possible.

problem.passage:
The Oaths of Strasbourg, sworn in 842 by two grandsons of Charlemagne, are often celebrated as the earliest surviving text in a language recognizably distinct from Latin. Because the chronicler Nithard recorded the oaths in the vernacular each army could understand, the document preserves forms such as "salvar" and "cadhuna," which show sound changes, including the weakening of Latin's final vowels, that had already pulled the spoken Romance of northern Gaul away from its parent tongue. Yet linguists caution against reading the text as a simple snapshot of everyday ninth-century speech. Nithard was trained in Latin, and his spellings frequently borrow Latin conventions, sometimes writing letters that speakers probably no longer pronounced. Scholars therefore treat the oaths as evidence that the shift had begun, while recognizing that the scribe's habits partly conceal how far it had progressed.

problem.passage:
Horace's Ars Poetica, a verse letter written around 19 BCE, offers only scattered advice about drama: a play should have no more and no fewer than five acts, violent deeds are better reported than shown, and a god should not intervene unless the plot truly demands it. Horace presented these remarks casually, often with humor, and never organized them into a system. Yet when Renaissance critics such as Julius Caesar Scaliger and Lodovico Castelvetro rediscovered the poem, they combined its offhand suggestions with passages from Aristotle and recast them as binding laws. By the seventeenth century, French academicians were judging new tragedies largely by how faithfully they observed these "rules," and playwrights such as Pierre Corneille felt compelled to publish essays defending their departures from them. In this way, a loosely composed letter came to shape, for more than two centuries, the standards by which European critics measured a play's structure.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.passage:
Ukiyo-e prints are often admired today as polished images of actors, courtesans, and famous landscapes, but historians of Edo-period Japan (1603–1868) increasingly value them for another reason. Because each print was produced collaboratively—a designer drew the image, a carver cut it into cherry-wood blocks, and a printer applied pigments block by block—publishers could issue hundreds of inexpensive copies within weeks of an event. Prints therefore appeared quickly in response to what city residents were talking about: a new kabuki production, a fashionable hairstyle, a fire that swept through a neighborhood. Historian Mariko Ishida argues that this speed makes surviving prints a kind of running record of Edo's urban life, capturing passing tastes and incidents that official government documents, concerned mainly with taxation and order, rarely mention.

When acrylic paintings from the Western Desert community of Papunya began appearing in Australian galleries in the 1970s, many collectors admired them as striking abstract compositions of dots, circles, and lines. For the Anmatyerr and Pintupi artists who made them, however, the works were closer to maps: concentric circles could mark waterholes or ceremonial sites, and connecting lines could trace the routes ancestral beings traveled during the Dreaming. Because some of this knowledge was restricted to initiated people, artists soon began covering sacred details with fields of dots, so that a painting could circulate in the market while its most guarded meanings stayed hidden from outside buyers. The commercial success of the style, in other words, depended partly on what the paintings deliberately concealed.

advisory.note: 파푸냐 점묘 회화가 신성한 세부를 가렸다는 내용은 실제 역사와 부합함. A와 B는 지문에 맞는 부분을 일부 담고 있어 비교해야 배제되고, C는 지문 밖의 그럴듯한 내용으로 구성되어 medium 난이도에 적합함.

problem.passage:
When Francesco Petrarch composed his sonnets in fourteenth-century Italy, he divided each poem into an eight-line octave that posed a problem or longing and a six-line sestet that answered or reconsidered it. English poets who adopted the form two centuries later found Italian's abundant rhymes hard to reproduce, so writers such as Shakespeare rearranged the fourteen lines into three quatrains and a closing couplet, which often delivered a sudden twist. Some literary historians describe this change as a loss of Petrarchan balance, but the shift in structure actually preserved the sonnet's central habit: building toward a decisive turn in thought. Modernist poets of the twentieth century went further, abandoning regular rhyme and meter altogether, yet many of their fourteen-line poems still pivot sharply partway through. Across these centuries, then, the sonnet's outward architecture proved negotiable, while its reliance on a turning point endured.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: When Francesco Petrarch composed his sonnets in fourteenth-century Italy, he divided each poem into an eight-line octave that posed a problem or longing and a six-line sestet that answered or reconsidered it. English poets who adopted the form two centuries later found Italian's abundant rhymes hard to reproduce, so writers such as Shakespeare rearranged the fourteen lines into three quatrains and a closing couplet, which often delivered a sudden twist. Some literary historians describe this change as a loss of Petrarchan balance, but the shift in structure actually preserved the sonnet's central habit: building toward a decisive turn in thought. Modernist poets of the twentieth century went further, abandoning regular rhyme and meter altogether, yet many of their fourteen-line poems still pivot sharply partway through. Across these centuries, then, the sonnet's outward architecture proved negotiable, while its reliance on a turning point endured.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although poets repeatedly reshaped the sonnet's structure, the form's characteristic shift in thought has persisted.
Although Shakespeare altered the sonnet's structure to suit English, his version lost the balance that defined Petrarch's poems.
Although modernist poets abandoned rhyme and meter, their poems no longer qualify as true sonnets.
Although Italian offered abundant rhymes, Petrarch's octave-and-sestet design was difficult for any poet to master.
problem.explanation: 지문은 페트라르카, 셰익스피어, 모더니즘을 거치며 소네트의 외형 구조는 바뀌었지만 사고의 전환(turn)은 지속되었다고 결론짓므로 A가 정답이다. B는 일부 학자의 견해를 언급할 뿐, 필자는 'actually'로 이를 반박한다. C는 모더니스트가 운율을 버렸다는 세부는 맞지만, 지문은 그들의 시도 여전히 전환을 유지한다고 하며 소네트 자격을 부정하지 않는다. D는 영어로 각운을 맞추기 어려웠다는 내용을 왜곡했고, 일부 세부에 불과하다.
problem.explanationEn: The text follows the sonnet from Petrarch through Shakespeare to modernism and concludes that its outward structure changed while its turning point endured, so A is correct. B repeats a view that some historians hold, but the author rejects that view with "actually." C gets one detail right (modernists dropped rhyme and meter), but the text says their poems still pivot and never denies that they are sonnets. D distorts the passage: the difficulty with rhyme belonged to English poets, not to Petrarch's design, and it is only a minor detail anyway.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The evolution of the sonnet form from Petrarch through Shakespeare to modernism

hardJudge.note: 지문 마지막 문장이 A를 직접 뒷받침하며, B는 'some literary historians'의 견해를 필자가 'actually'로 반박하는 구조를 정독해야 배제됨. C는 모더니스트의 운율 포기라는 세부는 맞으나 결론이 지문과 반대. D는 영어 시인의 각운 어려움을 페트라르카 구조로 왜곡. 두 해설 모두 정답·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 역사적 사실(14세기 페트라르카, 약 2세기 후 영국 소네트, 모더니즘의 자유시형 소네트)도 타당. 지문은 창작물로 보임.

advisory.note: 마지막 문장의 결론과 'actually'로 시작하는 반박 구조를 연결해야 답이 나온다. B(일부 학자의 견해)와 C(모더니즘 세부)는 지문 내용과 부분적으로 맞아서 비교해 봐야 배제된다. D는 언어 관계를 왜곡한 오답이지만 그럴듯하다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
In many Sufi communities of the Ottoman and Persian worlds, learning calligraphy was not treated simply as training in a decorative craft. Students often spent years copying a single master's letterforms, and teachers described this repetition as a discipline of the self: by subordinating personal habits of the hand to an inherited model, the copyist was thought to cultivate humility and patience. Some scholars have therefore argued that the elegance of Sufi-influenced calligraphy should be read less as an individual artist's achievement than as visible evidence of that inner effort. On this view, a balanced, unhurried line mattered because it signaled a balanced, unhurried spirit, so that aesthetic quality and spiritual formation were understood as two aspects of the same practice.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

On this view, a balanced, unhurried line mattered because it signaled a balanced, unhurried spirit, so that aesthetic quality and spiritual formation were understood as two aspects of the same practice.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: In Sufi communities, calligraphy students valued the decorative appeal of letterforms more highly than the moral lessons their teachers emphasized.
In Sufi communities, the beauty of calligraphy was understood as an outward sign of the spiritual discipline that producing it required.
In Sufi communities, calligraphy students copied a master's letterforms mainly to preserve historical styles that might otherwise have been lost.
In Sufi communities, the beauty of calligraphy was understood as proof of an individual artist's unique talent rather than of shared tradition.
problem.explanation: 지문은 대가의 글씨를 반복해 베끼는 일이 겸손과 인내를 기르는 수양으로 여겨졌고, 그래서 우아한 서체가 그 내적 노력을 눈에 보이게 드러낸 것으로 이해되었다고 말한다. 따라서 미적 아름다움을 영적 수련의 외적 표지로 본 B가 정답이다. A는 '장식적 공예'라는 표현을 활용하지만, 지문은 서예가 단순한 장식 기술로 취급되지 않았다고 말하므로 내용이 반대다. C는 대가의 글씨를 베꼈다는 사실은 맞지만, 그 목적을 양식 보존으로 제시하는데 지문은 목적을 자기 수양으로 설명한다. D는 지문이 개인의 성취로 읽어서는 안 된다고 한 점과 정반대다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says that copying a master's letterforms over and over was treated as self-discipline that built humility and patience. It then says an elegant line was seen as visible evidence of that inner effort. That makes B correct, because it describes beauty as an outward sign of spiritual discipline. A borrows the word "decorative," but the text says calligraphy was not treated simply as a decorative craft, so A gets the passage backward. C is right that students copied a master's work, but the text gives self-discipline as the reason, not preserving old styles. D says the opposite of the text, which argues that the elegance should be read less as an individual artist's achievement.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Sufi calligraphy as spiritual practice and aesthetic principle in Islamic art

hardJudge.note: 지문 마지막 두 문장(우아한 선 = 내적 노력의 가시적 증거, 미적 질과 영적 형성이 동일 실천의 두 측면)이 B를 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 '장식적'이라는 지문 어휘를 차용했으나 지문이 명시적으로 부정한 내용이고, C는 '대가의 글씨 베끼기'라는 세부는 맞지만 목적을 잘못 제시하며, D는 '개인 예술가의 성취'라는 지문 표현을 반대 방향으로 뒤집었다. 지문을 정독해야 B의 '외적 표지' 관계를 포착할 수 있고, C가 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하므로 medium에 적합하다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 역사적 서술은 '일부 학자들은 주장했다'는 완충 표현을 사용해 사실 오류 위험이 낮다.

advisory.note: B는 지문 마지막 두 문장(우아함 = 내적 노력의 가시적 증거, 미와 영적 수양은 하나)을 정확히 요약한다. C는 '베끼기'라는 사실은 맞지만 목적이 틀린 오답이고, D는 B와 같은 틀('beauty ... was understood as')을 쓰면서 'less ... than' 구조를 뒤집어 놓아서 훑어 읽으면 틀릴 수 있다. A는 'not simply decorative'와 반대여서 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 경계선에 있지만 medium에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
In nineteenth-century France, the Academy of Fine Arts ranked painting by subject. History painting—large canvases of mythological, biblical, or heroic scenes—sat at the top, while scenes of ordinary life were considered minor genres suited only to small formats. Gustave Courbet's A Burial at Ornans (1849–1850) deliberately broke this rule. The painting depicts an unremarkable funeral in Courbet's provincial hometown, attended by local villagers, yet it stretches more than six meters wide, the scale traditionally reserved for depictions of gods and kings. When it was shown at the Salon of 1850–1851, many critics condemned it as crude, but they were reacting less to its technique than to the claim its size implied: that the lives of rural laborers were as worthy of monumental treatment as the deeds of emperors.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Gustave Courbet's A Burial at Ornans (1849–1850) deliberately broke this rule. The painting depicts an unremarkable funeral in Courbet's provincial hometown, attended by local villagers, yet it stretches more than six meters wide, the scale traditionally reserved for depictions of gods and kings. When it was shown at the Salon of 1850–1851, many critics condemned it as crude, but they were reacting less to its technique than to the claim its size implied: that the lives of rural laborers were as worthy of monumental treatment as the deeds of emperors.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: By painting a village funeral at a size normally given to elevated subjects, Courbet challenged the Academy's view of which subjects deserved importance.
By painting a village funeral with crude technique, Courbet challenged the Academy's standards for how skillfully paintings should be executed.
By painting a village funeral for the Salon, Courbet challenged the Academy's preference for mythological scenes over biblical ones.
By painting a village funeral in his hometown, Courbet challenged critics who believed provincial artists could not exhibit at the Salon.
problem.explanation: A가 정답이다. 지문은 아카데미의 주제 위계를 설명한 뒤, 쿠르베가 평범한 장례식을 역사화 크기로 그려 농민의 삶도 기념비적으로 다룰 가치가 있다고 주장했다는 점을 핵심으로 삼는다. B는 비평가들이 '조잡하다'고 했다는 표현을 이용했지만, 지문은 그들이 기법보다 크기가 함축한 주장에 반응했다고 말하므로 틀리다. C는 신화화와 성서화를 모두 최상위로 묶은 지문 내용과 어긋난다. D는 지방 출신 화가의 출품 자격에 대한 이야기로, 지문에 근거가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: A is correct. The text explains the Academy's ranking of subjects, then shows that Courbet painted an ordinary funeral at the huge scale reserved for history painting, which implied that rural lives deserved monumental treatment. B picks up the word "crude," but the text says critics were reacting less to technique than to the claim made by the painting's size. C is wrong because the text places mythological and biblical scenes together at the top of the ranking, not one above the other. D brings up a question about provincial artists' right to exhibit, which the text never mentions.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Gustave Courbet's Realism movement challenging academic painting hierarchy

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산 일치: 지문은 아카데미의 주제 위계 → 쿠르베가 평범한 장례식을 역사화 규모로 제작 → 크기가 함축한 주장(농민의 삶도 기념비적 가치)이라는 구조로, A가 핵심을 정확히 요약. B는 '조잡하다'는 비평 표현을 활용하지만 마지막 문장("less to its technique than to the claim its size implied")을 정독해야 배제되는 양질의 오답. C는 신화·성서 장면을 함께 최상위로 둔 지문과 모순, D는 지방 화가의 출품 자격 논의가 지문에 없음(둘 다 지문 어휘를 차용해 그럴듯함). 사실 관계(Burial at Ornans 1849–50, 약 6.6m 폭, 1850–51 살롱 출품, 아카데미 장르 위계) 정확. 한·영 해설 모두 선택지 글자 참조 일치, 모순 없음, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 난이도는 B가 정독을 요구하는 핵심 오답이고 C·D는 다소 쉽게 배제되나 medium 범위 내로 판단.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 옳고, 사실관계(1849–50년 제작, 폭 약 6.6m, 1850–51년 살롱)도 맞다. 다만 그럴듯한 오답은 B('crude'를 이용한 함정) 하나뿐이다. C는 지문에 없는 신화화와 성서화 사이의 우열을 내세우고, D는 지문에 없는 출품 자격 문제를 내세운다. 둘 다 표면적인 단어만 빌려 왔을 뿐 부분적인 근거가 약해서 바로 배제된다. 따라서 '오답 중 최소 2개는 부분적 근거를 가질 것'이라는 medium 기준에 못 미친다.

problem.passage:
After the Great Fire of 1666 destroyed most of the City of London, Christopher Wren was commissioned to rebuild more than fifty parish churches. Many of the sites he inherited were cramped, irregular plots hemmed in by surviving houses and lanes, so a single standard plan was impossible. Rather than forcing a uniform design onto each lot, Wren treated every church as a separate problem, fitting naves into odd angles and placing entrances wherever the street allowed. Yet he held firmly to one priority across these varied buildings: that the congregation should be able to see the pulpit and hear the preacher clearly. Wren argued that a Protestant church was essentially an "auditory," a room for listening, and he kept interiors compact and largely free of obstructing columns. The striking towers and steeples that rose above the rooftops, often designed years after the main structures were finished, gave each church a distinctive public face, but the logic of the interior began with the spoken word.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus: After the Great Fire of 1666 destroyed most of the City of London, Christopher Wren was commissioned to rebuild more than fifty parish churches. Many of the sites he inherited were cramped, irregular plots hemmed in by surviving houses and lanes, so a single standard plan was impossible. Rather than forcing a uniform design onto each lot, Wren treated every church as a separate problem, fitting naves into odd angles and placing entrances wherever the street allowed. Yet he held firmly to one priority across these varied buildings: that the congregation should be able to see the pulpit and hear the preacher clearly. Wren argued that a Protestant church was essentially an "auditory," a room for listening, and he kept interiors compact and largely free of obstructing columns. The striking towers and steeples that rose above the rooftops, often designed years after the main structures were finished, gave each church a distinctive public face, but the logic of the interior began with the spoken word.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Wren adapted his church plans to irregular sites mainly so that each building could display a tower more distinctive than those of its neighbors.
Wren varied the layouts of his churches to suit difficult sites while consistently designing interiors so that worshippers could see and hear the sermon.
Wren abandoned the idea of a standard plan because the fire had left too few intact streets to guide the placement of entrances.
Wren designed compact interiors without columns primarily because the narrow plots left too little room for heavy structural supports.
problem.explanation: 지문은 부지가 불규칙해 각 교회를 따로 설계했지만(변화), 회중이 설교자를 보고 들을 수 있게 한다는 원칙은 일관되게 지켰다(불변)는 두 정보를 연결하는 것이 핵심이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 탑이 독특했다는 사실은 맞지만, 탑은 흔히 나중에 설계되었고 실내 논리는 설교에서 출발했다고 했으므로 부지 적응의 주된 이유로 볼 수 없다. C는 표준 설계를 포기한 것은 맞지만, 이유는 비좁고 불규칙한 부지 때문이지 남은 거리가 적어서가 아니다. D는 기둥 없는 실내라는 세부는 맞지만, 지문은 그 이유를 구조적 공간 부족이 아니라 청취와 시야 확보로 설명한다.
problem.explanationEn: The key is to connect two ideas: Wren designed each church separately because the sites were irregular (what changed), but he always made sure the congregation could see and hear the preacher (what stayed the same). That's why B is correct. A is right that the towers were distinctive, but the towers were often designed later, and the text says the interior logic started from the spoken word, so towers weren't the main reason he adapted to the sites. C is right that Wren gave up on a standard plan, but the reason was cramped, irregular plots, not a shortage of surviving streets. D gets the column-free interiors right, but the text explains them by the need to see and hear, not by a lack of room for structural supports.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — The architectural principles of Christopher Wren's baroque church reconstruction post-1666

hardJudge.note: 지문의 '변화(부지별 설계)+불변(청취·시야 우선)' 구조를 B가 정확히 요약. A·C·D 모두 지문의 실제 세부(독특한 탑, 표준 설계 포기, 기둥 없는 실내)를 포함하되 인과를 왜곡해 비교가 필요하므로 medium 적합. 역사적 사실(1666년 대화재, Wren의 50여 교회 재건, 'auditory' 개념, 첨탑의 후기 설계) 모두 정확. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: B가 지문의 두 요소, 즉 부지에 따른 설계 변화와 설교를 보고 듣게 한다는 일관된 원칙을 함께 담고 있다. A, C, D는 각각 지문의 실제 세부(독특한 탑, 표준 설계 포기, 기둥 없는 실내)를 쓰면서 이유를 잘못 연결한 오답이라 서로 비교해야 배제된다. medium 수준에 맞다. 'largely free'를 'without columns'로 바꾼 것은 오답 선택지 안의 표현이므로 문제없다.

problem.passage:
During the eighth and ninth centuries, the Byzantine Empire was divided by a bitter dispute over religious images, or icons. Iconoclasts, who sought to remove such images from churches, are often remembered as simple destroyers of art, but historian Leslie Brubaker argues that many of their objections were carefully reasoned. Iconoclast theologians contended that a painted figure of Christ could depict only his human form and not his divine nature, so any such image either separated the two natures or wrongly claimed to capture the divine. Defenders of icons, most notably John of Damascus, responded with an equally technical argument: veneration directed at an image passes to the person it represents, so honoring an icon is not the same as worshipping wood and paint. In Brubaker's view, the controversy was therefore less a clash between lovers and haters of art than a sustained debate about how the divine could, or could not, be made visible.

problem.passage:
Histories of medieval music often credit the composers of Notre-Dame in Paris, such as Léonin and Pérotin, with transforming plainchant into elaborate polyphony around 1200. Yet manuscripts associated with the cathedral school at Chartres suggest that experiments with layering voices were under way there more than a century earlier. Fragments copied at Chartres in the late eleventh century record a second vocal line moving against the chant, sometimes in contrary motion rather than in strict parallel, a technique that later Parisian singers would refine. Because many of these Chartres fragments were damaged or scattered over the centuries, scholars have only recently begun to compare them systematically with the better-preserved Parisian sources. That comparison indicates that the Notre-Dame achievement, while remarkable, built on practices that cathedral musicians elsewhere, including at Chartres, had already been developing.

problem.passage:
In the years after the 1917 Russian Revolution, many artists associated with Constructivism argued that painting on canvas was a relic of a private, bourgeois culture and should give way to useful design for posters, books, and buildings. El Lissitzky shared their desire to serve the new society, but he did not simply abandon abstract art. Beginning around 1919, he produced a series of works he called Prouns, in which geometric solids appear to float, tilt, and recede in ways that no single vanishing point can explain. Lissitzky described the Prouns as an "interchange station between painting and architecture," and he later carried their shifting perspectives into exhibition rooms, typography, and book layouts. For Lissitzky, then, abstraction was not an escape from practical work but a laboratory in which new ways of organizing space could be tested before being applied to the designed environment.

problem.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, editors of Emily Dickinson's poems quietly "corrected" her manuscripts, replacing her many dashes with commas and periods and lowering her idiosyncratic capital letters. Their assumption was that these marks were careless habits of private writing, not deliberate choices. __Yet when scholar Thomas H. Johnson restored the original markings in his 1955 edition, readers found that a single dash could hold two clauses in suspension, letting a line be read as both the end of one thought and the beginning of another.__ Later critics built on this observation, arguing that Dickinson's capitals similarly elevate ordinary nouns—"Hope," "Death," "Noon"—into something like abstract presences. For these scholars, her punctuation is less an obstacle to meaning than a second grammar operating alongside the words themselves.

problem.passage:
In fourteenth- and fifteenth-century English towns such as York and Chester, cycles of mystery plays dramatized biblical history from the Creation to the Last Judgment, with each episode staged on a wagon that rolled from one station to the next through the streets. problem.passage:
Filmmakers who adapt Virginia Woolf's novels face a peculiar problem: her narratives unfold less through events than through the drifting thoughts of characters, which slide from memory to perception to fantasy within a single sentence. Many critics have assumed that voice-over narration is the obvious cinematic solution, since it lets audiences hear a character's inner monologue directly. __Yet in her 1992 adaptation of Woolf's Orlando, director Sally Potter largely avoided extended voice-over, instead having her protagonist glance knowingly into the camera and deliver brief asides to the viewer.__ These moments, film scholars note, reproduce not the content of Woolf's interior passages but their effect: the reader's sense of being drawn into a private, shifting consciousness that is aware of its own performance.

D is wrong because the first sentence, not the underlined one, identifies the problem.

problem.passage:
Western listeners encountering a raga performance for the first time often assume that the musician is simply improvising freely, inventing melodies moment by moment. In fact, a raga supplies a dense set of constraints: a fixed collection of pitches, characteristic ascending and descending patterns, emphasized notes, and even associations with particular times of day. Rhythm is governed just as strictly by the tala, a repeating cycle of beats, such as the sixteen-beat tintal, that the performer must never lose. __Yet within these limits, a skilled musician may spend nearly an hour exploring a single raga without repeating a phrase, extending a line across several cycles before resolving it precisely on the first beat, called sam.__ Musicologist Lalita Rao argues that this tension is the point: the framework does not restrict creativity so much as give listeners a structure against which inventive departures and timely returns become audible.

B는 즉흥의 폭을 보여 준다는 점은 맞지만, 연주자가 여전히 sam에 정확히 돌아온다고 하므로 제약이 느슨하다는 뜻이 아니다. D는 자유로운 즉흥을 언급한다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 지문은 그 첫 가정을 오히려 바로잡는다.

Since the early 2000s, the stenciled images attributed to Banksy—a girl releasing a heart-shaped balloon, a protester hurling a bouquet of flowers—have often been treated as statements whose force depends on the artist's hidden identity. Many critics argue that anonymity lets the works speak as if from the street itself rather than from a single person with a career to protect. By around 1909, Arnold Schoenberg had abandoned the tonal system that had organized Western music for centuries, writing pieces in which no single pitch served as a "home" note. Critics often called this music chaotic, but Schoenberg himself found a different problem with it: without tonality's pull toward a central key, he struggled to sustain longer compositions, and many of his atonal works from this period are remarkably brief. __His solution, developed in the early 1920s, was to arrange all twelve pitches of the chromatic scale into a fixed sequence, or "row," that would govern the melodies and harmonies of an entire piece.__ Because no pitch could recur until the other eleven had sounded, the row prevented any note from gaining tonal prominence while still giving the composer a consistent structure on which to build extended works.

problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "His history plays often jump across decades"와 뒤 "some scenes take place years apart..."는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 쉼표와 등위접속사 and로 연결할 수 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 쉼표 스플라이스이다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 문장 흐름을 부자연스럽게 끊는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank, "His history plays often jump across decades," and the text after it, "some scenes take place years apart...," are both independent clauses. You can join two independent clauses with a comma plus a coordinating conjunction such as "and," so A is correct. B uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds a comma after "and" that doesn't belong there and breaks up the sentence for no reason.

problem.explanationEn: The art historian claims that Vicuña's works are meant to help people remember Andean traditions nearly lost under colonial rule. Choice A has Vicuña herself saying she makes the installations so viewers will recall record-keeping practices that colonial authorities tried to erase, which directly supports that purpose. Choice B gives a practical reason about the material, choice C a reason about eye-catching color, and choice D a reason about the size of the exhibition space, and none of these has anything to do with cultural memory. In fact, B, C, and D fit the critics' "purely decorative" view better.

problem.passage:
In eighteenth-century writings on art, the "sublime" described scenes that inspire awe mixed with fear, such as towering cliffs or violent storms. Philosopher Edmund Burke argued that a sense of danger is essential to the sublime: viewers feel it only when a scene suggests a threat that they themselves are safe from. An art historian proposes that landscape painters of the period followed Burke's idea and deliberately included signs of danger, such as crumbling rocks or dark storm clouds, in paintings meant to be seen as sublime.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the art historian's proposal?
problem.stimulus: In eighteenth-century writings on art, the "sublime" described scenes that inspire awe mixed with fear, such as towering cliffs or violent storms. Philosopher Edmund Burke argued that a sense of danger is essential to the sublime: viewers feel it only when a scene suggests a threat that they themselves are safe from. An art historian proposes that landscape painters of the period followed Burke's idea and deliberately included signs of danger, such as crumbling rocks or dark storm clouds, in paintings meant to be seen as sublime.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the art historian's proposal?
options: Many eighteenth-century landscape paintings were bought by wealthy collectors who displayed them in large country houses.
Paintings that eighteenth-century critics labeled sublime showed threatening features such as falling rocks or storms far more often than other landscapes did.
Eighteenth-century landscape paintings described as sublime were usually larger in size than paintings of gardens or farms.
Some eighteenth-century painters traveled to the Alps to make sketches before painting their landscapes in studios.
problem.explanation: 미술사학자의 주장은 숭고하게 보이도록 의도된 그림에 화가들이 위험의 징후를 일부러 넣었다는 것이다. B는 숭고하다고 평가된 그림에 위협적인 요소가 다른 풍경화보다 훨씬 자주 나타났음을 보여 주므로 이 주장을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 누가 그림을 샀는지에 관한 내용일 뿐 위험의 징후와는 관계가 없다. C는 그림의 크기를 다루므로 위험 요소에 대해서는 아무것도 알려 주지 않는다. D는 화가들이 위험할 수 있는 장소를 방문했다는 내용이지만, 그림 속에 위험의 징후가 담겼는지는 보여 주지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The art historian claims that painters deliberately put signs of danger into paintings meant to be seen as sublime. B supports this directly because it shows that paintings labeled sublime featured threatening elements much more often than other landscapes did. A is only about who bought the paintings and has nothing to do with signs of danger. C deals with the size of the paintings, so it tells you nothing about dangerous elements. D says painters visited places that might be dangerous, but it doesn't show that signs of danger actually appeared in the paintings.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 버크의 숭고 개념(안전한 거리에서의 위험)을 역사적으로 정확히 요약했고, 사학자의 주장(숭고 그림에 위험 징후를 의도적으로 포함)을 B가 직접 뒷받침한다. A(구매자), C(크기), D(알프스 스케치)는 그럴듯하지만 '그림 속 위험 징후' 여부를 보여주지 않아 한 단계 추론으로 배제 가능. 한·영 해설이 동일 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 영어는 자연스럽고 한글 없음. easy 적합.

problem.passage:

Valdés notes that Carrington's early Mexican portraits commissioned by patrons show women in fairly customary domestic poses, whereas a later group of private works depicts women as sorceresses reconfiguring the kitchen into a laboratory. If Valdés is correct, a viewer comparing these two groups should expect that ______

problem.stimulus: Art historian Mira Valdés argues that in Leonora Carrington's paintings, the density of alchemical symbolism—crucibles, eggs, distilling vessels—tracks how far a work departs from conventional depictions of women. In Valdés's account, Carrington borrowed alchemy's language of transmutation precisely because it offered a ready vocabulary for imagining female figures who escape assigned roles; the more transgressive the vision of womanhood a canvas pursued, the more heavily it leaned on that borrowed vocabulary. Valdés notes that Carrington's early Mexican portraits commissioned by patrons show women in fairly customary domestic poses, whereas a later group of private works depicts women as sorceresses reconfiguring the kitchen into a laboratory. If Valdés is correct, a viewer comparing these two groups should expect that ______

options: the private works will contain markedly more crucibles, eggs, and other alchemical motifs than the commissioned portraits do.
the commissioned portraits will contain markedly more crucibles, eggs, and other alchemical motifs than the private works do.
the private works became more transgressive because Carrington first decided to add more alchemical motifs to them.
the private works will differ from the commissioned portraits mainly in being painted on larger canvases with brighter pigments.
problem.explanation:
정답 A: Valdés의 이론은 '여성상이 더 위반적일수록 연금술 상징이 더 많다'는 정비례 관계다. 후기 개인 작품(부엌을 실험실로 바꾸는 마녀)이 의뢰 초상(관습적 가사 자세)보다 더 위반적이므로, 연금술 모티프가 더 많을 것으로 예상된다.
B: 관계의 방향을 뒤집은 오답이다. 관습적인 초상화에 상징이 더 많다는 것은 이론과 정반대다.
C: 인과를 뒤바꾼 오답이다. 이론은 위반적 비전을 추구하기 위해 연금술 어휘를 빌렸다고 하므로, 위반성이 원인이고 상징 사용은 결과다. 또한 이 선택지는 두 집단을 비교했을 때 무엇을 보게 될지 예측하지 않는다.
D: 이론과 무관한 제3의 요인(캔버스 크기·안료)을 결론으로 내세운 오답이다.
problem.explanationEn:
A is correct. Valdés's theory sets up a direct relationship: the more transgressive a canvas's vision of womanhood, the more it relies on alchemical symbolism. The later private works, which show sorceresses turning the kitchen into a laboratory, are more transgressive than the commissioned portraits of women in customary domestic poses. So the private works should contain more alchemical motifs.
B flips the direction of the relationship. It assigns more symbolism to the more conventional works.
C reverses cause and effect. In the theory, Carrington borrowed alchemical vocabulary in order to pursue a transgressive vision, so transgression is the cause and the symbolism is the result. C also fails to predict what a viewer comparing the two groups would actually see.
D brings in a factor the theory never mentions (canvas size and pigment), so nothing in the passage supports it.

hardJudge.note: 이론(위반성↑ → 연금술 상징↑)이 명시되고, 의뢰 초상(관습적)·개인 작품(마녀/실험실)이라는 두 집단에 적용해 예측을 도출해야 함. A가 방향 유지, B 방향 반전, C 인과 역전(및 비교 예측 아님), D 무관 요인으로 구조 충족. 검산: 개인 작품이 더 위반적이므로 상징 더 많음 → A 옳음. 다만 지문이 두 집단의 위반성 차이를 매우 명시적으로 서술해 사례 매핑 부담이 크지 않아 hard 중에서는 난이도가 낮은 편(중상 수준). 가상 평론가 Valdés 사용, Carrington 멕시코 활동은 사실과 부합, 저작권 문제 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 A가 맞고 해설에도 문제가 없다. 다만 이론을 사례에 적용하는 과정이 너무 직접적이다. 지문이 두 집단의 위반성 차이(관습적 가사 자세 vs 마녀·실험실)를 명시적으로 대비해 주고, 이론 문장도 'the more…the more' 형태로 방향을 그대로 노출한다. 그래서 실제 추론은 한 단계에 그친다. B(방향 반전)는 쉽게 걸러지고, C(인과 반전)는 예측 형식이 아니어서 쉽게 탈락하며, D는 이론과 무관함이 뻔하다. 체감 난이도는 어휘와 문장 길이에서만 나온다. 다중 자료 통합, 근거 충분성 판단 같은 hard 특성은 없으므로 전형적인 medium 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Some critics have charged that Anselm Kiefer's early works, in which he photographed himself giving the Nazi salute at sites across Europe, risked glamorizing the very regime they invoked. Art historian Lisa Saltzman offers a different reading: she argues that Kiefer staged these gestures not to celebrate the past but to force German viewers of the postwar generation to confront a history their society had largely chosen to leave unspoken. If Saltzman is correct, the works should have provoked discomfort chiefly among audiences who shared that silence, so her interpretation would be most strongly supported if it were found that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Some critics have charged that Anselm Kiefer's early works, in which he photographed himself giving the Nazi salute at sites across Europe, risked glamorizing the very regime they invoked. Art historian Lisa Saltzman offers a different reading: she argues that Kiefer staged these gestures not to celebrate the past but to force German viewers of the postwar generation to confront a history their society had largely chosen to leave unspoken. If Saltzman is correct, the works should have provoked discomfort chiefly among audiences who shared that silence, so her interpretation would be most strongly supported if it were found that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Kiefer later turned to materials such as lead, straw, and ash, which many critics regard as symbols of destruction and loss.
viewers in countries that had been occupied by Germany responded to the photographs with more anger than German viewers did.
German reviewers of the period frequently objected that the photographs exposed matters that their country had tacitly agreed not to discuss.
Kiefer studied under Joseph Beuys, an artist known for using performance to address social and political questions.
problem.explanation:
정답 C: Saltzman의 해석에 따르면 이 작품들은 과거에 대해 침묵해 온 전후 독일 관객을 겨냥했으므로, 불편함은 주로 그 침묵을 공유한 사람들에게서 나타나야 한다. 독일 평론가들이 '나라가 말하지 않기로 암묵적으로 합의한 것을 드러냈다'며 반발했다는 사실은 이 핵심 조건을 그대로 충족한다.
A: 후기 재료가 상실을 상징한다는 점은 주제상 관련 있어 보이지만, 초기 사진 작품을 관객이 어떻게 받아들였는지와는 상관이 없다.
B: 반응이 주로 독일 관객이 아닌 피점령국 관객에게서 나왔다는 것이므로 가설과 반대 방향을 가리킨다. 오히려 작품이 침묵을 깨뜨렸다기보다 나치를 미화한 것처럼 보였다는 비판 쪽에 가깝다.
D: 보이스에게 배웠다는 것은 전기적 배경일 뿐이다. 작품의 의도나 관객 반응에 대해서는 아무것도 보여 주지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, C: Saltzman says Kiefer's photographs were aimed at postwar German viewers who had stayed silent about the Nazi past. If she is right, the discomfort should show up mainly among the people who shared that silence. German reviewers complaining that the works exposed things their country had quietly agreed not to discuss fits that condition exactly.
A: Kiefer's later materials are related to the theme of loss, but they tell us nothing about how audiences reacted to the early photographs.
B: This says the strongest reaction came from viewers outside Germany, not German viewers. That points the opposite way from the hypothesis and fits better with the critics' claim that the works seemed to glorify the regime.
D: Studying under Beuys is just background about Kiefer's training. It says nothing about what the works were meant to do or how viewers received them.

hardJudge.note: Saltzman의 해석(침묵을 공유한 전후 독일 관객을 겨냥)에서 도출된 조건 — 불편함이 주로 그 침묵을 공유한 관객에게서 나타나야 함 — 을 C(독일 평론가들이 '암묵적으로 말하지 않기로 한 것을 드러냈다'고 반발)가 직접 충족. B는 피점령국 관객의 반응이 더 컸다는 것으로 방향이 반대이며 오히려 미화 비판 쪽을 지지하는 함정, A는 후기 재료라는 주제상 유관해 보이는 무관 사실, D는 전기적 배경. 사실 관계(Occupations 연작, Saltzman의 저서 논지, Beuys 사사, 납·짚·재 사용) 모두 문제 없음. 지문 내 조건 제시가 비교적 친절하지만, 가설에서 파생된 조건을 사례에 적용해 증거 충분성과 방향을 판별해야 하므로 medium 이상의 사고를 요구함.

advisory.note: 지문이 검증 조건('discomfort chiefly among audiences who shared that silence')을 명시해 버려서, 수험생이 이론을 사례에 직접 적용할 필요가 없다. 또 C는 'left unspoken'을 'tacitly agreed not to discuss'로 거의 그대로 바꿔 말한 것이라 어휘 대응만으로 고를 수 있다. 방향을 뒤집은 오답 B만 약간의 판단을 요구한다. 결과적으로 전형적인 medium 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Western viewers encountering Song dynasty landscape scrolls have often judged them to lack perspective, since the paintings contain no single vanishing point toward which lines converge. Yet the eleventh-century painter and theorist Guo Xi described three distinct kinds of distance—looking up at a peak from its base, peering from the front of a mountain into the valleys behind it, and gazing across level ground toward far-off hills—and he urged painters to combine all three within one composition. __Such a combination is impossible for an observer fixed in one spot, because each view requires the eye to stand somewhere different.__ A Song scroll, then, does not fail to achieve a single coherent viewpoint; it deliberately sets that viewpoint aside so that the viewer can wander through the landscape as if traveling within it, experiencing distance without being held at a distance.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Western viewers encountering Song dynasty landscape scrolls have often judged them to lack perspective, since the paintings contain no single vanishing point toward which lines converge. Yet the eleventh-century painter and theorist Guo Xi described three distinct kinds of distance—looking up at a peak from its base, peering from the front of a mountain into the valleys behind it, and gazing across level ground toward far-off hills—and he urged painters to combine all three within one composition. __Such a combination is impossible for an observer fixed in one spot, because each view requires the eye to stand somewhere different.__ A Song scroll, then, does not fail to achieve a single coherent viewpoint; it deliberately sets that viewpoint aside so that the viewer can wander through the landscape as if traveling within it, experiencing distance without being held at a distance.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why Guo Xi divided distance into three separate types, showing that each type corresponds to a different subject a painter might depict.
It offers evidence supporting the view of Western viewers mentioned earlier, conceding that Song paintings could not represent space convincingly.
It states the main claim of the text, asserting that Song landscape scrolls are designed to let viewers travel imaginatively through the scene.
It draws out an implication of Guo Xi's advice that links it to the absence of a vanishing point, setting up the claim that this absence was intentional.
problem.explanation:
정답 D: 밑줄 문장은 곽희가 말한 세 가지 거리를 한 화면에 결합하면 시점이 하나일 수 없다는 함의를 끌어낸다. 이를 통해 첫 문장의 '소실점이 없다'는 관찰과 이론을 연결하고, 마지막 문장의 결론, 즉 단일 시점은 의도적으로 내려놓은 것이라는 주장을 준비한다.
A(한 단계만 봄): 밑줄 문장은 세 가지 거리를 나눈 이유를 설명하지 않는다. 세 거리를 결합할 때 생기는 결과를 말할 뿐이고, 각 거리를 '서로 다른 소재'와 짝짓지도 않는다.
B(인접 문장과 혼동): '고정된 관찰자에게는 불가능하다'는 표현을 서구 관람자의 비판을 인정하는 말로 잘못 읽은 선택지다. 실제로 지문은 그 비판을 반박하는 쪽으로 나아간다.
C(전체 목적과 개별 기능을 뒤바꿈): 감상자가 풍경 속을 거닐게 한다는 주장은 마지막 문장의 결론이자 지문 전체의 요지이다. 밑줄 문장 자체의 기능은 아니다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, D: The underlined sentence draws out a consequence of Guo Xi's advice. If you combine all three kinds of distance in one painting, no single fixed viewpoint is possible. That ties his theory to the missing vanishing point mentioned in the first sentence. It also sets up the final sentence's conclusion that the single viewpoint was set aside on purpose.
A only looks at one step. The sentence doesn't explain why Guo Xi divided distance into three types. It describes what happens when you combine them, and it never matches each type to a different subject.
B mixes up the sentence with the earlier Western judgment. "Impossible for an observer fixed in one spot" doesn't agree with that criticism. The passage goes on to argue against it.
C swaps the passage's overall purpose with this one sentence's job. The idea that viewers travel through the scene is the claim made in the last sentence and the main point of the whole text. It isn't what the underlined sentence does.

hardJudge.note: 지문 구조: 서구 관람자의 관찰(소실점 없음) → 곽희의 삼원론 및 결합 권고 → 밑줄(결합의 함의: 고정 시점 불가) → 결론(단일 시점의 의도적 포기). 밑줄 문장의 기능을 확정하려면 첫 문장의 관찰과 마지막 문장의 결론을 모두 연결해야 하므로 D가 정답으로 정확하다. A는 '왜 세 가지로 나눴는가'라는 인접 단계의 역할로 혼동 유도, B는 '불가능하다'는 표현을 서구 비판의 인정으로 뒤집어 읽는 방향 역전 오답, C는 지문 전체 요지와 개별 문장 기능을 뒤바꾼 오답으로 설계 의도에 부합. 곽희의 삼원(고원·심원·평원) 서술은 사실과 일치하며 지문은 독창적 서술로 저작권 우려 없음. 해설은 각 오답의 설계 유형을 정확히 지적하며 정답과 모순 없음.

advisory.note: 밑줄 문장은 관찰(소실점 부재)과 곽희 이론, 그리고 결론(의도적 선택)을 잇는 중간 단계다. D가 정답이며, 이를 고르려면 세 단계를 연결해야 한다. B는 비판을 인정하는 방향으로 관계를 뒤집은 오답이고, C는 전체 요지와 해당 문장의 기능을 바꿔치기한 오답이다. 둘 다 오답 설계로 잘 작동한다. 곽희의 삼원법(고원·심원·평원) 서술도 사실에 부합한다.

problem.passage:
Composer Pauline Oliveros developed "Deep Listening," a practice in which performers attend not only to sounds they produce but to the entire sonic environment, including breath, room resonance, and distant traffic. Music educator Rachel Mendes argues that Oliveros's exercises belong in conservatory curricula chiefly because they sharpen students' pitch discrimination and ensemble timing—skills already central to conventional training. Musicologist Tomás Ibarra reads Oliveros differently. He notes that her early essays criticized the conservatory model itself, in which a single trained authority decides which sounds count as music and which count as noise. __For Ibarra, the exercises' value lies precisely in dissolving that hierarchy, since a student who learns to treat a cough in the audience as material equal to a scripted chord has stopped deferring to any single arbiter of musical worth.__ Teaching Deep Listening, he concludes, means questioning the institution that would host it.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Composer Pauline Oliveros developed "Deep Listening," a practice in which performers attend not only to sounds they produce but to the entire sonic environment, including breath, room resonance, and distant traffic. Music educator Rachel Mendes argues that Oliveros's exercises belong in conservatory curricula chiefly because they sharpen students' pitch discrimination and ensemble timing—skills already central to conventional training. Musicologist Tomás Ibarra reads Oliveros differently. He notes that her early essays criticized the conservatory model itself, in which a single trained authority decides which sounds count as music and which count as noise. __For Ibarra, the exercises' value lies precisely in dissolving that hierarchy, since a student who learns to treat a cough in the audience as material equal to a scripted chord has stopped deferring to any single arbiter of musical worth.__ Teaching Deep Listening, he concludes, means questioning the institution that would host it.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It specifies the grounds on which Ibarra would likely dispute Mendes's view that Oliveros's practice simply reinforces skills conventional training already prizes.
It specifies the grounds on which Mendes would likely dispute Ibarra's view that Oliveros's practice should challenge the authority of conservatories.
It specifies the grounds on which Oliveros herself developed exercises for heightening awareness of an entire sonic environment.
It specifies the grounds on which Ibarra would likely recommend replacing conservatory pitch training with improvisation in public spaces.
problem.explanation: 정답 A: 밑줄 문장은 Ibarra가 Deep Listening의 가치를 '판정 위계의 해체'에서 찾는다고 설명한다. 이는 Mendes가 이 연습을 기존 훈련(음정 판별, 합주 타이밍)을 강화하는 도구로 본 것과 정면으로 어긋나므로, Ibarra가 Mendes의 주장에 반박할 근거를 제시하는 셈이다. 다만 지문은 그 반박을 직접 언급하지 않는다. B: 두 입장을 뒤바꾼 오답이다. 밑줄 문장은 Mendes가 아니라 Ibarra의 관점을 담고 있다. C: Oliveros의 연습 소개라는 한쪽 내용만 근거로 삼았다. 밑줄 문장은 Oliveros가 왜 연습을 만들었는지가 아니라 Ibarra의 해석을 설명한다. D: 지문에 없는 반응을 지어냈다. 음정 훈련을 공공장소 즉흥연주로 대체하자는 제안은 어디에도 나오지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: A is correct. The underlined sentence explains that Ibarra values Deep Listening because it dissolves the hierarchy in which one authority judges musical worth. That conflicts with Mendes's claim that the exercises mainly sharpen skills conventional training already values, so the sentence gives Ibarra grounds to dispute Mendes, even though the passage never states that dispute directly. B is wrong because it swaps the two positions: the sentence presents Ibarra's view, not Mendes's. C is wrong because it relies only on the description of Oliveros's practice. The sentence gives Ibarra's interpretation, not Oliveros's reasons for creating the exercises. D is wrong because it makes up a reaction the passage never mentions: replacing pitch training with improvisation in public spaces.

hardJudge.note: Mendes(기존 기술 강화)와 Ibarra(위계 해체) 두 입장이 명확히 대비되며, 밑줄 문장은 Ibarra의 근거(기침=악보 화음과 동등한 재료 → 단일 판정자에 대한 복종 중단)를 제시하므로 A가 정확하다. 'simply reinforces'는 Mendes의 'chiefly because... skills already central to conventional training'과 대응한다. B는 입장 역전, C는 Oliveros의 동기로 범위를 오인, D는 지문에 없는 제안(공공장소 즉흥연주 대체)을 지어낸 것. 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하고 오답 근거도 적절하다. 'reads Oliveros differently'로 대립이 부분적으로 명시되어 있어 추론 부담이 아주 크지는 않으나, 초기 에세이의 비판→밑줄 문장의 근거→결론까지의 사슬을 연결해 Mendes 주장과의 관계를 재구성해야 하므로 medium 이상의 사고를 요구한다. Oliveros/Deep Listening은 실존 인물·개념이나 Mendes·Ibarra는 가상 학자로 보이며 저작권 문제는 없다.

advisory.note: 정답은 A로 타당하다. 밑줄 문장은 Ibarra의 근거(위계 해체)를 제시하며, 이는 Mendes가 이 연습을 기존 기술을 강화하는 도구로 본 것과 충돌한다. 지문에 반박이 명시되지 않아 추론이 필요하다. A의 'simply'는 Mendes의 'chiefly'보다 약간 강하지만 허용 범위다. B는 두 입장을 뒤바꾼 오답, D는 지문에 없는 내용을 지어낸 오답으로 체크리스트를 충족한다.
